Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United remain with just one win in nine league games and could find themselves in the relegation zone by the end of the weekend. The situation in Manchester has been untenable, but another defeat at the hands of one of their biggest rivals could force a decision being made among the club's hierarchy.

CARRICK'S RESPONSE SAYS IT ALL

The United boss couldn't even look at Lisandro Martinez as he walked off the pitch after getting sent off. The Argentine defender has let down his club - and several managers - time and time again since arriving at Old Trafford in 2022.

‌



View 5 Images Lisandro Martinez was shown a red card against Chelsea (Image: Getty Images)

However, his ridiculous antics against Chelsea could be the lowest he's fallen to at United. After getting embarrassed by Morgan Rogers and handed a yellow card for attempting to hack down the England star, he was shown a second yellow just seconds after fouling Fofana in the box.

The 28-year-old didn't look at the ball once when raising his hands against the Frenchman and was met by a similar snub by Carrick, who was writing in his notebook as Martinez made his way down the tunnel.

UNAVOIDABLE CHANGE NEARS

Michael Carrick wouldn't be the first United manager to face the ultimate punishment for his players' failures and he certainly won't be the last. The Englishman received a stay of execution after their 3-0 defeat to the Cherries, but remained under intense pressure after a disappointing start to the season.

‌



Despite a positive first-half against Chelsea, Carrick's side succumbed to the excellence of Morgan Rogers and the stupidity of Martinez that led Cole Palmer to net the Blues' second from the spot.

View 5 Images Michael Carrick has witnessed yet another defeat this season (Image: Ian Stephen/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

As is the case in football and sport as a whole, it's easier to part ways with one person than it is to overhaul an entire squad.

UNITED REACTION IS CLEAR

Carrick, 45, can be proud of his side's first-half showing at Stamford Bridge. In stark contrast to almost every other game this season, United showed desire, quality and steel in the first 45 minutes.

‌



They can even count themselves unlucky not to have scored after Amad's lack of potency and Cunha's disallowed goal. The positive reaction from the Red Devils has come after the United boss held clear-the-air talks with club captain Bruno Fernandes earlier this week.

View 5 Images Michael Carrick cleared the air with Bruno Fernandes (Image: Getty)

The Portuguese star had publicly criticised Carrick's tactics in the wake of their 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League, resulting in him being dropped for United's 3-0 home loss against Bournemouth last weekend.

However, he was swiftly restored to the team but was unable to stop them from falling to a fourth Premier League defeat of the season after an uninspiring second half .

‌



FOFANA DECISION MUST HAPPEN

Wesley Fofana may have thought it couldn't get worse after Chelsea's Carabao Cup penalty shootout defeat to Liverpool, but the defender was wrong. The Frenchman's handball in the midweek clash allowed Cody Gakpo to equalise for the Reds, before Fofana skied the crucial spot-kick to hand Andoni Iraola's side the victory.

An opportunity for redemption against United presented itself as he retained his spot in Xabi Alonso's side, but the 25-year-old endured a nightmare first-half. He was pickpocketed by Amad in his own half, with the Ivorian running through on goal and saw his shot saved by Mike Penders.

View 5 Images Wesley Fofana was caught out more than once by Amad at Stamford Bridge (Image: DAVID CLIFF/EPA/Shutterstock)

Just 10 minutes later, Fofana was easily overpowered by Amad and gifted him yet another clear sight on goal, but the 24-year-old skied the opportunity to spare the centre back's blushes.

‌



Brandishing a label of being a liability is a hurtful one, but it is accurate in Fofana's case. His mistakes could have resulted in his side going 2-0 down at home against a United team that have won just one league game this season.

Alonso may be short of defensive reinforcements with Maxence Lacroix and Reece James out injured, but removing Fofana from his starting XI is beginning to look like a necessity as every game passes.

Sports.title: What did Jamie Carragher say about Aston Villa? Furious response and what comes next
Sports.content:
In one of the most astonishing statements in recent Premier League history, Aston Villa have confirmed they intend to take legal action against pundit Jamie Carragher.

The bombshell announcement was issued late on Friday night after the Sky Sports pundit suggested manager Unai Emery should take the Manchester United job.

That sparked a furious backlash from Villa supporters, with Carragher then doubling down and telling fans to “shut the f*** up” and accept there is a chain in football - and United are above them.

But rather than the argument staying in the wild west of social media, the hierarchy at Villa Park decided to make the feud official. The statement - signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris - and said they would "not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football".

‌



And that resulted in a public apology from Carragher - where he accepted he had used 'clumsy language'.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

What did Carragher actually say?

"I think Unai Emery is unbelievable with what he does year after year," said Carragher. "That amount of change, players needing time to settle and he does it year after year.

‌



"But the reason I'm going to go back at Villa fans is I can't believe that a manager who is so successful in the Europa League, take a player, if you'd won the Europa League three of four times surely you'll then want to go for the Champions League.

"Aston Villa will never be Manchester United. I just think he didn't do well at PSG or Arsenal, and maybe that's because of egos in the dressing room and that sort of thing. But surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.

View 4 Images Jamie Carragher made the comments on the Overlap earlier this week (Image: The Overlap Fan Debate)

"Surely he would want that opportunity to manage a giant again. There is a chain in football, whether you like it or not.

‌



"So Real Madrid will take Manchester United's best player, they did it with (Cristiano) Ronaldo.

"And there will be teams below Aston Villa, and they'll take their players or manager. So shut the f*** up Aston Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Manchester United."

What was the response?

There had been no suggestion that Emery was interested in the job at Old Trafford, but his comments still drew a furious response.

Responding to that criticism Carragher said telling them to shut up had been "a joke" after "the stick Villa fans have given me over saying Emery may fancy joining Man Utd".

‌



View 4 Images Unai Emery led Aston Villa to Europa League success last season (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

He added that "for years" he had been praising Emery and Villa, while going further on The Overlap Daily, he added: "I just think Unai Emery is the best manager in the league and if you're Man United you're thinking 'what's the best we can get?'.

"I'm not saying he'll go - I'm just saying if it was me I'd ask the question. I think your own ego if someone said 'that's your level' would say 'no I'm not'. That was my point. It's grown arms and legs."

He has since expressed his regret at using the foul language, but insisted the comments were made in jest.

‌



What have Villa said?

Villa duly responded on Friday evening with a statement on social media signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris.

“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said.

“Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, Chairman.”

Have your say!

‌



Carragher's apology

On Saturday, just as the Premier League weekend was getting underway, Carragher took to social media to offer an apology.

He said: "I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners & their fans. My language this week was clumsy & wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue in cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV!"

What happens next?

For now...it's a waiting game. Villa have made their intentions clear, but it would still be pretty stunning if they follow through on their threats and what legal action they can take against a pundit expressing his opinion.

View 4 Images Executive Chairman of Aston Villa Nassef Sawiris (Image: Getty)

‌



But Sawiris is wildly ambitious, having guided the Villans from the Championship all the way to winning the Europa League and being regulars in the Champions League. Being told to accept their place in the food chain won't have sat well and doesn't match with how those inside the Villa Park corridors of power see their standing in 2026.

Ironically, Sky are covering Villa's home match against Fulham on Saturday night, where those in the stands will make their feelings very clear in front of the watching world.

At boardroom level, whether Carragher's public apology is the end of the matter remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Emi Martinez opens up on horrific injury that made him cry when he saw the x-ray
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez opens up on horrific injury that made him cry when he saw the x-ray

Emiliano Martinez suffered physically and emotionally in order to play at the 2026 World Cup, where he almost helped Argentina retain their crown - losing in the final to Spain

View 2 Images (Image: Getty Images)

Emiliano Martinez has revealed he cried every night after fearing his serious finger injury would prevent him from playing at the World Cup. The Chelsea goalkeeper reached his second consecutive final at the competition with Argentina this past summer, but lost 1-0 to Spain in extra time.

‌



‌



However, Martinez almost didn't travel with Lionel Scaloni's side after breaking his finger in Aston Villa's Europa League final triumph against Freiburg. The 34-year-old was convinced he'd miss the World Cup given the gravity of the injury, but was supported by national team coach Lionel Scaloni.

‌



A specially modified Adidas glove was created for the goalkeeper to compete in the competition. Martinez decided against surgery and remains in need of an operation months after the World Cup and admitted he's in daily pain.

‌



In an interview with Los Edul, the Albiceleste hero said his hand will remain disfigured after demonstrating a clenched fist unable to close his broken finger. Martinez said: "It will stay like this for the rest of my life. I broke my finger in the Europa League final.

"When the doctor showed me the X-ray, I started crying because I thought I would miss the World Cup. Scaloni messaged me and said: ‘Whether you make it or not, I’ll back you… come anyway’. We decided not to have surgery. Adidas made me a special glove, and I played with my finger completely wrapped.

"I could only feel four fingers. I couldn’t even train with normal footballs. I trained with volleyballs until the Switzerland game. How much did it affect me at the World Cup? Ten out of ten. I was practically a zombie."

He quickly usurped Robert Sanchez as the Blues' number one, with the Spaniard sent on loan to Como for the rest of the season. He made six appearances for the west London side before suffering a broken jaw against Everton a fortnight ago.

Sports.content:
Man City 'reject explanation' over Liverpool, Man Utd and Arsenal dinner meeting

Manchester City are preparing for their appeal hearing after the independent commission found them guilty of over 100 financial breaches

View 3 Images Man City's hierarchy believe the club have done nothing wrong (Image: Photo by MB Media/Getty Images)

Manchester City's hierarchy reportedly 'reject an explanation' over a 2017 dinner meeting between Liverpool, Manchester United and Arsenal, furthering suspicions from fans that a 'Red Cartel' have been working together to bring them down. The former Premier League champions are facing severe sanctions after being found guilty of 114 financial charges but are currently appealing the verdict.

‌



‌



United, Arsenal and Liverpool were three of the only four clubs that instructed lawyers to inform City that they had reserved their right to seek compensation should they be found guilty back in 2024. They are also said to be among the Premier League clubs pushing for City to face a serious punishment if their appeal fails.

‌



And there is now anger growing among City fans about the perceived role the three clubs - who all play in red, giving the alleged group its name - in their downfall.

‌



For those City supporters who believe their club has been the victim of a 'Red Cartel' of rivals colluding to bring their team down, a photograph taken by a diner at a New York restaurant co-owned by famed actor Robert De Niro is Exhibit A in their argument.

Premier League star to switch allegiance from England and play for new country READ MORE :

Michael Carrick gives Gary Neville blunt response over damning claim about Man Utd stars READ MORE :

It was taken in October 2017, which predates the Premier League bringing 115 charges against City for breaking the league's financial rules in February 2023, but falls within the 2009-18 time frame covered by the investigation that led to them being found guilty on 114 counts last month.

Liverpool owner John W. Henry, Ed Woodward, Joel and Avram Glazer and Ivan Gadizis, Arsenal chief executive at the time, were pictured at a diner seven days before a Premier League vote on future broadcast revenue. Tottenham Hotspur, City and Chelsea were left out of the meeting, but it could be explained by the fact that the three clubs were American-owned, while City (Abu Dhabi), Chelsea (Russian), Spurs (British) were not.

‌



According to ESPN, that explanation has never been accepted by City, while CEO Ferran Soriano referenced a 'conspiracy theory' at the top rung of the English football pyramid as he rejected the commission's verdict. The comments were said to be directed as much towards Liverpool, Manchester United and Arsenal hierarchy as the Premier League.

ESPN reported that while the club have declined to comment on the "cartel", sources have stated that those at the highest level of the club have no doubts about the intent from their rivals to create difficulty for the club.

‌



View 3 Images City have been far more successful than United, Liverpool and Arsenal in recent years (Image: AP Photo/Dave Thompson)

A source with links to City was quoted as saying: "From day one, United, Arsenal and Liverpool have been terrified of losing their ability to dominate everything from the Premier League to the transfer market.

‌



"Chelsea was already a problem for them under Roman Abramovich, but Sheikh Mansour came along [in 2008] and changed everything again, and the red clubs have been in a battle against City ever since."

The narrative surrounding the 'Red Cartel' will not be helped by the assertions from the Liverpool owner, Henry, and former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who publicly lambasted City's financial dealings in 2011, six years prior to the meeting.

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Wenger urged UEFA to investigate City and accused them of bending the rules .He said: "We must have done a bad deal. It raises the real question about the credibility of the financial fair play. That is what this is all about. They give us the message that they can get around it by doing what they want.

‌



“It means financial fair play will not come in. It is as simple as that. I can understand how they do it but it raises the real question. The difficulty and the credibility of the financial fair play is at stake.

"Plus, if the financial fair play is to have a chance, the sponsorship has to be at the market price. It cannot be doubled, tripled or quadrupled because that means it is better that we don't do it and we leave everybody free. That can be defended as well, but if they bring the rules in they have to be respected."

‌



Then active on social media, the Liverpool chief said: "A club's best player has to be worth at least 10% of your naming rights. Mr. Wenger says boldly what everyone thinks."

View 3 Images Liverpool fans protest against Manchester City after their guilty verdict.

‌



The trio of top-flight clubs found themselves in a battle on the pitch with City during the nine-year period, 2009 to 2018, jostling to be at the summit of the Premier League. City came out on top during that stage, and their supremacy stretched with Pep Guardiola's side winning four titles in a row.

The Telegraph reported earlier this month that United, Liverpool, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur were handed the guilty verdict early and previously gave City legal notice of the right to seek compensation.

‌



City have appealed the verdict from the Premier League as they feel they have 'irrefutable evidence' that backs their argument that they should have been found not guilty of any wrongdoing.

The commission dealing with appeals has to return a decision, under Premier League rules, within 12 weeks – giving a deadline of January 21. The ramifications for City's actions remain unclear, with the potential for record-breaking points deductions, relegations and even falling out of the English Football League (EFL).

‌



Former midfielder Gareth Barry expressed his sadness for the City supporters for being subjected to the abuse from terraces across the Premier League following the verdict.

Speaking on All Out Football 's In The Mixer , Barry said: "If the club have broken rules, then they have to get punished. It's natural, isn't it? The football world can't work properly if rules are in place and they're getting broken.

‌



"Listen, this is the financial side of it (football). Other teams we've seen in other countries that broke rules… You're going to get punished. So the club possibly are going to get punished at some point.

"But I think as ex-players and especially as fans, you want it done quicker rather than later. It's just an awkward situation for everyone now, isn't it?

Article continues below

"It's more of a sad feeling, probably for the fans. I mean the moments [I had at City], they've already happened. These are the sort of things that are not going to be ever taken away. They happened 12, 13 years ago. These things happened when I joined the club, 2009, even earlier than that.

"So I feel sorry for the fans, really. They're going to the games, getting songs sung about them and people calling them cheats. Players, fans, staff - there are decisions that you're not in control of. You don't know what's going on."

Sports.title: Premier League star to switch allegiance from England and play for new country
Sports.content:
Premier League star to switch allegiance from England and play for new country

Coventry striker Ellis Simms was called up to England squads in his youth, but he's been given the green light to represent another country during the November international break

View 2 Images Ellis Simms never played for England despite youth call-ups (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Premier League star Ellis Simms has received confirmation of his Polish citizenship and could make his debut for the country next month. Simms, 25, was born in Oldham but is eligible to represent Poland through his grandmother.

‌



‌



The Coventry striker was called up to England camps at both under-18 and under-20 level but never made an official appearance. Earlier this year, Simms applied to become a Polish citizen, and he's now been successful.

‌



According to Meczyki, the former Everton prospect is submitting documents in order to obtain a passport. That part of the process is expected to be a formality.

‌



Simms will therefore be available for Poland's Nations League fixtures against Romania and Sweden in November. Manager Jan Urban is due to announce his call-ups next Friday and has already talked up Simms' chances.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"There is a point. Players with Polish roots have the right to be treated the same as any other Pole with a passport," Urban told TVP Sport in September.

"He's not Erling Haaland, he's not some unknown type of player. He played regularly in the Championship, but things weren't going so well for him at Everton.

‌



"First, the paperwork: the passport and all the formalities. Only then will he be considered. If we think he can help the national team, he'll be called up. If not, we'll wait for him to improve. it's no secret we're interested in him."

Poland are looking for new strikers as captain Robert Lewandowski enters the twilight of his career. Lewandowski celebrated his 38th birthday in August, but Urban continues to rely on the Chicago Fire man, who bagged a hat-trick in his last outing.

‌



Simms has only started one of Coventry's eight Premier League games this season but scored off the bench in their 4-1 win against Newcastle earlier this month. Last season, the 25-year-old helped Frank Lampard's side earn promotion from the Championship by netting 13 goals.

Will Coventry survive relegation? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Ellis Simms has one Premier League goal to his name this season (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

With Coventry's focus on survival, Simms hopes his previous top-flight experience with Everton will come in handy. "I knew a little bit about the league already, the demands and what's required to be competitive at that level, so it was a great challenge for me to prove myself at this level again," he explained this week.

‌



"We know how ruthless the league is - it's a lot higher level than last year. I've heard how big of a fanbase and club Coventry us - we've been waiting to get back into the Premier League.

"It's been 20 odd years so we're happy that us as players have managed to get the club back, and we just want to try and stay there. We know it's difficult but we believe in ourselves - we've got a good coaching group, good fans and if we all stick together, I'm sure we can stay in the league."

Sports.title: Martinez sent off as Man Utd implode against Chelsea
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martinez was sent off as Manchester United sunk to a 2-0 loss to Chelsea to plunge Michael Carrick further into trouble.

The defeat extends United's winless run to nine games in all competitions, making it their longest since 1988, and puts them at risk of falling into the relegation zone this weekend.

Martinez, making only his second start since criticising the club's hierarchy, was shown a second yellow for raising an arm to the face of Wesley Fofana inside the United box following a VAR check, only three minutes after being booked for fouling Morgan Rogers.

Cole Palmer dispatched the resulting penalty, doubling Chelsea's lead after Rogers had charged through Manchester United's static defence and lifted a delicate finish over Senne Lammens for the opener at the start of the second half.

Image: Lisandro Martinez was sent off by referee Peter Bankes

United's second-half implosion piles pressure on head coach Carrick, who reinstated Bruno Fernandes after dropping the captain for his criticism of his tactics after the defeat to Como.

Fernandes' return to the side, after he was an unused substitute in the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth, appeared to help United in the first half but they were unable to convert a series of chances.

Fernandes missed the best of them, firing harmlessly over when unmarked from Bryan Mbeumo's centre. Amad Diallo was also culpable as he was twice denied by Mike Penders as Chelsea struggled to contain United's counter-attacks.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mike Dean gives his view on the penalty awarded to Chelsea at Stamford Bridge

But the visitors were made to pay for their wastefulness only five minutes after the interval, as Rogers accelerated into the box unchallenged to strike the first blow in a defeat which leaves United a point above the relegation zone, with Carrick's future in doubt.

The scoreline could have been worse for United, with the excellent Estevao having a third goal ruled out by VAR for offside before drawing a full-stretch save from Lammens. But two goals were sufficient for the Blues to move above Liverpool into fourth.

Sports.title: South Africa win decider over Aussies to take series and go top of Test rankings
Sports.content:
South Africa thumped Australia by 176 runs at Newlands as the hosts' bowling attack produced fireworks to clinch a 2-1 victory in the three-match series between the countries and propel the Proteas to the top of the ICC Men's Test Team Rankings.

This wasn't a chase that drifted away; it was snatched from Australia early on. Kagiso Rabada ripped through it in the first over and spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best 6-16 to destroy any hopes of a comeback.

Set a target of 288 for victory, the tourists were bowled out for 111 as South Africa leapfrogged them to go top of the Test world rankings for the first time since January 2016.

Matt Renshaw was caught by Ryan Rickelton down the leg side for a golden duck and Marnus Labuschagne was lbw for four. Travis Head followed for 14, caught by Marco Jansen at gully, as Rabada (3-39) took his 350th Test wicket.

That landmark made Rabada the quickest bowler to 350 Test wickets by balls bowled. He got there in 13,808 deliveries, ahead of compatriot Dale Steyn (14,719) and Pakistan's ‌Waqar Younis (14,905).

Image: South Africa's Kagiso Rabada celebrates the wicket of Australia's Travis Head (AP Photo/Halden Krog)

Australia's fourth wicket was a mess as Cameron Green called first-innings centurion Josh Inglis through for a quick single after pushing Harmer into the covers, but Inglis was left short and run out for four.

After that Harmer came into his own, exploiting the conditions expertly to also claim a first 10-wicket haul in Tests with figures of 10-120 across the match.

"The trend of this game was once you got yourself in there were runs to be had," Australia captain Pat Cummins said. "But within the first hour the game was away from us and we did not give ourselves a chance.

"We are a really good side but playing tough opponents away from home is always difficult. We came here thinking we were good enough to win but we ‌couldn't do it."

By this point, the second innings was in complete disarray for Australia after Harmer had Alex Carey caught at backward point with Marco Jansen taking another good catch.

Two balls later, Cooper Connolly was caught behind for a two-ball duck, leaving the visitors 42-6.

Harmer struck again before lunch, with Mitchell Starc – who faced 25 balls without opening his account – caught at short leg as the ball looped up off his pads.

Australia were 60-7 at lunch, with Green 25 not out.

Green was bowled by Harmer for 27 soon after the restart.

Image: South Africa's Simon Harmer celebrates the second of the six wickets he took on day five at Newlands (AP Photo/Halden Krog)

Cummins (11 from 90 balls) and innings top-scorer Nathan Lyon (33 not out) delayed the inevitable with a ninth-wicket stand that lasted 17.2 overs.

This time, Harmer went round the wicket, struck the Aussie skipper on the pad and three reds confirmed the lbw decision after a review – he went for 11 at 107-9 before Josh Hazlewood's wicket fell to wrap up the victory.

"It was just understanding what I needed to do, getting the ball in the right areas as often as I could, and playing with my pace and trajectories, the little nuances I have learnt along the way. It all worked out alright," Harmer said.

"Today was a lot of fun, fielders around the bat and trying to get the win. That is the stuff of dreams for a spinner."

South Africa had done the hard work on day four, when Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder made centuries in a 154-run sixth-wicket stand to turn a first-innings deficit of 100 into a target of 288.

Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs, South Africa won in Gqeberha by an innings and 31 runs, and the hosts took the decider in Cape Town with an irrepressible attacking display to thwart the tourists.

The victory also keeps alive South Africa's hopes of defending their World Test Championship title next year having beaten Australia at Lord's ‌in the previous decider in 2025.

Sports.title: Birmingham back to winning ways as Priske scores twice
Sports.content:
August Priske scored twice as Birmingham bounced back from defeat at Cardiff to beat Lincoln 3-1 in the Sky Bet Championship at the ProAmpac Stadium.

The big Dane scored either side of the break, with Alex Cochrane securing the win after Imps substitute Tom Bayliss had reduced the deficit.

Ukrainian midfielder Ivan Varfolomeev's recall for the injured Conor McGrandles was Lincoln's only change, while for the Blues Ethan Laird came in for Bright Osayi-Samuel, with Priske and Patrick Roberts replacing Luis Vasquez and Carlos Vicente respectively.

Cochrane fired the game's first effort wide inside four minutes, before Lincoln were denied by the goal frame four minutes later.

Reeco Hackett flicked a ball through for Ben House to run on to, he backheeled a pass to Mikkel Ladefoged, who hit a low shot past James Beadle, but which bounced against the goalkeeper's right-hand post and away to safety.

In what was a hectic opening quarter of an hour, Jay Stansfield almost produced a goal of the month contender as he flicked the ball over his head when tightly marked in the City box, span round and fired just wide.

But seconds later, Birmingham were ahead, with a goal owing to some fortune on their part. A Blues pass was inadvertently directed towards his own goal by Yunus Konak, straight to Priske on the edge of the box and he swivelled and fired a low shot into the bottom corner.

Laird could have seen red after half an hour after attempting to bring down a clearance on the visitors' right wing, but booting House in the face as the Lincoln forward attempted to seize possession and nip in towards goal. Referee Lewis Smith produced only a yellow card.

Dom Jefferies' low shot was comfortably saved by Beadle deep into first-half stoppage time, before the keeper then somehow kept our Deji Elewere's close-range prod, palming his shot up onto the bar and out for a corner.

Former Imps keeper Ryan Allsopp replaced Beadle at the break, with Priske testing George Wickens after 49 minutes from the edge of the box.

On the hour mark, Blues doubled their lead. A long throw into the box was flicked on and there was Priske to slide in and poke the ball past Wickens.

There minutes later, though, Lincoln reduced the deficit through Bayliss. Ladefoged laid the ball off to the substitute and he arrowed a ball into the corner of the net.

A terrific 50-yard run from Millar nearly ended with a goal for Stansfield, but his shot was deflected wide, but less than a minute later, Cochrane was given too much time and space in the centre of the pitch to run forward and plant a left-footed shot past Wickens after 73 minutes to make it 3-1.

Elewere blocked a goal bound Stansfield shot and Demarai Gray blasted wide when through on goal as Blues looked for a fourth.

Sports.title: Stoke see off dreadful Preston
Sports.content:
Stoke continued their impressive run in the Championship with a 2-0 home victory over basement side Preston.

Goals from Ben Wilmot and Jack McGlynn did the damage as Mark Robins' in-form team claimed a seventh win in their last 10 league games.

Centre-back Wilmot put the hosts ahead with a powerful 29th-minute header from McGlynn's pinpoint cross.

Then United States midfielder McGlynn got in on the scoring act himself with a sweet left-foot strike that doubled the Potters' advantage eight minutes after the restart.

Defeat for the struggling Lilywhites, who remain rooted to the foot of the table, was their fourth in five league games since appointing Graham Alexander as Paul Heckingbottom's successor.

Slovakian striker Robert Bozenik, the one change to the home side's team, had a penalty appeal turned down after just five minutes after going down following a tussle with Odel Offiah.

The hosts went close in the 14th minute when Ben Johnson dragged a left-foot shot agonisingly wide of the right post.

At the other end, former Potter Jordan Thompson went close with a powerful left-foot free-kick from the edge of the box that flew into the side-netting.

Wilmot then had to receive treatment for a bad cut above his right eye, but it mattered not as the towering centre-back scored soon after with a fine header from McGlynn's perfect delivery.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Ben Wilmot's terrific header put Stoke 1-0 up against Preston.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jack McGlynn's fine finish doubles The Potters' advantage against Preston, to make it 2-0.

McGlynn whipped the ball in after it fell invitingly to him from a corner and Wilmot rose well to power into the top-right corner for his second goal of the season.

McGlynn came close to doubling the Potters' lead five minutes before the break, but his powerful deflected left-foot strike was brilliantly saved by Preston shot-stopper Daniel Iversen.

Stoke flew out of the blocks after the break and Bozenik came close to poking home at the near post from Luca Bombino's pass, before Luke Graham headed inches wide after former Stoke loanee Iversen missed a punched clearance.

But a second goal was just around the corner and Ethan Galbraith teed up McGlynn to rifle home from close range to leave the visitors with plenty to do in search of a first win in nearly two months.

Bozenik should have put the contest out of sight but was thwarted in a one-on-one situation with Iversen, while Galbraith saw his goalbound shot deflected for a corner and Justin Devenny had a shot cleared off the line as the hosts went for the jugular.

Substitute Million Manhoef wasted a glorious chance to make it 3-0, when he somehow shot wide from point-blank range with three minutes left.

Sports.title: Norwich hit back to beat Watford in stunning comeback
Sports.content:
Norwich launched a storming second half comeback to beat Watford 3-2 and make it back-to-back wins in the Sky Bet Championship.

Dutch striker Myron Boadu opened his account for the visitors with two goals as Watford took a 2-0 lead into the interval against a misfiring home side.

However, the Canaries looked a different side after the interval and scored three times in 17 minutes to turn the game on its head, with Ben Chrisene, Anthony Musaba and Paris Maghoma getting the goals that made it another unhappy afternoon for under-pressure Hornets manager Alessio Dionisi.

Norwich made a bright start, with Federico Ravaglia making a good reflex stop to keep out Jacob Wright's deflected flick inside the first three minutes and Sam Field then curling a shot narrowly wide.

Image: Anthony Musaba celebrates after scoring for Nrowich against Watford

The visitors took the lead from their first genuine attack of the game in the 10th minute.

A quick break left the Canaries stretched at the back and Iker Bravo played a perfectly weighted ball into the path of strike partner Boadu, who skilfully guided the ball past onrushing goalkeeper Dan Grimshaw into the far corner.

The home side continued to have the bulk of possession, with Maghoma firing just wide after skipping past a couple of defenders - but the Hornets soaked up the pressure and doubled their advantage in the 27th minute.

This time Boadu picked up a speculative pass from deep from Mattie Pollock and turned Jose Cordoba before producing another neat side-footed finish past an exposed Grimshaw.

Norwich wasted little time in getting themselves back in it after the break, with Chrisene pulling one back in the 54th minute.

Ravaglia made a superb stop to keep out Cordoba's header from a Wright corner but the ball fell kindly for the City left-back to volley home from 10 yards.

The rejuvenated Canaries were now firmly on the front foot and levelled in the 62nd minute with a breakaway goal of their own.

Musaba used his pace to get on the end of a quick ball forward and then raced past Kevin Keben before cutting inside and blasting the ball home.

Norwich then made it three goals in a little more than a quarter of an hour to turn the game completely on its head.

With 71 minutes on the clock Field picked out Mathias Kvistgaarden in space on the right and the Danish striker picked out an unmarked Maghoma to drill the ball into the net in emphatic fashion for his second goal in successive games.

Watford rarely looked like mounting of a comeback of their own after the triple setback as the hosts comfortably saw out the game.

Sports.title: Manchester United crisis deepens with Chelsea defeat and Martínez red card
Sports.content:
Get ready for another week of agonising over the sorry state of Manchester United. The legends of old will rage, clips of a fuming Gary Neville will fly around social media, the airwaves will reverberate with complaints from angry supporters and by the time United play again there is every chance a new manager will be in the dugout.

There were echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge as the walls closed in on Michael Carrick at Stamford Bridge. United missed a series of golden chances when the scores were level, just as they did when Ten Hag lost to West Ham a day before his sacking two years ago, and Chelsea made the most of the reprieve after initially delivering a performance so bad it had you worrying for the nascent Xabi Alonso project.

Chelsea could not have been worse during the first half. It helped that their opponents were in a giving mood. United had opportunities to make their decision to give Carrick a stay of execution look like a wise move rather than the consequence of executive level confusion, but their finishing was awful and their defending even worse. They watched as Morgan Rogers breezed through to make it 1-0 early in the second half and their seventh defeat in 13 games was sealed when Lisandro Martínez earned a red card for giving away the penalty that allowed Cole Palmer to push Chelsea into fourth place.

It symbolised United’s decline under the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. Martínez has had a lot to say recently, but the Argentinian should have been sold long ago. That he is yet to go sums up United’s shoddy recruitment. They are carrying so much deadwood and it is hard to see their problems being fixed by a change of manager. Carrick is merely one of many issues. He will probably have gone by the time United face Roma on Tuesday and whoever takes over will inherit a team sleepwalking into a relegation battle.

This is not a happy ship. The ending was similar to last week’s defeat to Bournemouth. Carrick was applauded when he walked over at full-time. They sang his name and booed when the United players made a sheepish trudge to the away end at full time.

View image in fullscreen Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes cuts a dejected figure at the final whistle. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The spotlight was also on Alonso, defeats to Tottenham in the league and Liverpool in the Carabao Cup sparking criticism over team selections, and he lifted his side by handing Estêvão Willian his first start in the league this season.

Overlooked at Anfield, Estêvão was dangerous on the right flank after Alonso adjusted without the injured João Pedro up front. Pedro Neto rather than Danny Welbeck led the line in a 4-2-3-1 system but it was United who threatened first. Diogo Dalot combined with Mateus Cunha on the left and Andrey Santos, who left Chelsea for United last summer, swept a shot just wide from 20 yards.

Both sides brought vulnerabilities to the table. Chelsea had a long list of absentees – illness ruled Jordan Henderson out in midfield – and their defence wobbled without Maxence Lacroix. United, though not exactly secure whenever Chelsea punched through on the counterattack, felt optimistic at first.

The visitors had an escape when Senne Lammens spilled a Neto shot and an offside Estêvão tapped home but Carrick was the happier manager during the first half. Fernandes, back after clear the air talks with Carrick, shimmered in a floating role from the left. Bryan Mbeumo and Cunha were lively, although the worry for United was making their dominance count.

View image in fullscreen Omar Berrada, Manchester United’s CEO, and Jason Wilcox, their director of football, in the stands at Stamford Bridge. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Fernandes was wasteful at the end of a flowing counterattack, firing over from Mbeumo’s pass. Amad Diallo, dangerous against Marco Palestra, cut inside to fire two efforts on target and Chelsea, enjoying neither possession nor control against Santos and Carlos Baleba, were forced into emergency mode.

Levi Colwill intervened when Cunha broke through and Wesley Fofana took flak from the home fans after a couple of trademark brain farts. Mbeumo and Diallo missed after mistakes by the Frenchman, though it is worth stressing that a dismal half from Chelsea was a team effort. They were lucky when Cunha had what would have been the opening goal disallowed by the video assistant referee (VAR) for offside.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The away end ran through the anti-board chants – urging the Glazers to sell up and questioning Jason Wilcox’s credentials as technical director – and United feared being punished for their profligacy. There were a couple of flashes from Chelsea; Moisés Caicedo diverted a Fofana header against the woodwork and Neto shot wide after a stumble from Harry Maguire.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer fires home Chelsea’s second from the penalty spot. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Chelsea were more assertive at the start of the second half and it was easy to predict United’s unravelling. They were punished when Mbeumo turned into trouble in midfield. Caicedo blocked his path, Roméo Lavia nicked the ball past Baleba and Rogers took over. Facing no resistance, the £117m man’s saunter through the middle placed United’s failure to strengthen in defence into sharp focus.

It was a bit like a goal you see at the end of a casual five-a-side between a group of dads playing for the first time since 2019. Maguire barely lifted a leg, Martínez gawped and Rogers dinked over Lammens for 1-0.

The challenge for United was to dig deep, to stand tall. Good luck with that. Lavia was running the midfield for Chelsea now.

There was a sense of the players in red giving up when Martínez elbowed Fofana at a corner. The Argentinian was already on a booking and he was off when Peter Bankes reviewed the incident, leaving Palmer to put United’s 10 men to bed by making it 2-0 from the spot.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher apologises to Aston Villa for ‘clumsy and wrong’ comments
Sports.content:
Jamie Carragher has apologised to Aston Villa for using “clumsy and wrong” language when discussing the club, after club had threatened legal action. “I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong,” Carragher wrote on X on Saturday.

“I can assure Villa fans it was tongue-in-cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV [Up the Villa]!”

On Friday, Villa had announced plans to take legal action against Carragher for his “unacceptable insults”, in a statement on X signed by their chair, Nassef Sawiris. The pundit had said Villa fans should “shut the fuck up” after facing criticism for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Aston Villa will initiate legal action against Jamie Carragher for his unacceptable insults about the club and its fans,” the statement said. “Aston Villa will not allow anyone to stop our ascension in English and European football. Nassef Sawiris, chairman.”

The former Liverpool defender made his remarks on the Stick to Football podcast while discussing the prospect of Emery replacing Michael Carrick at Old Trafford. Carragher said: “I’m not trying to annoy Villa fans, but there is a chain in football, whether you like it or not. So Real Madrid will take Man United’s best player, they’ll take [Cristiano] Ronaldo. There’s very few above United, the same with Liverpool.

“But there will be teams below Aston Villa and they [Villa] will take their manager or they will take their players, so shut the fuck up, Villa fans. Aston Villa will never be Man United.”

Aston Villa have not responded publicly to Carragher’s apology, at time of writing. They face Fulham at home in the Premier League on Saturday night.

Sports.title: Suspicious bets returning £149,000 for predicting Ballon d’Or under investigation
Sports.content:
A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police.

It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award. Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outlet Upside’s investigation.

According to Raphaël Pautard, the co-founder of Upside, his team identified 12 Polymarket accounts created between 1 October and 20 October. The accounts displayed strikingly similar patterns of activity, leading investigators to suspect they could be connected to the same individual or group. Seven of the 12 accounts had not participated in any other betting markets, while six placed their first bets 15 minutes after being created.

Pautard revealed that his team managed to trace one transaction back to a French platform. After sharing the relevant blockchain transactions and wallet addresses with the company’s team, the platform reportedly confirmed it had identified the individual behind one of the accounts involved in funding the suspicious bets. The identity of that individual has not been publicly disclosed, but the development could prove significant in establishing connections between the accounts and tracing the money behind the wagers.

Quick Guide How do I 

Upside passed its findings to France Football, which Groupe Amaury owns and which has organised the awards since 1956. It is understood to have received confirmation on Friday afternoon that an investigation has been opened, with the French police also to be informed. France Football has been contacted for comment.

Rather than spreading their money across different outcomes, the accounts concentrated their wagers on a specific scenario: Kane winning, followed by Mbappé in second, Yamal in third, Rodri in fourth and Messi in fifth. Every position subsequently matched the official results, generating nearly $200,000 in profits.

According to the investigation by Upside, one account purchased a contract predicting Kane would win at 37 cents before selling it when the price reached 67 cents. The funds were subsequently redirected towards bets on specific finishing positions, including Yamal finishing third. This sequence of transactions has attracted attention because it suggests the account holder adjusted their strategy as the relevant markets developed.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Before the ceremony, France Football had indicated that only a handful of people knew the winner in advance. The possibility that confidential information could have reached betting accounts before the official announcement is therefore a serious concern, particularly given the precision of the predictions and the amount of money involved. “How do we keep the winner’s identity hidden? I think a well-kept secret is one that is shared with as few people as possible,” said the former France Football editor Pascal Ferré last week.

Sports.title: No big deal: how Mac Allister shook off contract doubts to fire Liverpool’s revival
Sports.content:
Alexis Mac Allister found himself in a strong position to apply pressure on Liverpool over a new contract before Atlético Madrid’s visit to Anfield last month, although only in the physical sense of being up on stage to preview the game in front of a mass audience. In reality, the 27-year-old’s negotiating stance was relatively weak. And in fairness to the Argentina international, he has been true to his word in flipping the narrative in his favour ever since.

As the past two Premier League champions prepare to meet at Anfield on Sunday, when Liverpool can narrow the gap on Arsenal to three points with a fourth successive home win in all competitions, Mac Allister’s form encapsulates the impressive improvement of Andoni Iraola’s team. He has become the indispensable part of Liverpool’s central midfield and to an extent that, merely seven weeks on from that headline-grabbing Champions League press conference, it is not only Mac Allister who thinks he deserves a contract extension.

“The fans don’t need to worry as I will give my 100% and maybe they [Liverpool] change their minds,” said the midfielder after expressing sadness over the absence of a new contract offer and a little envy, cloaked in happiness, over the ones awarded to Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch. The following night he struck an immaculate winner against Diego Simeone’s side. He has continued to walk the walk for a Liverpool team that has rediscovered its intensity and started to repair relations with the Anfield crowd as a result. Winning does that.

Iraola said on Friday: “You mention the press conference he had and I was there also, after him. The most important thing from that is that he wants to stay here. That is very important. He wants to work hard, he wants to be at his best so he can continue here helping us. A player of that level who has achieved what he has achieved, who can be as clear as that with his intentions, is very good for us because I appreciate him a lot. He’s a top player.”

A major influence when Liverpool won their 20th league championship under Arne Slot, Mac Allister faded badly in the Dutchman’s second and final season in charge. He was not alone on that score but, despite reminding a global audience of his qualities as Argentina reached a second World Cup final in succession, rumours of an Anfield exit this summer were met with a general shrug of shoulders rather than howls of protest. Liverpool’s stance over a contract that had entered its final two years confirmed they also didn’t consider an extension a priority. The club have also been paying Mac Allister a lucrative salary from the moment he walked through the door in June 2023, having signed him for £35m – below market value – due to a release clause in his Brighton contract.

View image in fullscreen Alexis Mac Allister hits the winner against Atlético Madrid in September. Photograph: Jan Kruger/Uefa/Getty Images

It was largely overlooked at the time of the Atlético press conference but Mac Allister’s refusal to use a painful groin injury as an excuse for last season’s struggles reflected the character of a winner. “I don’t think that was why,” he said that day, declining the easy option. “I take responsibility because it was not a good season for me individually and for us as a team.”

The midfielder’s sense of responsibility extends to implementing Iraola’s instructions for his new team. Figures from Opta show Mac Allister is winning more tackles per Premier League game this season – 2.3 on average compared to 1.8 last season; winning more duels (4.8 from 3.8); winning more aerial duels (0.9 from 0.6) and winning more possession (5.6 on average compared to 3.8). He is sacrificing the offensive side of his game to bring more aggression and organisation to the defensive aspect, and his touches in the opposition box, chances created, goals and assists are all down on last season as a consequence. Not that Iraola is complaining.

View image in fullscreen Alexis Mac Allister, pictured in action against Brentford, has rekindled his dominating form from Liverpool’s 2025 title season. Photograph: Kin Cheung/AP

“The thing about Mac Allister is that he understands the game overall, not just the demands of his position,” Iraola added. “It is just what is happening overall in the game. Sometimes he is the first one to correct his teammates, not just the one who is next to him. He understands what is happening around him which is a very important quality to have.”

Last season, and early in the current one as Liverpool adapted to their change of coach, there would have been concern at Anfield over the potential damage an Arsenal midfield of Declan Rice, Bruno Guimarães and Martin Ødegaard could inflict on Sunday. They still might, with Iraola saying his team need to improve “almost everywhere”. But talk of the midfield being frequently overrun has fallen silent during a winning run underpinned by aggression, resilience and intensity. Mac Allister has embodied it all. His negotiating position is strong once again.

Sports.title: Grealish could have been Everton’s poster boy of a new era. Now his career is in limbo
Sports.content:
For the biggest game in Manchester City’s history, Jack Grealish was given a starting berth while Phil Foden, Julián Alvarez and Riyad Mahrez were on the bench. Grealish played the full 90 minutes of the Champions League triumph against Inter because Pep Guardiola had the greatest faith in the attacking midfielder, but three years on he is at risk of being yesterday’s man.

That trust dwindled, not helped by injuries, and Grealish made only 17 Premier League starts over the next two seasons under Guardiola. City wanted him to leave in the summer of 2025, and Everton provided the solution, taking him on loan and borrowing him again for this season. Six Everton appearances into this campaign he was left out of the squad for Thursday’s Carabao Cup win against Newcastle after missing training on Monday. Everton went public with the fact that there had been “a breach of club discipline”.

Grealish is 31 and has 39 England caps. He is supposed to be a senior player but his career has involved far too many indiscretions. Breaking lockdown rules, a driving ban and more than once becoming a viral sensation for being pictured inebriated out and about have painted an unwanted picture. Learning from mistakes is part of life but Grealish’s indiscipline is apparently not dwindling with age. Guardiola warned him over his behaviour, dropping him in 2021 for a match against Newcastle after he and Foden arrived for training worse for wear.

Grealish is aware of his flaws, which is a starting point, but dealing with them is a separate matter. “People go: ‘He likes to go out, he likes to party,’ and I do,” Grealish told Sky Sports last year. “I want to be able to live my life and enjoy myself but obviously there’s a time and a place to do that. Sometimes, I’ll be honest with you, I probably haven’t picked the right times.”

Initially at Everton it seemed Grealish could be the poster boy of a new era. There were winners against Crystal Palace and Bournemouth by early December of last year and he had accumulated six assists in 20 Premier League appearances before his season was ended in mid-January by a foot injury. Grealish had been inconsistent, though. He has not played more than 28 league games in a season since 2019-20 at Aston Villa, which should concern him.

There were reservations at Everton about taking Grealish back this summer but Iliman Ndiaye’s sale to City made it a pragmatic move to fill the void. Grealish had carried out pre-season under Enzo Maresca, who gave him chances in the Community Shield and on the opening day against Bournemouth. The Italian had time for him but the unlikely redemption arc at City was soon quashed. Maresca showed affection for Grealish on Friday, saying: “I still think that he’s a good boy, big heart.”

View image in fullscreen David Moyes was terse on the subject of Jack Grealish and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond the length of his current loan. Photograph: Tony McArdle/Everton FC/Getty Images

At his best, Grealish is a wonderful player, a carefree spirit when dribbling with his socks around his ankles. In full flow, he gets fans up off their seats, makes and takes goalscoring chances and forces opponents to foul him, but those moments have been fleeting for far too long. The next seven months are crucial to Grealish’s career; he is at an age where he could play at the top for years but his status is declining rapidly. He is a £100m City signing and treble winner but those are past glories. Grealish needs to prove he has the respect for himself and for Everton to want more.

Grealish’s contract at City concludes at the end of the season, so there is plenty of incentive for him to show he is capable of shining in the Premier League and inspiring Everton to the cup win they crave. Instead, his career is in limbo. David Moyes was terse on the subject of Grealish on Thursday and seems unlikely to recommend keeping him beyond his loan. The Everton manager is working with a very small squad, so losing a senior player for avoidable reasons will surely frustrate and irritate him.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In an industry where the public is kept at arm’s length, Grealish is very approachable, happy to sign autographs for longer than his peers, eager to do the charity elements that come with playing for major clubs and known for his personal touch when others are businesslike. When entering and leaving Hill Dickinson Stadium, Grealish is mobbed, such is his popularity. He embraces it, posing for selfies with anyone who demands one, channelling a lot of positive energy into others, but he needs to find the self-awareness to do the same for himself.

“With me, I’m a big confidence player – I want to feel loved,” Grealish once said. He will not be feeling that from Moyes any time soon without radical change.

Sports.title: ‘We are not in Disneyland’: Arteta warns Dowman of Arsenal’s demands
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has warned Max Dowman that he “is not in Disneyland” and must learn from his red card against Fleetwood after Arsenal’s appeal against his three-match suspension was rejected.

The 16-year-old became the youngest player ever to be sent off in the League Cup on Tuesday as the Premier League champions crashed out to the League Two side Fleetwood. Arteta said he was “very disappointed” that the Football Association rejected the appeal against his red card and felt Dowman was lucky not to suffer a broken foot from “reckless tackles”.

But despite describing his reaction as “minimal”, the Arsenal manager revealed he had spoken to Dowman this week to underline his responsibilities after he was also sent off this month playing for England Under 19s.

“I’ve done it, so I try to prevent that [in future]. That’s why I’m so protective of these things and especially with young players, because we have made those mistakes. You know how much you can get punished and how much it can change what happens next, and it’s not the first time, so obviously we need to put an end to it very, very quickly,” Arteta said.

Arteta said he had not seen the criticism of his angry reaction to Dowman’s red card, when he appeared to aim a few choice words towards the forward as he headed down the tunnel. But he defended his actions after warning Dowman he was likely to be targeted before the game. “It’s something that we discussed just before we went out, because it’s not the first time that happened,” he said.

“For me, it was the best reaction ever to be able to be who I am. You want to see the reaction of his teammates? When they have to play with 10, you want to see that? That’s the level, and that’s the reaction. But the reaction when I don’t win, you know what the reaction is? I’m pissed off, big time.

“So we need to be ready for that. This is the environment and this is the reality. Otherwise, we are in Disneyland. We are not in Disneyland. We are in the Premier League at this level and we look after him so much that you cannot imagine. But at the same time, we’re going to demand [from] him like anybody else because he needs to earn the right to play.”

Dowman will be suspended for Sunday’s trip to Liverpool and the games against Hull and Newcastle, while Noni Madueke faces a late test to see if he has recovered from an ankle problem that kept him out of the game against Fleetwood. Arteta also revealed that Bukayo Saka is not expected back until at least after the international break as Arsenal await more news on his thigh injury.

Arteta said they had “put every argument on the table” in an attempt to clear Dowman’s name but to no avail. “Very disappointed,” he said. “Especially with the reckless tackles that he received, and then his reaction is minimal in relation to the action.

“I think you have to read the context of the player, the age, and what happened previously. It could have been really bad. And we are lucky today that he hasn’t had a broken foot. That’s clear.”

Sports.title: Putellas provides mindset change as London City bid to upstage champions
Sports.content:
As Martin Semmens, the London City Lionesses chief executive, sits down is his office he looks like the cat that got the cream. He says he has just learned that the club’s Instagram page has generated 34m hits since Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d’Or on Monday evening, and it is only Thursday afternoon. On Sunday, two clubs with seven of the top 30 players in the Ballon d’Or rankings will go head-to-head when Manchester City visit Hayes Lane, Bromley. It is, Semmens, says, “awesome for the WSL”.

From the outside, it can feel slightly surreal. The independent women’s club, owned by the businesswoman Michele Kang, are third in the top flight, two‑and‑a‑half years after finishing eighth in tier two, and Semmens believes signing the world’s best player has helped change the mindset of everyone at the club.

“Her impact on our commercial business is extraordinary,” he says. “From a leadership point of view, she allows us to start thinking about really winning. The environment today feels like it can beat Man City on Sunday and that’s a lot down to her.”

He acknowledges that Putellas, a World Cup winner with Spain and four-time European champion with Barcelona, and her brand – she has more Instagram followers (3.7m) than a men’s club the size of Porto, for example – were pivotal in helping the club secure what they claim is the largest front-of-shirt sponsorship deal in the women’s game, with Nike. The club say it is worth more than the new NWSL franchise Atlanta’s sponsorship of $4m (£3m) a year.

“It’s insanely big,” Semmens says. “Our view on how to run this business, rightly or wrongly, was to invest first, invest in the everything to make it awesome, and then the commercial deal will be big. The other way, of: ‘Let’s sit back, let’s grow a fanbase, let’s wait for the money to come’ – we don’t have the patience for that. Michele’s vision was: ‘I’m going to invest now to prove that we can bring these deals in.’ That deal allows us to kick forward, it allows us to keep investing in players and infrastructure, because without it, we’re just burning Michele’s money, which is not the plan.”

Even with Kang’s money, signing a player who had been loyal to Barcelona for 14 years was never going to be straightforward. Semmens, the former Southampton chief executive, says: “The conversation went: ‘Wait until I’ve finished winning a Champions League with Barcelona and then we’ll have a conversation,’ which we loved and we respected, but we always had a feeling she would come.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas has provided a huge commercial lift to the club. Photograph: Alex Ferrelly/Sports Press Photo/Shutterstock

“I think she had bought into four or five significant things. One, that we are independent, we’re a women’s-first environment. [Two] there’s a lot of power in coming to London, as a city. The WSL is important – people see WSL as the growth brand. And, after that, Michele had an unbelievably massive impact [on Putellas’s decision]. Alexia said to me: ‘Well, she said she was going to do all this stuff and she’s done it. So I want to be part of that.’ And then also, it allows her to have a legacy in the future – she will grow this club to a point where she’s creating a pathway for the next young players to come through in London.”

There are questions facing the club in relation to how much they have been spending and eyebrows were raised – to put it mildly – around the rest of the league when London City recorded an operating loss of more than 10 times their revenue for the 2024-25 season, when they won promotion as second-tier champions. Since then salary cap rules have been introduced in the WSL, stating no club’s player wage bill can exceed the following figures combined: 80% of revenue, plus up to £4m or a further 25% of revenue (whichever is higher).

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas’s arrival has undoubtedly put London City Lionesses on the map. Photograph: Nina Farooqi/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock

Last season, when London City finished sixth, the league’s handbook said no punishments would be dished out for any breaches of that cap for that campaign only. From this term, points deductions could apply, which is one reason why it was imperative to increase commercial revenues. But were they within the rules last term?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“We are 100% within the rules, we will always be,” Semmens says. “It’s so important to Michele.” He says the “goal of the business” is to be profitable within five years and likens last year’s investments to a “start-up fund”: “The [salary cap] rules were set up with a clear understanding that they wouldn’t come until this year. The handbook is 100% clear. We want to see investment coming into the women’s game. Anything that kind of restricts positive and good investment obviously worries [me] but there is a need for rules and we’re 100% fine with that. We are super-transparent. We can reassure the fans that we are financially viable, sustainable, and we’ve made serious investments over the last two years to be profitable and successful in the future.”

Another question facing the club, particularly given their league position, is whether they would be eligible to compete in the Women’s Champions League, given Kang also owns the record eight-time European champions OL Lyonnes in France. Semmens says in reference to Uefa’s multi-club ownership rules: “One hundred per cent, it can be resolved. We will continue to argue the case that you should be able to [invest into multiple clubs] to see the women’s game accelerated.“It’s not about exchanging players like the men’s game. It’s not about one club dominating and the other being a feeder club. It’s a different model but we fully understand and respect the rules. Therefore, we will set ourselves up in a way where we’re allowed to and can compete in Europe together. There are clear rules, clear precedents in the men’s game and clear things you can do to allow both teams to flourish. We’re fully aware of that and we’ll comply with the rules.”

London City are three points off Chelsea and Manchester City, and Semmens says the aim is to “build a squad that is consistently in the top three”. He is looking forward to Sunday. “This is probably the No 1 game in the women’s game in the world this weekend,” he says. “That’s what we want to be: on the map.”
