​”So, while we believe deeply in prayer, we also recognise the need to do our part. As leaders, we took an oath to protect the lives and properties of our citizens.

“At the same time, we must continually seek Almighty Allah’s guidance and ease to help us protect our people, our states, and our nation”, Governor Sani stated.

Also, Governor of Borno State, Babagana Zulum, said the most important thing about the trip is the return of peace and tranquillity to Nigeria.

“We pray that Almighty Allah shall give us lasting peace and tranquillity in Nigeria. As we are with nothing coming closer to the election, we pray that everything will go well, and God will give us a better future, so that everyone in Nigeria will enjoy it.

“We believe there is nothing better than peace. We believe there is nothing better than unity of our own country, and therefore we should do everything possible that will ensure a peaceful election, Inshallah, Mr Zulum said.

A media aide to the president, Tunde Rahman, stated that regular spiritual rejuvenation has always been a core facet of MrTinubu’s life and leadership ethos,

Mr Rahman noted that President Tinubu has consistently made seeking divine intervention a steadfast annual devotion for years.

Mr ​Rahman recalled that since he began working closely with the Nigerian leader nearly a decade ago, Mr Tinubu has never missed dedicating time each year to seek the face of God, while using such solemn platforms to intercede on behalf of Nigeria and its citizens.

“Mr President has always been somebody who believes in regular spiritual rejuvenation. It has always been part of his life. I recall over the years, from about 2016, that I joined him. There’s never been a year that we didn’t come to seek the face of our Almighty Allah.

“He is a regular part of his life, and on occasions like that, he has always used the opportunity to pray for himself, to pray for the country, and I think this is a very critical moment where we need a lot of prayers”, Mr Rahman stated.

Former Zamfara State Governor and Director General of the APC presidential campaign council, Abdul’aziz Yari, described Mr Tinubu’s leadership as one grounded in prayer, reliance on God, and commitment to public service

Mr Yari highlighted the spiritual and moral posture of the leadership, noting that the nation’s helmsman prioritises the collective welfare of Nigerians through continuous prayer.

“That is what makes a leader because when you ask him, he first pray for the country, pray for every Nigerian being the leader, and also he said this election is election of God has selected the person will be a leader, only him that can put a leader otherwise. So in total, he depended on Almighty Allah to do it for him, as he did it for him in 2023.

“By God’s grace, we should welcome and work. That’s all the procedure we have been under: the protocol to campaign, to talk to people, to convince them, to show them what we have done, what we achieved, and by God’s grace, people will be convinced to elect us”, Mr Yari stated.

The president’s spiritual exercise in Saudi Arabia follows a flurry of high-level political and international engagements by the Nigerian leader.

Before the spiritual journey, President Tinubu had returned from a month-long foreign trip to Europe.

Upon his return to domestic engagements, the President officially flagged off the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign in Kaduna State, where thousands of party chieftains, governors, and supporters rallied behind his re-election bid ahead of the upcoming general elections.

During the Kaduna rally, Mr Tinubu renewed his pledge to consolidate economic recovery, tackle poverty, and deepen infrastructure development across the country.

​Shortly after launching the nationwide campaign in Kaduna, President Tinubu departed the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja on Thursday afternoon for Saudi Arabia.

According to the Presidency, the visit was strictly a personal spiritual journey aimed at performing Umrah and seeking divine guidance, unity, and sustained peace and progress for the nation.

World.title: PT Health Watch: How to stay safe as El Niño raises heat risks in Nigeria
World.content:
As El Niño influences global weather patterns and raises the likelihood of above-normal temperatures in parts of the world, Nigerians may face increased health risks from extreme heat, particularly amid unreliable electricity supply and limited access to cooling facilities.

Staying safe during periods of intense heat requires simple but deliberate measures, including adequate hydration, proper ventilation and recognising the early warning signs of heat-related illnesses.

El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon characterised by unusually warm surface waters in the central and eastern equatorial Pacific Ocean. It influences atmospheric circulation, often resulting in significant changes in temperature and rainfall patterns across different parts of the world.

According to the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet), El Niño increases the likelihood of above-normal temperatures in many parts of the world and can significantly alter rainfall patterns.

In August, NiMet issued a seasonal climate forecast indicating that observations of the Pacific Ocean suggested the onset of a strong El Niño event, which was expected to influence global climate patterns between August and October.

“The evolving super El Niño event represents one of the strongest ocean-atmosphere phenomena in recent decades, with significant implications for Nigeria’s rainfall patterns,” the agency said.

During the three-month period, the agency projected wetter-than-normal conditions across parts of northern Nigeria, particularly Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Katsina, Kano, Yobe, Borno, Bauchi and Jigawa states.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

However, parts of southern Nigeria, including Oyo, Ogun, Lagos, Osun, Ekiti, Edo and Delta states, were expected to experience drier-than-normal conditions.

The forecast also indicated that Kogi and parts of Benue State could experience drier-than-normal conditions.

Health risks of extreme heat

Prolonged exposure to high temperatures can overwhelm the body’s ability to regulate its internal temperature, potentially resulting in heat-related illnesses such as heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

Heat exhaustion occurs when the body loses excessive amounts of water and salt through sweating. Its symptoms include heavy sweating, weakness, dizziness, headache, nausea and an elevated body temperature.

Heat stroke, however, is a more severe and potentially life-threatening condition that occurs when the body’s temperature regulation system fails. Warning signs include confusion, altered behaviour, irritability, seizures and loss of consciousness.

Speaking with PREMIUM TIMES, Tanimola Akande, a professor of public health at the University of Ilorin, said extreme heat associated with El Niño could increase the risk of heat exhaustion and heat stroke in Nigeria.

Mr Akande said unreliable electricity supply makes it more difficult for many households to cope with high temperatures, particularly those who depend on electric fans and air conditioners for cooling.

He also warned that prolonged exposure to extreme heat could negatively affect agricultural productivity.

However, he said individuals and households could adopt practical measures to reduce their exposure to excessive heat.

How to stay safe

According to Mr Akande, improving ventilation is one of the affordable ways households can make their living spaces cooler.

“Low-cost ways to stay cool and prevent heat stroke include ensuring adequate ventilation with big windows and ensuring cross ventilation,” the public health physician said.

He also recommended planting trees around homes to provide shade and reduce direct exposure to sunlight.

Mr Akande advised Nigerians to wear loose-fitting, lightweight clothing and avoid dark-coloured clothes that absorb more heat.

He also emphasised the importance of drinking sufficient water throughout the day, even when they do not feel thirsty.

People should also avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight, particularly during the hottest hours of the day, and take regular breaks in shaded or cool environments.

What to do in an emergency

Mr Akande said prompt action is essential when someone develops symptoms of heat exhaustion or heat stroke.

“If someone collapses from heat exhaustion, the person should be moved away from the area to a cool place, remove extra clothing and use cold water to tepidly sponge the person,” he said.

He added that water or an oral rehydration solution could be given to someone who is conscious and able to swallow.

However, he cautioned against forcing someone who is unable to drink independently to take fluids.

“If the person is unable to drink on his or her own, he or she should not be forcefully made to drink water. Plans should be made to take the person to the nearest health facility,” he said.

Heat stroke requires immediate emergency medical attention. While waiting for medical assistance, the affected person should be moved to a cooler environment and cooled rapidly using available methods, such as cold water, wet cloths and fanning.

People at greater risk

Although extreme heat can affect anyone, some groups are more vulnerable to heat-related illnesses.

They include outdoor workers, children, older people and pregnant women. People living with chronic conditions, including diabetes and cardiovascular diseases, may also face increased risks.

These groups may require additional protection, including regular access to drinking water, shaded environments, adequate ventilation and reduced exposure to intense heat.

World.title: Oando reports 9% revenue growth to ₦2.78trn as production rises 14% Sept ending 2026
World.content:
Oando Plc, Africa’s leading indigenous energy solutions provider listed on both the Nigerian Exchange and Johannesburg Stock Exchange, has published its unaudited results for the nine months ended 30 September 2026. The Group recorded nine percent increase in revenue to ₦2.78 trillion, reflecting higher crude oil liftings, increased gas and Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) sale volumes, and improved average realised prices. Operating performance also strengthened, with the Group moving from an operating loss of ₦109.7 billion in 9M 2025 to an operating profit of ₦159.7 billion in 9M 2026.

Gross profit increased by 483% to ₦174.5 billion, compared with ₦29.8 billion in the corresponding period of 2025, reflecting improved production efficiency with a reported facility uptime of 96.1% compared to 85%.

Commenting on the results, Wale Tinubu, Group Chief Executive of Oando PLC, said: “Our performance in the first nine months of 2026 demonstrates how diligent execution under our operatorship, supported by our renewed investment drive, is delivering greater efficiency, improved reliability, lower unit costs and ultimately higher production across our expanded upstream portfolio. Production averaged 42,985 boepd, up 14% year-on-year, while facility uptime improved to 96.1% and production operating costs declined by 22% to US$15.39 per boe. These gains were achieved with zero fatalities and zero lost-time injuries across approximately 14.9 million hours worked.”

Average daily production of the Group’s upstream subsidiaryincreased from 37,614 boepd in 2025 to 42,985 boepd in 2026, with growth across crude oil, gas and NGLs. Crude oil production rose 12% to 12,193 barrels per day, gas production increased 13% to 28,689 boepd, and NGL production grew 53% to 2,103 barrels per day in 2026.

Crude oil liftings rose 43% to 3.97 MMbbl, while natural gas sales rose five percent to 34.01 billion standard cubic feet (Bscf). NGL sales increased by 90% to 0.57 million barrels. In total, E&P sales volumes rose by 21% to 10.21 million barrels of oil equivalent (MMboe).

Operational improvements further strengthened performance. Production operating costs declined by 22% to US$15.39/boe, reflecting cost optimisation across transport, logistics, services, and information and communications technology, alongside higher production across a largely fixed field cost base. Oando recorded zero fatalities and zero lost-time injuries across approximately 14.9 million hours worked during the period, an increase of 55% in total hours workedfrom the corresponding period of 2025. Its improved facility uptime also strengthened the reliability of production and evacuation infrastructure, supporting the Group’s capacity to handle additional volumes as its development programme progresses.

Total borrowings declined to ₦2.16 trillion, 22% below the peak recorded at the end of 2024, while cash generated from operations reached ₦285 billion. The Group also invested ₦110.7 billion in capital expenditure, primarily directed towards drilling across OMLs 60–63.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Group’s seven-well drilling programme for 2026 has progressed across its operated assets. Idu 6ST and Idu 15 have been completed and brought on stream, while workovers at Samabri 4T and Samabri 7T have been completed. Drilling is ongoing at Idu T and Samabri A50, with the final well, Ogbainbiri, scheduled to spud in December 2026.

On completion, the drilling campaign is expected to add approximately 16,000 to 20,000 boepd (gross) of production, helping to sustain output and offset natural field decline across the operated portfolio and support its medium-term ambition of approximately 100,000 boepd in the next four to five years.

In clean energy, electric buses deployed through Oando’s electric mobility partnership with the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) recorded more than 212,000 passenger journeys in the first nine months of 2026, with average capacity utilisation of 73%. An additional 11 electric buses – the first batch of a planned 50 – arrived in Lagos, bringing the fleet to 13. The expanded fleet is expected to enter service in the fourth quarter, with LAMATA operating the buses on behalf of Lagos State.

Oando enters the final quarter of 2026 focused on completing its drilling programme, sustaining operational performance and advancing its capital management initiatives. The Group has narrowed its full-year production guidance to 40,000–45,000 boepd and expects full-year capital expenditure of approximately US$90 million to US$100 million, focused on high-impact, short-cycle upstream activities.

Commenting on the Company’s outlook, Mr Tinubu said: “For the remainder of 2026, our priorities are to progress the seven-well development programme, sustain operational reliability and strengthen shareholders’ funds through our impending equity raise. These initiatives are intended to reduce leverage, enhance our capacity to fund growth and support future shareholder distributions. We have demonstrated what we can achieve across our strategic assets and are confident in the opportunities ahead. Our commitment remains to realise the full potential of our substantial resource base and deliver lasting value for our shareholders.”

With production growth, improved operational efficiency and a stronger cash flow position, Oando is focused on sustaining its operational momentum, advancing its drilling programme,and strengthening its financial position to support long-term growth and shareholder value.

World.title: Iheanacho targets Bursaspor legendary status after record-breaking start in Turkey
World.content:
Super Eagles striker Kelechi Iheanacho has set his sights on becoming a Bursaspor legend, with the Nigerian forward determined to help the Turkish club secure promotion to the Süper Lig.

Iheanacho has enjoyed a remarkable start to life in Turkey, scoring 16 goals in his first 12 league appearances for Bursaspor, who currently lead the TFF First League table. The 30-year-old has found the net in every league match he has featured in and has become the first player in Turkish league history to score in 12 consecutive appearances.

The former Celtic forward joined Bursaspor as a free agent during the summer, but even he admits his early impact has surpassed his expectations.

Speaking to the club’s media team, Iheanacho described the TFF First League as a competitive division filled with quality players, while expressing his desire to maintain his impressive form as the campaign progresses.

“The First League is a really good and tough league. Incredible players are playing there. I didn’t expect to start this well. I want to show more of these performances as the season progresses,” he said.

Despite his outstanding individual numbers, Iheanacho insists that securing the league title and earning promotion to Turkey’s top flight remain his biggest priorities.

“At the end of the day, we aim to become champions and get promoted to the Süper Lig. We want to do this, and we are playing for it,” the striker added.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Beyond the immediate target of promotion, the former Leicester City and Manchester City forward also hopes to leave a lasting legacy at the club, admitting that becoming one of Bursaspor’s greats would mean a lot to him and his family.

“Becoming a legend of a great club like Bursaspor would be a great honour for me and my family. I hope something like that happens,” he said.

Iheanacho has already secured his place in Turkish football history. His goal against Muğlaspor on 15th October extended his scoring streak to 10 consecutive league matches, taking him past the previous record jointly held by Galatasaray legends Metin Oktay and Saffet Sancaklı.

He subsequently stretched that remarkable run in Bursaspor’s 4-2 victory over Keçiörengücü, a result that sent the club to the top of the standings with 28 points from 12 matches.

Bursaspor will welcome Bandırmaspor to the Centennial Atatürk Stadium on Saturday (today), with Iheanacho expected to lead the attack as the club looks to maintain its position at the summit.

The Nigerian striker will also be eager to extend his extraordinary scoring streak as he continues his pursuit of a historic season in Turkey.

World.title: Our part of Mbappe, China issue over – Real Madrid’s Mourinho
World.content:
(FILES) Real Madrid’s Spanish forward #10 Kylian Mbappe reacts during the Spanish league football match between Elche CF and Real Madrid CF at Martinez Valero Stadium in Elche on September 15, 2026. Kylian Mbappe was dropped on October 27 by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. (Photo by JOSE JORDAN / AFP)

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho said Saturday the club’s involvement in the controversy over Kylian Mbappe’s comments about an internet meme about himself and former Chinese leader Mao Zedong was over, after both the player and club apologised.

Mbappe’s remarks sparked a backlash in China, with Real Madrid, the France forward and La Liga all issuing apologies, but Chinese state television nevertheless pulled Spanish football from its schedules.

In a clip from an interview with French show “The Bridge” which has since been taken down, Mbappe had said he was amused by an internet meme showing his face photoshopped onto “some guy, think he’s a Chinese dictator”, an apparent reference to Mao.

Mourinho said both Mbappe and 15-time European champions Real Madrid “had the class” to issue swift apologies and believes there is nothing more for them to do.

“I’ve seen a lot of responsibility from a club which, at this level, is a club of great class, and as far as we’re concerned, that’s it, we’ve done our part, there’s nothing more for us to do,” Mourinho told reporters.

Mocking former leader Mao — blamed by historians for millions of deaths — is taboo in China, and the 27-year-old’s remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure to anger Beijing.

“With this situation involving China, these are the dangers of today’s world, where many times the best thing you can do is keep your mouth shut, because there’s danger in so many things you say or comment on,” said Mourinho.

Mbappe has endured a difficult week, after he finished second behind Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane in Monday’s Ballon d’Or ceremony.

Mourinho praised Mbappe’s reaction after England international Kane was named the world’s best player.

“Kylian is very intelligent, very mature, with a very high level of self-esteem,” said Mourinho.

“At the same time, he shows real class in the way he’s interpreted the Ballon d’Or going to Harry. In him I’ve only seen and felt class and respect.

“One thing is knowing you’re the best, and another is having respect for those who have also done a lot to win a trophy. From him I only see class.”

Mourinho said midfielder Jude Bellingham coming in 11th in the voting left him with his “mouth open”, implying the Englishman should have finished far higher.

However, the veteran Portuguese coach, who worked with Kane at Tottenham between 2019 and 2021, said he was happy for the Bayern hitman.

“I had the privilege of working with Harry, he’s a great player and a great professional and a great person,” added Mourinho.

“Inside the frustration that my player (Mbappe) didn’t win, well, I have to be honest and say I’m very happy for Harry, a player and a boy who deserves it.”

World.title: One dies, others injured in multiple accidents across Lagos
World.content:
By Olasunkanmi Akoni

The Lagos State Emergency Management Agency, LASEMA, has cleared three overnight and early morning emergencies across the state, with one fatality recorded in Epe and two persons injured in three major incidents.

According to reports, the first incident occurred at about 7:58pm on Friday on Odo-Iyalaro Bridge inward Maryland.

Permanent Secretary, Dr Olufemi Damilola Oke-Osanyintolu, said the operations reflect the commitment of the Babajide Sanwo-Olu administration to prompt emergency response.

The incident occurred when a Toyota Camry with registration number AGL-70HU and a Toyota Venza with registration number FST-893KF collided.

Preliminary investigation revealed that the Venza had stopped by the roadside due to fuel insufficiency, while the driver of the Camry who was suspected to be under the influence of alcohol rammed into the stationary vehicle.

Fortunately, no loss of life was recorded, however the driver of the Camry sustained injuries.

He was stabilised by the agency’s paramedics and Lagos State Ambulance Service, LASAMBUS before being evacuated to the Trauma Centre for further care. Both vehicles were towed to Area F Police Station and the bridge reopened to traffic.

Also at about 10:36pm, the Eagle Response Team responded to a broken down truck at Olosha, Mushin.

The team discovered a HOWO truck with registration number JJJ-293XZ stuck due to a failed portion of the road, blocking about 60 percent of the carriageway. No casualty was recorded.

Road diversion measures were put in place to manage traffic while before it was eventually towed away with the deployment of the agency’s heavy-duty equipment, restoring free vehicular movement.

In the third incident, at about 6:19am on Saturday, the Whales Response Team stationed at Epe responded to a road traffic accident at Oke-Oso inward Itokin, Epe involving two tipper trucks loaded with granite.

Investigation revealed that one of the trucks with registration number ABG-226XB suffered brake failure, lost control and had a side collision with another tipper.

Sadly, the motor assistant of the first truck was thrown off the vehicle and died on impact and one other injured.

The lifeless body was recovered, bagged and handed over to the Federal Road Safety Corps while both trucks were recovered and taken to the Federal Road Safety Commission, FRSC office.

LASEMA commiserated with the family of the deceased and urged motorists to maintain their vehicles, avoid driving under the influence of alcohol and adhere strictly to road safety regulations.

The agency assured residents of its readiness to respond to emergencies through its toll-free lines 767 and 112.

World.title: Iran has no plans for talks with US — Foreign minister
World.content:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi

Iran’s top diplomat on Saturday said there were no plans to hold talks with the United States despite growing concerns over a return to war.

“Currently, there are no plans for meetings with American officials, and any speculation to the contrary is merely media assumption,” Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said in an interview with Al Jazeera, according to the state news agency IRNA.

“Under current circumstances, Iran sees no necessity for a meeting with the Americans; Iran’s conditions are clear, and consultations regarding them are ongoing among mediators,” he said.

Araghchi confirmed that Iran received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, following days of diplomatic efforts to head off a return to violence.

“The message from American Vice President JD Vance has been carefully reviewed and discussed in high-level meetings,” he said.

“If Washington’s objective in sending the message is to sow discord, this would be yet another misstep, adding to America’s previous errors.”

But Araghchi added: “The American side’s effort to open a dialogue and reach a broader understanding is viewed as a positive step.”

AFP

World.title: Chelsea beat Man Utd 2-0, push Carrick closer to exit
World.content:
Manchester United’s Belgian goalkeeper #01 Senne Lammens is unable to save a penalty kick from Chelsea’s English midfielder #10 Cole Palmer (R) during the English Premier League football match between Chelsea and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge in London on October 31, 2026. (Photo by Glyn KIRK / AFP) / RESTRICTED TO EDITORIAL USE. No use with unauthorized audio, video, data, fixture lists, club/league logos or ‘live’ services. Online in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No video emulation. Social media in-match use limited to 120 images. An additional 40 images may be used in extra time. No use in betting publications, games or single club/league/player publications. /

Michael Carrick’s stay of execution as Manchester United boss may not last long after his team imploded in a 2-0 Premier League loss at Chelsea on Saturday.

The visitors wasted a string of chances to take the lead at Stamford Bridge before Morgan Rogers waltzed through the heart of the United defence to open the scoring on 50 minutes.

Lisandro Martinez then ruined any chance of a revival from Carrick’s men with two quickfire yellow cards, the second of which also conceded a penalty converted by Cole Palmer.

Winless in nine games, defeat leaves the 20-time English champions still just one point above the relegation zone and in danger of ending the weekend in the bottom three.

Many expected Carrick to be axed following last weekend’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth.

The former United midfielder was instead given the chance to turn his side’s fortunes around and will lament a lack of ruthlessness during the first half.

Carrick recalled captain Bruno Fernandes after he was left out last weekend in the wake of criticising his manager’s tactics during a 4-1 thrashing at Como in the Champions League.

Fernandes should have marked his return with the opener when he blazed over from Bryan Mbeumo’s inviting cross.

The roles were reversed when Mbeumo could not stretch to meet Fernandes’s delivery at the back post before twice Amad Diallo was denied by Chelsea’s stand-in goalkeeper Mike Penders.

United did finally get the ball in the net when Matheus Cunha turned in Harry Maguire’s header from a corner, but the Brazilian had strayed just offside.

Carrick could not hide his frustration in a half-time interview to broadcasters and his mood soured further with a disastrous start to the second period.

– Martinez sent off –

Rogers credits Carrick for revitalising his career during a spell together at Middlesbrough but dealt a potentially decisive blow to his former boss.

The England international collected the ball inside the centre circle but was allowed to drive directly towards the United goal before dinking the ball over Senne Lammens.

Martinez also spoke out publicly in recent weeks to criticise United’s lack of spending in the transfer market to bolster Carrick’s squad.

But on this season’s evidence, Martinez is one of those most in need of replacing.

The Argentine international could not cope with Rogers’s strength moments later as he was penalised for hauling back the Chelsea forward.

From the resulting free-kick, Martinez then needlessly crashed into Wesley Fofana with a raised forearm.

After a VAR review, referee Peter Banks awarded a penalty and showed Martinez a second yellow card.

Lammens got hands to Palmer’s spot-kick but still allowed the ball to trickle into the bottom corner.

On a rare start since Xabi Alonso took charge of the Blues, Estevao had a third goal disallowed for offside when he crashed Palmer’s pass into the top corner.

Cries of “sacked in the morning” rained down from the Chelsea fans as their side toyed with United for the final quarter without adding to their lead.

Another big decision awaits the United hierarchy before a massive Champions League clash at home to Roma on Tuesday.

Beaten in two of their three European games so far, United face both the embarrassment and financial shock of an early exit should they fall to another defeat against the Italians at Old Trafford.

AFP

World.title: Two suspected Ebola cases identified in North-East Nigeria – NCDC
World.content:
Two suspected cases of Ebola disease have been identified in Nigeria’s North-East region, with both individuals isolated as health authorities conduct investigations and laboratory tests.

An update on the disease situation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), said contact identification and listing were ongoing, while samples from the suspected cases were being subjected to laboratory testing.

It clarified that the classification of the individuals as suspected cases did not mean they had tested positive for Ebola, noting that confirmation would depend on laboratory results.

The public was advised to maintain proper hand hygiene, practise enhanced sanitation and follow preventive guidance issued by public health authorities.

The update added that further information would be provided as verified details become available.

World.title: 2027: ‘Three factors that’ll swing votes for Tinubu’
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

The Director General of the ruling All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, has named President Bola Tinubu’s faith in God, his record of performance and the campaign organisation’s capacity to win the hearts of the electorate as the three factors that will swing votes for him in January’s presidential election.

Read Also: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain

Yari, a former Governor of Zamfara State, spoke with journalists at the weekend in Mecca, Saudi Arabia, where he joined the President and other eminent Nigerians to perform Umrah, the muslim lesser pilgrimage. The footage of the interview was obtained on Saturday in Abuja.

He said the three factors would ultimately secure victory for Tinubu, and reaffirmed the APC-PCC’s commitment to securing the buy-in of Nigerians for the President’s second-term bid.

His remarks followed a media chat in Saudi Arabia on Friday, at which Tinubu expressed what he called enormous faith in God to be re-elected.

“I believe that Allah’s wish in His court must prevail. And there’s no other God but Allah. Allah is the only one who can define a human being, what he will be, and what he will become”, he said.

Yari said the President’s response was the mark of a true leader.

“That is what makes a leader, because when you ask him, he first prayed for the country, prayed for every Nigerian and also he says this election is an election that God has selected the person who will be a leader, and only Him that can put a leader or otherwise,” he said.

The APC-PCC boss added that the campaign would match that faith with work on the ground.

“So in total, I depend on Allah to do it for him as he did it for him in 2023. By that, Allah says we should work, that all the procedures we are undertaking, to campaign, to talk to people, to convince them, to show them what we have done, what we have achieved and that by His grace, people will be convinced to elect us,” he said.

World.title: ADC-PCC gives Sokoto authorities 24-hr ultimatum over attack on guber candidate
World.content:
By Luminous Jannamike

The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) has given security authorities in Sokoto State 24 hours to arrest those behind an attack on its governorship candidate, Alhaji Munir Dan Iya.

The ultimatum followed the alleged attack by operatives of the state-owned Sokoto Marshals, the vandalisation of several vehicles in the candidate’s convoy and the reported abduction of two Department of State Services (DSS) personnel attached to him.

In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC said the attack occurred along Airport Road, Sokoto, on Friday night, as Dan Iya returned to the city after accompanying former governor and Senator representing Sokoto South, Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, from the airport.

Ologbondiyan said the candidate’s personal SUV was among the vehicles vandalised, adding that Dan Iya had personally reported the incident to the Sokoto State Commissioner of Police.

But the council said the attack was only part of a wider campaign of intimidation, alleging that operatives of the Sokoto Marshals had taken positions at various historic gates into the metropolis, harassing motorists and targeting vehicles displaying ADC posters, insignia and other party symbols.

It said the reported abduction of two DSS personnel attached to the candidate had further heightened concerns over the incident.

“This is not governance. It is banditry in uniform, and it must not be tolerated in a democracy,” Ologbondiyan declared.

The ADC-PCC described the incident as part of what it called a growing pattern of political violence against opposition figures, recalling similar attacks reportedly recorded in Kaduna and other states in recent weeks.

It warned that the party would no longer stand by while its candidates, leaders and members were subjected to intimidation and violence, insisting that it was prepared to defend their constitutional rights through every legitimate means.

The council called on the Inspector-General of Police, the Sokoto Commissioner of Police and relevant security and intelligence agencies to immediately investigate the attack, arrest those responsible and secure the release of the two DSS personnel.

It gave the authorities 24 hours to rein in the operatives, guarantee the safety of its candidate and members, and commence decisive action against those implicated.

“Failure to do so will leave the leadership of our party with no option but to take further decisive and lawful steps to protect its members, defend its political rights and safeguard our democracy,” the statement warned.

The ADC-PCC cautioned that the alleged deployment of a taxpayer-funded security outfit against political opponents could push the country towards an era of state-backed political intimidation, insisting that it would resist any attempt to silence the opposition through violence.

World.title: Atiku’s son: ‘My support for Tinubu is personal’; pledges 10  buses
World.content:
Abba Abubakar

By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

The son of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Abba, has said his decision to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election is a personal choice made in conscience, which he acknowledged may be viewed against the political positions of people he shares family relationships with.

Read Also: ‘Northern leaders begged Tinubu to support Buhari, promised to return power after eight years’ – APC chieftain

Abubakar, Founder and Chairman of the Haske Bola Tinubu Organisation, HBTO, made the declaration at the group’s press conference in Abuja.

He said political decisions that differ from the positions of relatives “often attract considerable public attention” and that he was “equally conscious that my own political decision may be viewed within this context.”

“However, I wish to make one fundamental point: political conviction is a matter of personal judgement, conscience and the freedom of every individual to make independent choices,” he said.

He described the formation of HBTO as “a deliberate political choice, one I have made in my personal capacity and with a firm belief in the direction we have chosen to pursue.

“I hold no reservations about the right of others to their differing political opinions, just as I expect my own convictions to be respected,” he added.

Abba Abubakar said HBTO is a political mobilisation and support platform established to bring together Nigerians who share a common conviction in the leadership and reform agenda of the president and the All Progressives Congress, APC-led administration.

On Tinubu’s reforms

He admitted that the president’s reforms “have come with difficult adjustments for Nigerians,” but said it was “equally important to recognise the progress, opportunities and long-term benefits that several of these initiatives are designed to deliver.”

Citing examples, Abba pointed to the Nigerian Education Loan Fund, NELFUND, which he said “has opened new opportunities for students to access interest-free educational loans, helping to ease the financial burden on families and improve access to higher education.”

He also credited the administration’s investments in roads and other transport networks for “improving connectivity, facilitating the movement of goods and services, and strengthening economic activities across the country.”

On state finances, Abba Abubakar noted the increased revenue allocations to state governments through the Federation Account Allocation Committee FAAC, which he said have given states “greater fiscal capacity to meet their obligations, including the payment of salaries, pensions and other outstanding commitments.”

He added that public sector workers have benefited from “interventions aimed at cushioning the effects of prevailing economic realities, including the recent N70,000 transportation support.”

The HBTO chairman announced that the group would begin a transportation support programme with “the initial provision of 10 luxury buses,” starting in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja, before expanding to other parts of the country.

“For us, supporting the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda must translate into meaningful actions that positively affect the everyday lives of Nigerians,” he said.

Abubakar also disclosed plans for what he called a “two-million-man mobilisation march across Nigeria’s six geopolitical zones,” to begin in Abuja.

‘We are working with Wike’

He said the group’s immediate focus would be “supporting the FCT Minister, whom we recognise as a key political leader in our mobilisation structure, in the collective effort to secure victory for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu in the Federal Capital Territory in 2027.”

According to him, HBTO is working in alignment with the FCT Minister’s objective of delivering both the FCT and Rivers State for the president in the forthcoming election.

“Our organisation is preparing for a major political mobilisation exercise in Rivers State next week,” he said. “I can assure you that our structures are being activated, our members are on ground, and our supporters are ready to demonstrate the strength and reach of this movement.”

He said the effort was not about “numbers or political appearances,” but about “building a disciplined, coordinated and effective grassroots mobilisation network capable of translating political support into electoral results.”

Abba Abubakar said HBTO would establish a presence across the geopolitical zones and work with “political stakeholders, community leaders, youth organisations, women groups and other well-meaning Nigerians.”

“We are confident in our direction, committed to our objectives and determined to contribute our quota to the success of the President’s reform agenda and his re-election bid in 2027,” he said.

Vanguard News

World.title: Ikogosi Marathon 2026: Plateau Athletes Set Pace in 17.5km Race, Competition Eyes Global Recognition
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado Ekiti

Athletes from Plateau State on Saturday stamped their authority on the Ikogosi Marathon 2026 17.5km Race, emerging as the dominant force in the elite category as the competition continued its steady march towards international recognition.

The Plateau contingent produced a remarkable one-two finish, with Gyang James crossing the finish line first in 57 minutes, while his brother, Francis James, followed closely in 58 minutes to claim the second position. Rochas Sunday completed the podium after finishing third in 59 minutes.

The marathon, which began in Ilawe-Ekiti and ended at the iconic Ikogosi Warm Springs Resort in Ikogosi-Ekiti, attracted elite athletes from across Nigeria and foreign participants from Kenya and Ethiopia, with runners drawn from 28 states of the federation.

The event was attended by prominent dignitaries, including former Governor of Ekiti State, Chief Segun Oni; former presidential aide, Senator Babafemi Ojudu; Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly, Adeoye Aribasoye; Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the National Institute for Hospitality and Tourism (NIHOTOUR), Dr Abisoye Fagade; Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Student Engagement, Sunday Asefon, among others.

Beyond the competition, the 2026 edition of the Ikogosi Marathon reflected the growing ambition of the organisers to transform the race into a globally recognised sporting platform capable of promoting athletics, tourism and youth development in Ekiti State.

In the female elite category, Teyei Davou emerged winner, followed by Tanko Nvou in second position and Vivian Obadiah in third.

For the indigenous female category, Arinde Miracle, Bako Gift and Ademisoye Adesewa took the first, second and third positions respectively, while Adeyemi Tunde, Adetiba Abiodun and Sunday Emmanuel emerged the top three finishers in the indigenous male category.

Speaking on the significance of the event, the Convener of the Ikogosi Marathon Initiative, Makinde Araoye, said the fourth edition marked a major milestone, recording about 14,000 registrations and attracting participation beyond Nigeria.

Araoye said the marathon was established not only as a sporting competition but also as a vehicle for tourism promotion, economic development and talent discovery.

He disclosed that the initiative had identified 10 promising indigenous athletes from Ekiti State who would receive financial rewards and further support aimed at preparing them for international competitions.

According to him, the elite category winners received N5 million, N4 million and N2.5 million for first, second and third positions respectively, while the indigenous category was created to encourage and nurture home-grown talents.

Araoye, however, called for greater support from corporate organisations operating in the state, urging them to embrace the competition as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR).

He expressed optimism that the 2027 edition would be upgraded into a full international marathon, attracting more foreign athletes and creating greater opportunities for Nigerian long-distance runners.

“Our vision is to position Ikogosi Marathon as an international event that will expose Nigerian athletes to global competition. We want to create a platform where talents discovered here can compete and succeed internationally,” he said.

Also speaking, Sunday Asefon described the marathon as a strategic platform for youth empowerment, talent discovery and national unity.

Asefon urged the Ekiti State Government and relevant stakeholders to invest in the indigenous athletes discovered through the competition, noting that sustained support could help them become internationally competitive.

For the champion, Gyang James, the victory was a reward for determination and improved preparation after he finished fourth in the previous edition.

James said his earlier disappointment motivated him to intensify training, adding that the Ikogosi Marathon had become an important avenue for Nigerian athletes to pursue their dreams and gain exposure.

World.title: Brown Chieftaincy House Launches N400m Trust for Widows, Indigent Students
World.content:
Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt

The Abobo Brown Chieftaincy House in Finima, Bonny Local Government Area of Rivers State, has launched a N400 million humanitarian trust to sustain the philanthropic legacy of Aseme-Alabo Abinye Owen Brown and expand support for widows, indigent students and other vulnerable members of the community.

The Chief Abinye Owen Brown Excellence and Legacy Trust were unveiled during a ceremony marking the traditional leader’s birthday, with organisers describing the initiative as a deliberate effort to institutionalise his two decades of humanitarian service and ensure its sustainability for generations.

The trust will focus on education, youth empowerment and humanitarian assistance through two major programmes: the Widows Support Scheme and the Students Educational Support Scheme.

Speaking at the event, Chairman of the Planning Committee, Boma Kuronye, said the initiative was designed to immortalise Brown’s values while recognising his contributions to the welfare of the people.

“We are gathered not to mourn but to honour a living legend in his lifetime. We are gathered to institutionalise the values of a man who is still with us, still guiding us, and still serving Finima,” he said.

Kuronye described Brown as a traditional leader whose commitment to humanity transcended titles and positions.

“Aseme-Alabo Abinye Owen Brown has taught us that true greatness is not in titles but in how many burdens you lift for others. For decades, he has been a father to many, a counsellor to the House, and a quiet pillar for widows and students in Finima,” he said.

The Widows Support Scheme is also designed to improve the livelihoods of widows and restore their dignity, while the Students Educational Support Scheme will provide assistance to indigent students to ensure that financial difficulties do not deny them access to education.

According to the planning committee, the establishment of the trust marks a transition from individual acts of generosity to a structured institution capable of delivering consistent and long-term humanitarian interventions.

A citation presented in Brown’s honour described him as a respected custodian of Ibani culture and tradition, a bridge-builder and a humanist whose contributions to Finima and Grand Bonny extend beyond philanthropy.

It also acknowledged his role in promoting reconciliation, preserving the community’s history and defending its territorial integrity.

Beyond his traditional responsibilities, Brown has earned recognition for supporting widows and sponsoring indigent students, often without seeking public attention.

The citation highlighted his belief that “education is the only inheritance that cannot be stolen,” while stressing that the strength of a community could also be measured by how it treats its widows.

The ceremony attracted members of the Abobo Brown Chieftaincy House, traditional rulers, youth representatives, women’s groups, beneficiaries and other stakeholders.

The organisers said the trust was established during Brown’s lifetime to enable him to witness the impact of his humanitarian vision.

They expressed optimism that the initiative would expand educational opportunities, improve the welfare of vulnerable households and provide a sustainable framework for community development in Finima and beyond.

World.title: Edo Community Pleads with Okpebholo for Reversal of Clan Head Removal
World.content:
Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

Concerned Indigenes of Ikpeshi/Egbigere Clan in Akoko-Edo Local Government Area of Edo State have appealed to Governor Monday Okpebholo to reverse the removal of Regent Nicholas Saliu Odamah III and the reinstatement of Lukeman Momodu Odamah III, as the traditional ruler of the clan.

It would be recalled that Governor Okpebholo had on November 13, 2025, in a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government, Umar Musa Ikhilor, removed Lukeman Momodu and appointed Nicholas Odamah as regent pending the determination of the rightful occupant of the throne.

The state government, however, removed the regent in a statement issued by Secretary to the State Government on October 20, 2026, and reinstated Lukeman Momodu Odamah.

The government explained that the decision was taken in the interest of peace, stability and due process, and after reviewing appeals from Akoko-Edo indigenes and confirmed that the chieftaincy dispute was already before a court of competent jurisdiction.

But the group coordinator, Ms Peggy Agbo, in a news conference, made the appeal on behalf of the indigenes in Benin City.

She expressed concern that the state government’s decision could threaten the peace and stability currently enjoyed in the community

She said the community had experienced relative peace during the 11 months of Nicholas Odamah’s regency before he was removed, warning that the decision could heighten tensions if not urgently reviewed.

According to her, the group had also submitted a written objection to the governor and the State Executive Council and approached the court to maintain the status quo.

She appealed to the relevant authorities to intervene urgently and ensure that the dispute was resolved peacefully and in accordance with the law.

“We are appealing to Governor Monday Okpebholo, who is a man of peace, to suspend this action and reverse the decision contained in the statement issued by the Secretary to the State Government. We want peace, not war,” Agbo said,

Responding, Lukeman Momodu Odamah III, said the government has acted in accordance with the law and with the customary tradition of the people.

He said the case is in court and that protest cannot change the customer tradition of the people, advising the protesters to wait for the court to decide.

World.title: INEC Receives 5,400 Claims, Objections to Voter Register, Targets December 15 for Clean-up
World.content:
· Admits registration officers introduced AI-generated images, irregularities

· Amupitan: Commission has no preferred candidate, party for 2027 elections

· Atiku, ADC Demand Independent Forensic Audit, Allege Sabotage

Chuks Okocha, Adedayo Akinwale and Erizia Rubyjeana in Abuja

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) yesterday disclosed that it had received more than 4,800 claims and about 600 objections to the Preliminary Register of Voters, as it assured Nigerians that the cleaning of the register would be completed before December 15, 2026.

The development comes amid concerns over the discovery of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-generated photographs and other irregularities in the preliminary register, with the Commission admitting that some registration officers were responsible for introducing suspicious entries into the database.

However, the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and its presidential candidate, former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, have demanded a full explanation of how the photographs entered the register, the identification of officials responsible and an independent forensic audit of the database.

INEC Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed the number of claims and objections while receiving the ECOWAS Pre-Election Fact-Finding Mission at the Commission’s headquarters in Abuja.

Amupitan, in a statement issued yesterday by INEC Director of Voter Education and Publicity, Mrs. Victoria Eta-Messi, said the Commission was working to ensure that all claims and objections were addressed before the Final Register of Voters was certified on December 15, 2026.

He said: “The objections were received from the various wards through electoral officers and Resident Electoral Commissioners.

“The display of the register online is also confirming some of the complaints we had earlier received.”

He said the Commission has no preferred candidate or political party in the 2027 elections.

“Our sole allegiance is to the rule of law, the sovereign will of the Nigerian electorate, and the democratic progress of our nation,” he added.

The Chairman explained that given the size of the register, which now stands at over 103 million registered citizens, any discrepancies noticed during the display would be corrected ahead of the final release.

He also announced that the Commission planned a nationwide mock accreditation exercise in November to test accreditation and result transmission simultaneously in all states.

Amupitan said INEC had introduced a safeguard whereby results would be authenticated at the polling unit before they were transmitted to the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV).

He explained that when he assumed office, the question was whether to introduce a different technology, but that was not an option given the timeline, so the Commission focused on improving the existing system.

On its preparedness for the 2027 general election, he said the Commission had visited the South-west in Lagos, the North-west in Kaduna, the South-east in Enugu and, earlier in the week, the North-east in Gombe, with the North-central zone scheduled for a visit the following week.

He emphasised that the tours had already led to adjustments, particularly in areas requiring higher deployments because of terrain and security challenges.

The chairman also said the Commission was perfecting plans for Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) “to ensure inclusivity, that no one is completely excluded.”

Earlier, the leader of the ECOWAS mission and former Vice-President of Sierra Leone, Victor Bockarie Foh, said the mission was deployed on the strength of the Supplementary Protocol on Democracy and Good Governance, Article 53C of the ECOWAS Conflict Prevention Framework, and “the authority of heads of state decision to send pre-election fact-finding missions to member states holding elections.”

Meanwhile, INEC’s Director of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Dr. Lawrence Bayode, said the Commission would complete the cleaning of the preliminary register before December 15, 2026, following the discovery of AI-generated photographs and other irregularities during the public display.

Bayode gave the assurance during an interview on ARISE NEWS, saying the final register would address the anomalies identified by INEC and members of the public.

Speaking on the irregularities, he said the Commission was reviewing the entries and was confident that the final register would reflect the necessary corrections.

“So, we are working on that, we are cleaning up the register and we believe that the register that will be released on the 15th of December will have taken care of all this AI-generated or other irregularity pictures that we have also seen on the register,” he said.

He explained that although the Commission had deployed AI-powered chatbots for public enquiries and logistics support, it had not used the technology for voter registration.

“Like in logistics, we are deploying chatbots where people can ask questions and the AI will respond to them, deploy it in logistics to ease our logistics movement when it comes to moving materials from one location to the other,” he said.

Bayode attributed the irregularities to the actions of some registration officers who had access to the voter registration system.

“And this thing got into the register by the registration officers, because they have access to register people,” he said.

He added that the Commission’s findings showed that the problem was not restricted to locations whose suspicious entries had attracted attention on social media, but involved some registration officers across the country.

“What we have found out is that some of these registration officers, not only the place that we are seeing even on social media, some of them, not all of them now, some of them across the states nationwide, they have done different things to bring these irregularities onto the register,” he said.

The ICT director said INEC had identified how some of the irregularities were introduced into the system, although he could not explain the motive of the officers involved.

“When the ABs was run on the system, we saw these people, we know what they did, we know how they did it, but honestly, I don’t know why,” he added.

Bayode maintained that INEC had not deployed AI for voter registration, despite the appearance of AI-generated photographs on the preliminary register. He also assured Nigerians that the Commission had removed the irregularities identified by its officials and members of the public.

“I can assure you that all these irregularities that we have seen and that the Nigerians have seen, we have removed them from the register,” he said.

The preliminary register was displayed at registration areas between October 9 and 15 for public scrutiny. The exercise attracted concerns over suspicious photographs and other errors in the database.

Bayode said the preliminary register had recorded an increase of more than nine million voters over the 93 million registered voters used for the 2023 general election.

Atiku Demands Disclosure, Independent Audit

Reacting to the development, Atiku called on INEC to explain how AI-generated photographs and other questionable entries found their way into the register, identify those who submitted them and disclose the verification procedures they underwent.

In a statement issued by his media adviser, Paul Ibe, the former vice-president said the Commission’s description of the register as preliminary did not adequately address the circumstances that allowed the suspicious records into its database.

“With more than 103 million registered voters, Nigerians deserve precise answers: how many records are affected, what percentage of the register do they represent, and where are they concentrated?” he asked.

Atiku said public scrutiny of the preliminary register was important but could not replace effective verification by the electoral commission.

“But describing the register as ‘preliminary’ does not answer how those records entered the system in the first place. Public scrutiny is a safeguard; it cannot substitute for effective verification by the electoral umpire,” he said.

He warned that the discovery of suspicious photographs could raise questions about other possible anomalies, including duplicate identities, underage registrations and fictitious entries.

According to him, the Commission must demonstrate that the vulnerabilities in its database had been addressed before the 2027 elections.

Atiku therefore urged INEC to publish the number and geographical distribution of flagged records, explain how they entered the register, preserve the audit trail and allow an independent forensic audit involving political parties and credible civil society organisations.

He also called for the publication of the audit findings and corrective measures, while ensuring that voters’ personal information remained protected.

The ADC presidential candidate insisted that any official found to have deliberately compromised the register should face sanctions, while eligible voters must be protected against wrongful deletion during the cleanup.

In a separate statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku described the discovery of AI-generated images as a serious challenge to INEC’s credibility.

He faulted the Commission for acknowledging that some registration officers had introduced irregularities into the register without disclosing their identities or explaining the steps taken to hold them accountable.

“If INEC knows how the register was compromised, it must disclose the evidence, identify every officer involved and explain why they have not been suspended and prosecuted,” he noted.

Atiku also demanded an independent forensic audit, particularly in view of the allegation that more than 20 million AI-generated images might be involved.

He called for the preservation of voter records, image files, access logs and audit trails to enable independent experts, political parties, civil society groups and credible international observers to examine the evidence.

The former vice-president further accused INEC of failing to address opposition parties’ demands for disclosure of companies contracted to produce sensitive election materials.

ADC Alleges Sabotage, Cites Electoral Act

Also expressing concern, the ADC accused INEC of deliberately undermining its credibility ahead of the 2027 general elections, arguing that the discovery of AI-generated photographs and fictitious entries had exposed serious weaknesses in the Commission’s processes.

In a statement, the party’s National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, questioned why no arrests had been made despite INEC’s admission that some registration officers were responsible for introducing irregularities into the register.

“If INEC knows that its own officials compromised the voters’ register with AI-generated photographs, why has nobody been arrested? Why have these individuals not been handed over for prosecution? What exactly is INEC waiting for?” the party asked.

The ADC also accused the Commission of failing to publish the preliminary voters’ register online within the timeframe stipulated by Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act 2026, which requires the register to be made available for public scrutiny not later than 90 days before the general elections.

The party drew attention to Section 19(5), which it said makes failure by an INEC official to comply with the publication requirement a criminal offence punishable by a fine, imprisonment or both.

It questioned whether the Commission’s repeated difficulties in preparing the register reflected incompetence or a deliberate attempt to undermine the electoral process.

“We are beginning to wonder whether INEC is intentionally trying to make itself incompetent. Because how else do you explain an electoral umpire that had at least three years to prepare for elections, but is suddenly unable or unwilling to produce a credible voters’ register in accordance with the strict requirements of the law?” the party said.

The ADC warned that the Commission’s handling of the register had raised concerns about its willingness to comply with other mandatory provisions of the Electoral Act on election day.

It cited the use of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and serialised ballot papers as examples of safeguards that must be respected to ensure credible elections.

The party demanded an independent forensic audit of the register, the identification and investigation of officials implicated in the irregularities, and a public explanation of the Commission’s alleged failure to comply with the statutory publication requirement.

It insisted that compliance with the Electoral Act was not optional and urged INEC to demonstrate, through verifiable actions, that it was prepared to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027.

World.title: FG Rolls Out N50,000 Monthly Cash Relief for Vulnerable Nigerians
World.content:
Kuni Tyessi in Abuja

The federal government has commenced a monthly cash relief programme offering N50,000 to vulnerable households to cushion the impact of rising living costs.

The Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, announced this in a statement issued yesterday in Abuja.

Doro said the National Emergency Relief and Stabilisation Intervention (NERSI) was a presidential initiative designed to provide immediate financial assistance to millions of vulnerable Nigerians.

He said the intervention was introduced in response to global food inflation and rising costs of essential goods, which continued to place pressure on households.

“Under this intervention, eligible beneficiaries will receive N50,000 monthly, providing direct assistance to help meet essential needs and ease the burden of living costs,” he said.

The minister explained that the programme would be reviewed regularly in response to changes in the cost of living, with beneficiaries notified directly before any adjustment.

He said the ministry was working with licensed digital financial service providers to ensure secure, prompt and transparent delivery of the funds.

According to him, beneficiaries will receive text messages from the providers requesting their consent before payments are made directly into their bank accounts or mobile wallets.

Doro stressed that beneficiaries were not required to apply, pay any fee or register through agents to access the intervention.

He warned Nigerians against fraudsters, advising beneficiaries not to disclose their personal identification numbers (PINs) or Bank Verification Numbers (BVNs) to anyone.

“If you are unsure about any message, or anyone asks you for money, call the official NERSI helpline on 0700-022-2222,” he said.

The minister said NERSI complemented existing federal government social protection and economic support programmes, while supporting household resilience and economic stability.

He added that the intervention aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda and reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to delivering the programme with dignity, transparency and accountability.

World.title: Hamzat Unveils 100-point Agenda, Pledges Accountability for Campaign Promises
World.content:
*Sanwo-Olu urges Lagosians to sustain continuity

Segun James and Wale Igbintade

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Governorship candidate in Lagos State, Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, yesterday unveiled a 100-point development agenda for the State, pledging that his administration, if elected, would be judged by measurable achievements rather than political rhetoric.



Hamzat gave the assurance during the presentation of his governorship manifesto and campaign song at the Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and Creative Arts (formerly the National Theatre, Iganmu), Lagos, where he outlined proposals covering transportation, affordable housing, security, potable water, infrastructure, environmental management and youth empowerment.



He urged residents to scrutinise the manifesto, identify commitments that directly affect their families and communities, document them and demand explanations for any that remain unfulfilled.

“Take the promise, read it, question it. Find the commitment that matters most to you, to your family, your street, your community. Write it down,” he said.



He added: “Then, bring it back to me. Show me what I delivered. Show me what is left to do. Hold me accountable for both. That is my promise.”

The APC candidate said his ambition was to build a Lagos that works for all residents, with an administration focused on development, inclusion and improved living conditions.

“This is the mandate I ask of you. The opportunity to serve you as your governor. The responsibility to deliver and the duty to answer to you,” he declared.

On transportation, Hamzat promised to expand the state’s public bus fleet from the current 1,000 to more than 4,000, with a target of transporting one million passengers daily.

He also pledged to expand the rail network, promising to extend the Blue Line to Ojo and establish an interchange connecting the Blue and Red lines at the National Theatre station.

He further pledged to advance the proposed Green Line from Marina to the Lekki Free Zone in collaboration with the Federal Government.

According to him, the Blue Line, upon reaching Trade Fair station early next year, is projected to carry 250,000 passengers daily.

Hamzat said his administration would integrate road, rail and water transportation into a coordinated system supported by unified ticketing arrangements and timetables to make commuting easier for residents.

Under the water transportation component, he pledged to dredge an additional 140 kilometres of waterways, optimise 15 ferry routes, rehabilitate 27 of the existing 47 terminals and procure 75 electric ferry boats.

Describing Lagos as a water state, he said the lagoon should become the state’s third major transportation corridor.

On road infrastructure, the candidate promised an aggressive rehabilitation of inner roads across communities in partnership with local governments, local council development areas and the Lagos State Public Works Corporation.

He also pledged to reconstruct strategic traffic-bearing roads, activate the Fourth Mainland Bridge through partnerships, accelerate the regional road along the Lake Yembe axis and commence the second phase of the Ogbebe-Mindene Link Bridge to connect with the Third Axial Road.

On housing, Hamzat promised to make home ownership more accessible through a mortgage arrangement requiring an initial deposit of 10 per cent, lower interest rates and longer repayment periods.

On security, he promised to strengthen the Lagos State Neighbourhood Safety Agency and extend its operations to every ward across the state’s 20 local government areas and 37 local council development areas.

He also proposed establishing a state intelligence centre to strengthen the fight against cybercrime, financial crimes and organised criminal activities.

“Lagos has given me a lifetime of work. Today, I give Lagos my promise,” he declared.

He recalled his father’s advice on public service, saying he had been taught that leadership was fundamentally about serving the people.

“A promise is a loan. I have lifted it onto my head before you. I’m asking you to watch me carry it,” he said.

Earlier, Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, who attended the event as Special Guest of Honour, urged residents to sustain the APC-led administration in the state, saying ongoing development projects required continuity rather than experimentation.

He described Hamzat, his deputy for seven years, as an experienced public administrator who had been part of the state’s governance and development process for more than two decades.

Sanwo-Olu said Hamzat had served as commissioner under former governors Bola Tinubu and Babatunde Fashola before becoming deputy governor in 2019.

He recalled that Hamzat had stepped down from the 2018 governorship contest following the intervention of APC leaders and subsequently agreed to serve as his running mate.

The Governor described the decision as a demonstration of Hamzat’s loyalty and commitment to the party and the development of Lagos.

He also credited his deputy with playing significant roles in major projects and policy decisions, including the development of the Blue and Red rail lines and the Lekki Deep Sea Port.

Sanwo-Olu argued that Hamzat’s experience in successive administrations placed him in a position to sustain ongoing projects and advance the state’s development agenda.

Using a relay race analogy, he described the transition of leadership in Lagos as a process in which successive governors must build on the foundations laid by their predecessors rather than start afresh.

He identified ongoing projects, including the Fourth Mainland Bridge, the proposed Lekki-Epe International Airport, the Omu Creek project, food hubs and logistics parks, as initiatives requiring continuity beyond the present administration.

“This is not the time to experiment with Lagos. This is the time to consolidate,” he said.

Sanwo-Olu, who said he had seven months left in office, described a peaceful transition of power to his deputy as one of his administration’s most significant legacies.

He urged Hamzat to sustain public engagement, complete ongoing projects and preserve the institutional framework that had supported successive administrations.

Also speaking, former Lagos Deputy Governor and representative of the Governance Advisory Council (GAC), Princess Sarah Adebisi Sosan, stressed the importance of continuity while acknowledging the need to address emerging development challenges.

She said the state’s progress under successive administrations had resulted from deliberate planning, sacrifice and purposeful leadership.

According to her, the next administration should preserve policies and programmes that had delivered results while correcting identified shortcomings and introducing improvements where necessary.

She noted that Lagos’ growing population, expanding business activities and rising expectations required strategic planning and experienced leadership.

Sosan also urged the government to prioritise issues affecting residents, including transportation, road infrastructure, education, affordable healthcare, security, employment, housing and environmental sanitation.

Director-General of the PBAT-KOH Campaign Council, Senator Musiliu Obanikoro, pledged that the campaign would be peaceful, disciplined and issue-based.

He said the organisation would focus on Hamzat’s experience, competence and policy proposals rather than personalities or political structures.

Obanikoro said the campaign would take its message to every local government, ward and community across the state, emphasising the need for unity among APC leaders, members and supporters.

He explained that the campaign’s guiding principles, ‘Forward and Together’, represented the commitment to sustaining development while ensuring that every resident, irrespective of religion, ethnicity, occupation or social status, had a stake in Lagos’ progress.

He said the next administration must consolidate existing achievements, address development gaps and create additional opportunities for residents.

World.title: Rising Investor Confidence Lifts Stock Market to N165trn, Adds N65.7trn in 10 Months
World.content:
Kayode Tokede

Riding on improved macroeconomic conditions, stronger investor confidence and impressive corporate earnings, the Nigerian stock market added N65.74 trillion in value in the first 10 months of 2026, with market capitalisation crossing the N165 trillion mark for the first time.

The Nigerian economy has so far in 2026 witnessed relative stability in the foreign exchange market, renewed investor confidence, impressive corporate earnings, easing inflation, a cut in the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent by the Monetary Policy Committee of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), and improved liquidity in the financial sector.

Market capitalisation, which opened trading in 2026 at N99.376 trillion, has gained N65.74 trillion, representing a 66.15 per cent increase, to close at N165.114 trillion yesterday.

Similarly, the NGX All-Share Index advanced by 98,686.46 basis points, or 63.42 per cent Year-to-Date (YtD), from 155,613.03 basis points at the beginning of the year to 254,299.49 basis points.

Key market sectoral indicators showed that the NGX Oil/Gas Index led other indices as the best performer, while the NGX Insurance Index emerged as the worst performer in its YtD performance.

The NGX Oil/Gas Index gained 127.9 per cent YtD to close at 6,085.42 basis points as of October 30, 2026, while the NGX Insurance Index declined by 13.6 per cent YtD to close at 1,027.06 basis points.

The NGX Industrial Index, NGX Banking Index and NGX Consumer Goods Index advanced by 114.9 per cent, 60.27 per cent and 0.97 per cent YtD, respectively.

Checks by THISDAY showed that Airtel Africa Plc, Dangote Cement Plc and MTN Nigeria Communications Plc contributed an estimated N65.48 trillion, or 39.7 per cent, of the overall N165.114 trillion market capitalisation as of October 30, 2026.

The share price of Airtel Africa appreciated by 178 per cent YtD to N6,300 per share from N2,270 per share at the close of trading in 2025, while Dangote Cement advanced by 133.2 per cent YtD to N1,420 per share from N609 per share at the beginning of 2026.

In addition, the share price of MTN Nigeria Communications appreciated by 66.34 per cent YtD to close at N850 per share from N511 per share.

In recent months, the Nigerian stock market has witnessed positive momentum as investors reacted to favourable developments at home and abroad.

In October 2026, the market gained N2.01 trillion, crossing the N165 trillion mark for the first time amid investors’ demand for highly capitalised stocks quoted on the bourse and impressive nine-month earnings ended September 30, 2026, by listed manufacturing companies, among other factors.

Following its return to FTSE Russell in September 2026, the stock market gained N5.37 trillion, or 3.4 per cent Month-on-Month (MoM), to close at N163.104 trillion from N157.739 trillion at the end of August 2026.

Nigeria, on September 21, 2026, returned to Frontier Market status after a three-year absence from the global index provider’s classification. Developments in the foreign exchange market and T+1 settlement, among others, have contributed to a surge in Nigeria’s capital importation amid improved stability.

The market in September 2026 also saw the N2.1 trillion Initial Public Offer (IPO) of Dangote Refinery.

Commenting on the stock market’s performance in the first 10 months of 2026, the Managing Director of AVA Securities Ltd, Ms. Adejoke Ganiyu, said: “Monetary policy remains a key driver of market performance as investors seek higher-returning assets. The previous cycle, marked by foreign exchange management, high interest rates and elevated inflation, largely favoured banks.

“The current environment signals stability: a steadier foreign exchange market, moderating inflation and a cumulative 350 basis point cut in the MPR to 23 per cent. This is already visible in fixed income, with Nigerian Treasury Bill (NTB) yields down to about 18 per cent.

“As money market yields adjust to the lower-rate environment, we expect a sector rotation. Consumer goods and consumer discretionary stocks are posting strong numbers so far, as the cycle now works in their favour. Barring names with an already high base, we expect further gains from this segment.”

On the outlook, she added: “Overall, lower NTB yields and the MPR cut should continue to support the equities market over the remaining two months of 2026, as capital rotates from fixed income into equities, particularly consumer goods.”

World.title: Rev360: Reimagining Tax Administration for a Digital Nigeria
World.content:
By Emmanuel Jonathan

For many taxpayers, the true measure of an effective tax system is not the complexity of its laws or the sophistication of its technology, but a much simpler question: how easy is it to comply?

This question is central to the Nigeria Revenue Service’s (NRS) ongoing transformation of tax administration through Rev360, its next-generation digital tax administration platform.

Since its go-live on 30th April, 2026, Rev360 has marked an important milestone in the Service’s transition towards a more integrated, intelligent and taxpayer-centric system.
