Building on previous advances in digital tax administration, the platform is designed to simplify compliance, improve service delivery, strengthen transparency and support more efficient revenue administration.

As implementation progresses, attention is increasingly shifting from the introduction of the platform to its adoption, operational effectiveness and the tangible improvements it delivers for taxpayers and other stakeholders.

More Than a Digital Platform

Rev360 comprises an interconnected digital architecture designed to serve different participants in the tax ecosystem.

The Unified Revenue Collections Workspace (URCW) is the internal workspace for NRS personnel. It provides staff with a digital environment for administering revenue and managing taxpayer-related processes and information.

The Taxpayer Self-Service Portal (TSSP) is the principal digital channel for taxpayers. It enables taxpayers to access tax services and interact with the NRS without depending entirely on physical offices and manual paperwork. Through the TSSP, taxpayers can undertake key compliance activities and access relevant services digitally.

The Tax Consultants’ Portal (TCP) provides a dedicated channel for tax consultants and professionals who assist taxpayers with their obligations. It gives them a structured digital interface through which they can support their clients.

The Government Tax Portal (GTP) is designed for Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs), extending the digital tax environment into government institutions and supporting their interaction with tax administration.

The Developers’ Portal provides a connection point for third-party software developers and supports interoperability between external technology solutions and the wider Rev360 ecosystem.

The significance of these channels lies not merely in the existence of separate portals, but in their connection within a broader digital tax administration environment. Taxpayers, tax professionals, government institutions, NRS personnel and technology developers can therefore engage with the Service through channels designed around their respective roles.

What Rev360 Means for Taxpayers

For taxpayers, however, the technology behind Rev360 matters less than the experience it creates.

The important questions are practical: Can a taxpayer register more easily? Can returns be filed without unnecessary complications? Can payments be made conveniently? Can compliance issues be resolved more efficiently? Can taxpayers obtain assistance without repeated visits to tax offices?

The TSSP is particularly significant because it creates a direct digital channel between taxpayers and the NRS, providing access to services such as tax filing, payments, tax clearance, assessments and other taxpayer services.

The Tax ID also plays an important role in the wider digital tax administration framework by providing a basis for identifying taxpayers and supporting access to tax services. However, the Tax ID framework should be distinguished from Rev360 itself. The NRS Tax ID service states that the Tax ID is jointly issued by the NRS and the Joint Revenue Board in accordance with Nigerian tax laws.

For businesses, predictable processes and easier access to tax services can reduce the administrative burden associated with compliance.

The objective, therefore, is not simply to digitise existing procedures but to make the overall experience of dealing with the tax authority more convenient, accessible and predictable.

From Implementation to Adoption

Since its introduction, Rev360 has progressed through a phased implementation process designed to support an orderly transition for taxpayers and other stakeholders.

Beyond the deployment of technology, the NRS has prioritised stakeholder sensitisation, user training, technical support and continuous engagement to facilitate adoption and address implementation challenges.

The early implementation period is naturally one of adjustment. Taxpayers, professionals, government institutions and NRS personnel have to become familiar with the digital environment and adapt to processes that may differ from previous ways of working.

The success of Rev360 will ultimately be determined by measurable improvements in taxpayer experience, service reliability, processing efficiency, accessibility and voluntary compliance.

As implementation progresses, user feedback and operational performance data will remain essential to identifying opportunities for improvement and ensuring that the platform delivers on its objectives.

Turning Data into an Advantage

Another important dimension of digital tax administration is data.

Tax administration generates enormous amounts of information. When that information exists in disconnected systems, its usefulness can be limited. When appropriately integrated, it can provide a clearer picture of taxpayer behaviour, compliance patterns and revenue trends.

Rev360’s digital architecture is intended to support greater integration of tax administration processes and information. Such integration can help reduce duplication, improve coordination and strengthen the Service’s ability to use data in administering tax obligations.

The potential benefits extend beyond revenue collection. Reliable tax data can support economic planning and policy decisions by providing government with a stronger evidence base on economic activity.

This makes the digital transformation of tax administration relevant not only to taxpayers and the revenue authority but also to the wider economy.

Connecting to Global Tax Practice

Rev360 is being implemented at a time when tax administration globally is becoming increasingly digital.

Businesses increasingly operate across borders, while tax authorities are relying more heavily on digitalisation, data integration, transparency and information exchange.

Nigeria therefore needs a tax administration capable of operating effectively within this changing international environment.

A modern digital tax ecosystem can improve domestic administration while strengthening the country’s capacity to respond to developments in international taxation and cross-border economic activity.

Rev360 consequently represents an important stage in Nigeria’s continuing transition towards a more connected and digitally enabled tax administration.

Adoption Will Determine Success

Technology alone cannot guarantee transformation.

Nigeria’s taxpayer population is diverse, ranging from large corporations to medium-sized businesses, entrepreneurs, professionals and individual taxpayers. Their levels of digital literacy, access to technology and familiarity with tax processes vary.

This makes communication, taxpayer education and user support essential to the success of Rev360.

Users need clear information about which channel applies to them, what services they can access, how to use those services and where to obtain assistance when problems arise.

The success of digital tax administration will therefore depend not only on the technology itself but also on the ability of taxpayers and other stakeholders to understand, trust and effectively use the system.

As implementation continues, sustained engagement, responsive support and attention to user feedback will be critical to ensuring that the benefits of digitalisation are experienced across different categories of taxpayers and stakeholders.

The Real Measure of Transformation

The significance of Rev360 extends beyond the tax office.

Nigeria needs stronger domestic revenue to finance infrastructure, public services and development. At the same time, businesses need a tax environment that provides greater certainty, accessibility and predictability.

A more efficient digital tax administration can contribute to both objectives by making compliance easier for taxpayers while providing the revenue authority with more effective tools for administering the tax system.

The transformation of the NRS under the leadership of Executive Chairman Dr Zacch Adedeji reflects a broader effort to reposition tax administration around technology, data, efficiency and improved taxpayer experience.

But the real measure of that transformation will not be the sophistication of the technology or simply the number of digital channels created.

It will be whether taxpayers experience a meaningful difference.

Can taxpayers register and access services more easily? Can businesses file and pay with fewer complications? Can tax consultants manage their clients more efficiently? Can government institutions interact more effectively with the tax authority? Can NRS personnel work with better-integrated information? And can the Service use reliable data to improve compliance and revenue administration?

These are the questions that will increasingly define the success of Rev360.

Nigeria is moving from a tax administration shaped largely by physical processes towards one increasingly built around digital connectivity, integrated information and self-service.

Rev360 provides an important architecture for that transition.

Its ultimate achievement, however, will not be measured by technology alone. It will be measured by whether taxation becomes simpler for taxpayers, more efficient for government, more transparent for stakeholders and more predictable for the Nigerian economy.

*Emmanuel Jonathan, a Communications Expert and Manager with the Nigeria Revenue Service, writes from Abuja.

World.title: North West farmer Donovan Marx: Ears could NOT be saved
World.content:
Donovan Marx's ears could not be surgically saved after his farm attack on Wednesday. Images via X

The family of Donovan Marx have provided a disheartening update on his medical recovery – his ears that were chopped off in a farm attack could not be surgically saved.

The North West farmer has made international headlines after he was stabbed, shot at and tortured by three armed suspects who escaped in his red van on Wednesday, 28 October.

They remain at large. A reward of R200 000 for information leading to their arrest and conviction has been offered.



NORTH WEST FARMER: EARS CANNOT BE SURGICALLY SAVED

On Saturday, Ian Cameron, the Chairperson of Parliament’s Portfolio Committee on Police, shared an update on Donovan Marx’s injuries.

The North West farmer was attacked on his property in Syferfontein on Wednesday morning by three armed men.

According to Cameron, Donovan’s wife, Louise shared that he was receiving medical treatment at Mediclinic Potchefstroom.



While he is stable, his injuries remain serious – with confirmation that his ears, which were chopped off during the attack, could not be surgically saved.

The family has denied rumours that Donovan was castrated by his attackers.

They have confirmed the following injuries:

Donovan Marx was shot in the back, with the bullet passing through a kidney.

An injury to his colon required part of it to be surgically removed.

He was also stabbed in the leg.

Cameron added that the family appealed for privacy and for the public not to interfere in the investigation.



He shared: “The SAPS investigation is at a sensitive stage and has expressed full confidence that it is being handled seriously and thoroughly.

“They have asked people to stop publicly discussing possible suspects, investigative leads and other details of the case. Please respect that request and allow investigators to do their work without unnecessary interference”

R200K REWARD

Meanwhile, a reward for information leading to the arrest and conviction of Donovan Marx’s attackers has been raised to R200 000.



The money was raised by fellow farmers in Potchestroom and Ventersdorp.

The community are also reportedly looking into establishing a BackaBuddy campaign to raise funds for Marx to undergo ear reconstruction surgery.

World.title: Ahmed-inspired Stormers see off Ulster
World.content:
An outstanding all-round performance by Yaqeen Ahmed lifted the Stormers to an ultimately commanding 33-7 win against Irish giants Ulster on a perfect Saturday afternoon in Cape Town.

On a day that could have gone horribly wrong for the Stormers , the Cape side overcame what looked like a first-half a self-destruction mission to clinch a four-try bonus-point victory that provisionally lifts them up to second in the URC standing (ahead of the Bulls, Leinster and Edinburgh).

To put this contest into perspective, the Stormers had the better of Ulster in almost every facers of the game as they exerted dominance across the board. Ahmed and Markus Muller, the two Stormers rookies who received Springbok call-ups earlier this week, had Ulster’s defence on the ropes with their running lines and line breaks. The duo’s exuberance of youth was on full display.



However, poor handling led to a number of squandered scoring opportunities inside the strike zone and before long, Ulster took the lead against the run of play. That said, it was a contest for about 30 minutes before the Stormers finally pulled themselves together. And from there it was one-way traffic until the end.

FIRST HALF RECAP: StoRMERS SERVE AS THEIR OWN WORSE ENEMIES

It would have been a nervous John Dobson watching from the coach’s box as his team failed to settle into rhythm. They produced the gain-line dominance, the line-breaks, the offloads, the territorial supremacy, the set-piece dominance, aerial ascendancy; they produced everything except the finishing touches.

By contrast, Ulster scored the opening try of the game at the first chance of asking. Sensing that – despite their supremacy – this match holds the potential to derail horribly, the Stormers came alive late in the first half.

In an action packed seven minutes before the interval, JD Schickerling crashed over from close quarters to draw the home side level on the scoreboard, the Stormers lost in-form winger Leolin Zas with what appears to be a serious knee-injury, and bagged a fortuitous touchdown when Paul de Villiers’ was on hand to charge down and score from an Ulster clearance kick inside the 22.

SECOND HALF RECAP: ULSTER HAVE NO ANSWER FOR THE CAPE TIDE

The second stanza was equal parts sluggish and outstanding. Defensively the Stormers were at their very best, repelling multiple attempts on their own tryline. And in attack, they were dazzling at times and infuriatingly erratic at others.

When Ahmed pounced on a loose ball and transferred possession to his inside man Cobus Reinach, Evan Roos was on hand to take the final pass and scuttle downfield to score a runaway try.



That was in the 46th minute. And from that moment, there was to be no more points scored until the last 10 minutes of the game. With the scoreboard at 19-7 and the game still very much handing in the balance, Ahmed showed a level of maturity beyond his years and experience as he took control of the game.

With Ulster’s defence stubbornly denying the Stormers close to the tryline, the 20-year-old executed a perfect kick-pass for captain Ruhan Nel to latch onto and score in the right hand corner; before fighting his way through numerous would-tacklers for a self-converted touchdown to wrapped up the game and the result for the Stormers.

World.title: Weather: Brace for severe thunderstorms across most of KZN
World.content:
SAWS warns of severe thunderstorms across most of KwaZulu-Natal. Image: Pexels

Here is what the weather has in store for KZN, the Free State, and the North West on Sunday 1 November 2026.

SAWS has issued a Yellow Level 4 warning for severe thunderstorms across most of KwaZulu-Natal, except the north-east.

Heavy downpours, hail and excessive lightning could cause damage to settlements and infrastructure.



Extremely high fire danger conditions are expected in the western parts of the Free State and North West.

KWAZULU-NATAL

Morning fog over the south-eastern interior, otherwise partly cloudy and warm to hot, but very hot in places in the north.

It will become cloudy in the afternoon with scattered showers and thundershowers, but isolated in the north-east.



Moderate to fresh northerly to north-easterly winds will blow along the coast at first.

The winds will shift to southerly to south-westerly from the south by mid-morning, reaching Richards Bay in the afternoon.

The UVB sunburn will be moderate.

DURBAN

Durban is going to be partly cloudy, becoming cloudy in the afternoon with scattered showers and thundershowers.



Moderate north-easterly winds will blow at first, before shifting to moderate to fresh southerly to south-westerly winds.

Temperatures will range from 20°C to 27°C.

The UVB sunburn index will be moderate.

FREE STATE

Partly cloudy and warm with isolated showers and thundershowers.



BLOEMFONTEIN

Bloemfontein is going to be partly cloudy with isolated showers and thundershowers.

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 18°C to a maximum of 29°C.

NORTH WEST

North West is going to be partly cloudy and hot, with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers.



MAHIKENG

Mahikeng is going to be partly cloudy with isolated afternoon showers and thundershowers.

Temperatures will range from a minimum of 19°C. to a maximum of 35°C.

Weather forecast data provided by the South African Weather Service.

World.title: Four spotted gully sharks released back into the wild
World.content:
Four spotted gully sharks in the care of Cape Town’s Two Oceans Aquarium have returned to the sea.

According to the aquarium, the sharks – consisting of three males and one female – were released into the ocean at Mgwalana in the Eastern Cape on 19 October 2026.

STORY OF THE SHARKS

Spotted gully sharks are currently classified as “Near Threatened”, as per the IUCN’s Red List of Threatened Species. They are vulnerable to overfishing, habitat destruction and pollution, among other threats.



The four aforementioned marine animals were housed within the Two Oceans Aquarium’s Kelp Forest Exhibit. Here, they served as ambassadors for their endangered species for several years.

Now, after outgrowing the space, it was time for these endemic marine animals to return to their natural habitat.

BACK TO SEA

With the aid of the aquarium’s Curatorial and Collections team, the sharks were transported from Cape Town to the Eastern Cape. They were transported in an oxygenated chamber.

First, the team found a calm spot with warm water along the beach in Mgwalana. Then, the sharks were stretchered one-by-one into the surf. Each one was given a moment to acclimate to the ocean temperature before the team released the stretcher’s straps.

Kevin Spiby, Curator of Operations and Animal Husbandry at the Two Oceans Aquarium, explains how these sharks naturally took to the seawater:

Each of the sharks swam off into the ocean strongly and confidently. Gully sharks display no parental care, so their natural instincts are hardwired into them from birth. This allows them to adjust easily back to life in the ocean after a period at the Aquarium. 

SHARK TRACKING

While parting is such sweet sorrow, the aquarium is still able to keep an eye on their charges from afar:

All four sharks were fitted with acoustic tags that will allow us to track their movements along the coastline, marking another important contribution to our ongoing research on spotted gully sharks along the southern African coastline.

While it’s too soon to say how these sharks are faring nearly two weeks after their release, we’re certain that it won’t be long before their tags start transmitting valuable data.

In related news, the Two Oceans Aquarium released Blue, the ragged-tooth shark, into the ocean off Struisbaai back in March. Much like her spotted gully brethren, Blue’s species is also under severe threat and is currently classified as endangered.

World.title: Severe thunderstorms could disrupt power supplies in Mpumalanga on Sunday
World.content:
SAWS warns of severe thunderstorms in south-eastern Mpumalanga on Sunday. Image: AI illustration

Residents in parts of Mpumalanga could face power cuts and communication disruptions on Sunday, as severe thunderstorms threaten the south-eastern parts of the province.

The South African Weather Service (SAWS) has issued a Yellow Level 2 warning for severe thunderstorms from 15:00 until 23:59 on Sunday.

The weather service expects thunderstorms across large parts of Mpumalanga, but warns that some could become severe in the extreme south-east.



Which areas face the severe thunderstorms warning?

SAWS has highlighted the extreme south-eastern parts of Mpumalanga as the areas at risk of severe storms.

Although thunderstorms could develop across much of the province, not every area will experience severe conditions.

Residents in the affected areas should prepare for possible damage to property and interruptions to essential services.

Severe thunderstorms could disrupt electricity supplies and communication networks in affected communities.

Strong winds and lightning can damage electricity infrastructure, while falling trees and branches can bring down power lines.

SAWS warns that the storms could cause short-term disruptions to essential services, including electricity, communication, healthcare and education.



However, the warning does not mean that power cuts will definitely occur.

What damage could the thunderstorms cause?

SAWS warns that severe storms could damage homes, buildings, vehicles and other property.

The storms could also affect informal settlements, infrastructure, livestock and people’s livelihoods.

Residents should secure loose outdoor items and avoid unnecessary travel during severe weather, particularly when visibility drops or roads become flooded.

When will the warning end?

The Yellow Level 2 warning will remain in place from 15:00 until 23:59 on Sunday, 1 November.

Residents should keep checking SAWS forecasts and warnings for updates, as weather conditions can change.

Anyone who encounters a fallen electricity line should stay away from it and report it to the relevant electricity provider or municipality.

World.title: Proteas beat Australia at Newlands to win Test series 2-1
World.content:
Simon Harmer and Ryan Rickelton star as the Proteas win the third Test against Australia. Image: Proteas Men CSA (X).

South Africa has won the third Test against Australia after dominating with the bat and ball.

The home team surged on days 4 and 5 to claim crucial points in the World Test Championship.

Here’s how the Test unfolded day by day as the Proteas beat Australia at Newlands on 31 October.



How THE THIRD TEST UNFOLDED

Day 1

South Africa started on the front foot with Aiden Markram and Marques Ackerman.

They put on 158 runs for the opening partnership, with Ackerman falling just short of a debut century.

David Bedingham contributed a handy 50, but things soon went downhill, according to ESPN Cricinfo.

Apart from Ryan Rickelton’s 42 and Marco Jansen’s 52, no other Proteas batsman reached double figures.

South Africa were eventually bowled out for 329 at the close of the first day.

Mitchell Starc gave a reminder of his fearsome bowling with a six-wicket haul, conceding just 72.



Day 2

In reply, Australia lost Travis Head and Marnus Labuschagne early in their first innings.

Matt Renshaw and Cameron Green stabilised the innings with a superb 126-run partnership.

The responsibility then fell to John Inglis and Alex Carey, who were unbeaten at the close of play.

Australia ended their day on 330/4, having just taken the lead.

Simon Harmer and Jansen did the damage with the ball, taking 2 wickets apiece.

Day 3

Inglis was dismissed early in the day as Harmer found grip and turn in the pitch.

Carey fell a few overs later, and the rest of the batting lineup was soon to follow.

As the Proteas bowlers began firing, Australia were eventually bowled out for 429.

Harmer was the pick of the bowling attack with 4 important wickets.

South Africa then returned to the batting crease, chasing down a 100-run deficit.

Things took a turn in the final session, as Starc dismissed Markram and Ackerman.

Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon also got in on the action with 1 wicket each.

The Proteas ended on 140/4, with Matthew Breetzke and Rickelton needing to survive.

350 Test Wickets For Rabada! 😤



Another monumental milestone for one of South Africa’s finest! 🇿🇦



Kagiso Rabada reaches the incredible 350-wicket mark in Test cricket, further cementing his place among the very best to wear the badge! 👑



A relentless competitor, a world-class… pic.twitter.com/zf1ZDOHngQ — Proteas Men (@ProteasMenCSA) October 31, 2026

Day 4

The Proteas managed to steady the ship despite losing Breetzke for 43.

Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder rooted themselves at the crease for most of the day.

Their partnership contributed 154 vital runs to keep South Africa in the hunt.

Rickelton was eventually run out for 101, with the lower order looking to swing for the fences.

Jansen fell for a duck, and Harmer and Gerald Coetzee contributed 1 run each.

The Proteas were eventually all out for 387, with Mulder’s 115 the top score.

Australia were then left to start the last day fresh, needing 288 to win.

Day 5

With the series at stake, Rabada tore into the Australian top order.

He returned to form by dismissing Head, Renshaw, and Labuschagne within the first 7 overs.

Cameron Green’s promising 27 ended when Harmer beat him with flight and turn.

Wickets continued falling rapidly as South Africa turned up the pressure.

Cummins and Lyon were eventually left at the crease, with their country on 63 for 8.

The Australian skipper hung around for 90 balls, but the writing was on the wall.

Lyon fell a few deliveries later to seal a 176-run win for South Africa.

The Proteas have also closed the gap on Australia and New Zealand in the WTC table.

SINCE THE PROTEAS BEAT AUSTRALIA, WILL THESE TEAMS PLAY IN THE WORLD TEST CHAMPIONSHIP FINAL?

World.title: NOW OPEN: Inside Cape Town’s ‘ugly’ luxury waterfront hotel, and its nightly rates
World.content:
Among the hotel's five restaurants and bars is a rooftop restaurant alongside a heated swimming pool. Image: EDITION

Cape Town’s newest luxury hotel is now open, bringing 142 rooms and suites to the V&A Waterfront. However, its appearance has already divided opinion.

The Cape Town Edition is located at Quay 7, overlooking the Waterfront’s new superyacht marina, with views of Table Mountain.

The hotel’s arrival marks the African debut of the international Edition Hotels brand. Its portfolio includes properties in London, New York, Tokyo and Barcelona.



Unfortunately for the brand, the building attracted the wrong kind of attention long before welcoming its first guests.

The architecture references warehouse structures that previously occupied the location. Image: EDITION/ Facebook

Images shared during the construction phase sparked debate, with critics describing its concrete-heavy exterior as overly Brutalist.

Some commentators called the “Soviet-style architecture” an eyesore on the Mother City’s skyline, while some likened the design to that of a “prison.”



Local shock jock Gareth Cliff was also far from impressed when the first images of the waterfront hotel went live, calling the building “ugly.”

Why is almost everything built since 1920 so purposefully designed to be ugly? Why did the postmodernists influence architects so easily. The match of form and function is such a glorious thing when achieved with beauty as a virtue for its own sake… https://t.co/N3qJsD6Efp — Gareth Cliff (@GarethCliff) August 9, 2026

The inspiration behind the design

Designed by Shanghai-based architectural firm Neri&Hu, in collaboration with Cape Town-based architects, the Cape Town Edition hotel draws inspiration from the site’s industrial maritime history.



“Its architecture references the warehouse structures that previously occupied the location, with a long, low-slung form, pitched rooflines and materials inspired by the working harbour,” writes BizCommunity.

Over six million bricks were hand-laid in varying patterns to give the building its distinctive textured façade.

A look inside Cape Town’s new waterfront hotel

The property features 142 guestrooms and suites. Its largest accommodation options are the 240-square-metre Penthouse and the 112-square-metre Harbour Suite.



The hotel also has five restaurants and bars, led by executive chef Phil Carmichael.

These include Shale, its signature restaurant, and Eave, a rooftop restaurant and bar alongside a heated swimming pool.

Other facilities include a spa below sea level, a 24-hour gym, a ballroom and several meeting spaces.



The hotel also features The Drum, a cylindrical open-air space with a spiral staircase leading to a viewing platform overlooking the harbour, Table Mountain and the Atlantic Ocean.

What does it cost to stay?

A night at the new luxury Cape Town Edition comes with quite a hefty price tag.

The average rate per night for the cheapest rooms, based on November 2026 availability, is roughly R17 000. That’s for two guests, with breakfast excluded.



Prices climb considerably over the festive season. Rates during the Christmas week were listed from around R28 000 per night.

World.title: Parts of Cape Town face a 12-hour water outage on Tuesday
World.content:
The City of Cape Town will shut off the water supply to parts of Steenberg and Fish Hoek for 12 hours on Tuesday, 3 November.

The City’s Water and Sanitation Directorate will carry out the work from 8:00 to 20:00 in both areas. These are the longest planned outages on the City’s maintenance schedule for the week of 2 to 6 November.

Residents in the affected areas will have no water during this period.



Why the water will be off in Steenberg and Fish Hoek

In Steenberg, the maintenance team will switch over to temporary water supply bypasses along Uithof Street (between Main Road and Easson Road), Frogmore Road (between Cul-de-Sac and Easson Road) and Lake Road (between Main Road and Frogmore Road).

In Fish Hoek, the outage will affect Kinross Crescent, 17th Avenue, Paris Road, Nelson Road, Kommetjie Main Road and possibly surrounding streets. The team will switch over to temporary bypasses along 17th Avenue and portions of Kinross Crescent and Paris Road.

The city has not listed water tankers for either area, so residents should store enough water before the work begins.

The city also warns that maintenance work can prove more complex than anticipated, which could push repairs beyond the scheduled times.

Other water outages in Cape Town this week

Several other areas will also go without water this week:

Kommetjie (Wireless Road): Tuesday, 8:00 to 19:00

Ottery: Tuesday, 9:00 to 19:30

Kleinvlei, Spandau, Perm Gardens, Forest Glade, Forest Heights, Park Village, Somerset Heights and Rosedale: Tuesday, 9:00 to 19:00

Gordon’s Bay: Monday, 9:00 to 19:00

Brackenfell Heights, Springbok Park and Brackenfell Central: Thursday, 9:00 to 18:00

Kuils River: Monday, 9:00 to 16:00

Zero-pressure tests may also cause low pressure or no water in Kalkfontein, Oude Westhof, Fairways, Parkwood, Helderrand, Erinvale Residential Estate, parts of Bellville South and low-lying areas of Khayelitsha on various days.



How to prepare for the water outage

The city advises residents to store enough water in clean, sealed containers for domestic use before the outage starts. Residents should also keep their taps closed to prevent water loss or damage when the supply returns.

Once the city restores the supply, the water may appear discoloured or milky for a short period due to trapped air in the pipes. If left to stand in a glass, it will clear.

World.title: Pogacar 'happy to be alive' after difficult Vuelta crash recovery
World.content:
PARIS - Tadej Pogacar has revealed he suffered three fractured vertebrae in the crash that ended his season, admitting he is "just happy to be alive" after scans uncovered the full extent of injuries that also left him battling concussion-related balance problems.

The Slovenian rider had initially been diagnosed with a fracture in his neck and a broken collarbone following his Vuelta a Espana accident, but a follow-up scan in his home country uncovered further damage.

"There's actually a funny story. Two weeks ago, I was in Slovenia and I went to do another CT scan. I knew I had a C7 fracture, but then we saw I had two more broken vertebrae, the T1 and T2," Pogacar told The Athletic in an interview published Saturday.

"At that moment, I was happy I didn't do the European Championships, which had been my initial goal. When I saw I had three broken vertebrae? I'm just happy to be alive, actually, or just to be standing."

The five-time Tour de France champion said he has now returned largely to normal life, although he remains cautious as he continues to heal.

"I don't have discomfort anymore," he said. "I have to be careful not to crash on the bike, or do some heavy lifting with my left arm or with my neck. But I can do basically everything normal now."

Pogacar said the first weeks after the accident were particularly difficult. A concussion left him struggling with dizziness, nausea and poor coordination, preventing him from resuming normal activities.

"I had to be showered with the help of the team doctor. I could not shower. I was getting dizzy as soon as I stood or when I put my head down. I was just completely out of it and it was so tough," he said.

- 'Really depressed' -

The 28-year-old underwent surgery but said recovery was slower and mentally tougher than he had expected.

"It took one hour and 40 minutes, a long time, and when I got out of anesthesia the doctor was trying to make some jokes, but I was not feeling it. I was really depressed after the surgery," said Pogacar.

"For the first two weeks, I was really mentally not OK. I was really down. I was not a fun person to be around."

Pogacar said his mood improved once he resumed rehabilitation and indoor training.

"When I started to get on the home trainer, to go to physio every day, then I started to feel better -- also in the head. But it was a day-to-day fight."

Although doctors classified the neck fracture as stable, Pogacar said its potential consequences remained sobering.

"But if I crash again on the bike now, it can be very problematic. Everybody says that I was lucky, and you're always lucky after a crash where you can walk away and you're fine.

"You see it's pretty serious and not to joke around. It's a bit scary, to be honest, to think about it."

World.title: South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs in third Test to win series
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - South Africa beat Australia by 176 runs and clinched a series victory when Australia were bowled out for 111 on the fifth day of the third Test at Newlands on Saturday.

Kagiso Rabada took two wickets in the first over and followed up with a third in a devastating opening spell which ripped out Australia's top three batsmen after they had started the day needing 288 to win.

Off-spinner Simon Harmer took a career-best six for 16 in 21.1 overs as South Africa completed their win shortly before tea.

Josh Inglis was run out to add to Australia's woes after Rabada's initial burst before Harmer took two wickets in three balls to plunge the tourists to 42 for six.

Australia were 60 for seven at lunch when Mitchell Starc was caught at short leg but in keeping with a series of multiple changes of fortune, South Africa were kept in the field for another two hours before completing their win.

South Africa, the defending World Test champions, were projected to depose Australia at the top of the International Cricket Council world Test rankings at the end of a series in which all three matches produced a result on the fifth day.

Travis Head scored a single off Rabada's second delivery but Matt Renshaw, Australia's most successful batsman in the series, was out first ball, glancing Rabada down the leg side to a diving wicketkeeper Ryan Rickelton.

Three balls later the out-of-form Marnus Labuschagne padded up to a ball which swung in sharply and was given out leg before wicket, with a review showing umpire's call on off stump.

Head fell to a reflex catch by Marco Jansen at gully as the left-hander flashed at Rabada and the South African players celebrated the demise of a batsman capable of playing a match-changing innings.

World.title: The Voting Booth | What coalition combinations will work for your metro?
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - On Sunday 1 November at 11 am, eNCA will reveal what party supporters truly want their own parties to go into coalition with.

Having polled a thousand people each in all six of the country’s major metros in the eNCA MarkData poll, we asked supporters of every party which parties they want their parties to work with and which parties they absolutely did not want their parties to go into coalition with.
