World.title: Poland: Protesters clash with police over sacked court chief
World.content:
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk defended the firing of top court President Bogdan Swieczkowski as a move to "restore the rule of law."

Protesters gathered outside Poland's Constitutional Court on Friday night, with authorities sending police to the scene to secure the court's grounds.

It all comes after a statement appeared on the top court's website saying President Bogdan Swieczkowski and his deputy had been suspended for one month. Fellow judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska will lead the institution during this period.

According to Warsaw police, officers responded to one judge who alerted them to possible threats to the safety of judges and staff.

Tusk vows to 'restore rule of law'

Swieczkowski is one of a slew of politically aligned judges who were appointed by the right-wing conservative Law and Justice Party (PiS), which governed Poland from 2015 to 2023.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk backed the move in a post on X.

"Restoring the rule of law is our duty," Tusk said.

"After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way," he added.

Officers responded to a judge who alerted them to possible threats to the safety of judges and staff Image: Wojtek Radwanski/AFP

When Tusk's center-left alliance took over after the 2023 parliamentary election, the group announced it would reverse controversial PiS government reforms in the judiciary.

Riot police deployed to court

Dozens of riot police were deployed to the court as followers of PiS protested against the ousting of Swieczkowski through the evening.

The court's official X social media account said there had been a "coup d'etat," with some chanting "Tusk traitor" as they condemned the step taken by the Tusk government.

Polish president cancels trip abroad

Right-wing Polish President Karol Nawrocki reacted to the situation by canceling a planned trip to Senegal.

"At a moment like this, the president must be in Poland," Nawrocki said.

Upon returning to Poland, he entered the Constitutional Court, making his way through the police barricade, his chief of staff said early on Saturday.

"President Karol Nawrocki, accompanied by the First President of the Supreme Court, Zbigniew Kapinski, entered the Constitutional Tribunal building," Pawel Szefernaker wrote on X.

In recent months, Nawrocki had refused to swear in five top court judges nominated by parliament.

When these judges instead took their oath before parliament, Swieczkowski had denied them access to the building.

World.title: Una cadena de fallos técnicos tumbó el sistema de seguridad ferroviaria LZB en Urda
World.content:
La ficha de la incidencia abierta por Adif a las 8.30 del miércoles, 23 minutos antes del siniestro, señala pérdidas de tensión, comunicaciones telefónicas caídas y “pérdida de información intermitente”. Posteriormente, la empresa pudo constatar que la comunicación con los maquinistas se mantuvo en pie

El sistema de registro de incidencias del gestor de la infraestructura ferroviaria Adif recoge una cadena de fallos técnicos en el área de Urda (Toledo) el miércoles día 28, a las 8.30 de la mañana, que desembocan en una serie de instrucciones inconexas a los maquinistas, por parte del centro de mando en Madrid-Atocha, y en el fatal accidente entre un AVE de Renfe y un tren de Iryo. La ficha abierta a esa hora por “avería en instalaciones de seguridad” entre las localidades toledanas de Mora y Orgaz toca al tramo que va del kilómetro 89,5 al 119,7 de la línea de alta velocidad Madrid-Sevilla. El siniestro ocurre en el 118. La descripción del fallo, según recoge el documento, es “Caída central LZB Urda”, lo que resume una cadena fatal de incidencias tecnológicas.

Adif tiene en ese punto una central con equipos (tres ordenadores) que dan servicio al sistema de seguridad alemán LZB, que comunica trenes e infraestructura, modula la velocidad de circulación e impide que los convoyes entren en riesgo de colisión. Cuando las órdenes de al menos dos de esos ordenadores al tren no coinciden, el LZB se desactiva. Como es sabido, por el relato del ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, esa caída del sistema de señalización motivó la parada de seis trenes, entre ellos los dos siniestrados. Pese a quedar inhábil, el escudo cumplió la misión final de frenar el tráfico sin que hubiera que lamentar hasta ese momento problema grave alguno.

En el texto de la ficha de Adif se puede leer: “Caída central LZB Urda, con fallos de transmisión generalizados Meta 40 y Meta 0”. A continuación, la empresa pública constata en este parte de incidencia que “se revisan LTV [limitación temporal de velocidad] del tramo, encontrándose todas señalizadas”. A partir de este punto, en el que la situación está bajo control pese a perderse la señal del sistema de seguridad, se añade que “tras sufrir fallo de velocidad Meta 0, se circula con BSL [sistema de señalización a través de balizas laterales] hasta recuperar transmisión fuera de la central”. Es decir, se espera que una vez rebasada la estación de Urda, los trenes puedan volver a guiarse por el sistema LZB.

“La incidencia coincide con fallos en las comunicaciones GSMR en el punto”, indica Adif en la ficha de las 8.30. El GSMR o Global System for Mobile Communications-Railway es el estándar internacional de comunicación inalámbrica diseñado específicamente para el sector ferroviario. Además de quedar inhábil el LZB, se describe el fallo en las comunicaciones y, además, “se produce pérdida de información intermitente momentánea en los circuitos de vía de Urda”. Tercer problema concatenado, al que se suma un cuarto: “Coincide con pérdida de tensión a la salida de la estación de Urda en ambas vías y ocupación CV237”. Los cuatro fallos concretan la pérdida del LZB.

Una revisión posterior del sistema, explica un portavoz oficial de Adif, aclara que “todas las comunicaciones entre el centro de control de Atocha y los maquinistas se realizaron sin problemas”. Aunque se incluyó la referencia al GSMR en la ficha de incidencia, conocida de puertas adentro como GIFO, “se ha verificado lo ocurrido y confirmado que el contacto entre Atocha y los maquinistas no falló y que en ningún caso tuvo una relación directa con el accidente”.

Hasta ese punto en crisis de la línea Madrid-Sevilla llegó en torno a las 8.35 un equipo de mantenimiento de Adif para intentar levantar el sistema LZB, del que dos ordenadores iban a permanecer bloqueados hasta el momento de la colisión, a las 8.53 horas. Se intentó incluso rearmar el sistema usando un solo ordenador, pero tampoco fue posible. La investigación policial y técnica deben verificar ahora el estado de los equipos, a los que se prohibió el acceso a la empresa encargada del mantenimiento, Hitachi Rail, en cuanto el caso cayó en manos del juzgado de instrucción de Orgaz.

Mientras el personal de Adif atendía esta incidencia, de las que el ministro Puente relató ayer en rueda de prensa que se han dado en lo que va de año 170 de distinta naturaleza que han tumbado al LZB en la misma línea de alta velocidad (dijo que el 75% por causas ajenas a Adif), un tren de Iryo queda paralizado ante la estación de Urda y pese a dos intentos de la maquinista, le es imposible reiniciar el sistema LZB y continuar la marcha. Todo ello es comunicado a las 8.41 y 8.48 por la conductora al centro de control de Adif en Madrid-Atocha. Desde 25 kilómetros detrás sí avanza un AVE de Renfe, con amparo del sistema de seguridad BSL y con orden de marcha normal. Durante 17 minutos de trayecto alcanza hasta 200 kilómetros por hora sin que su conductor supiera en ningún momento que encontraría un obstáculo en la vía, el tren de Iryo. El choque que deja un balance de 69 víctimas mortales, se produce a las 8.53. La Autoridad Independiente para la Investigación Técnica de Accidentes (AITAT) estima en un primer informe que el AVE alcanzó a la unidad de Iryo a una velocidad de 160 a 200 kilómetros por hora.

El ministro Puente reconoció el miércoles, y reiteró ayer, que el control de la circulación de Adif “tuvo tiempo para evitar la tragedia”. Esa compañía pública depende de su ministerio. También concedió que se aplicó erróneamente el protocolo de circulaciones en caso de caída del LZB y la existencia de obstáculos en la vía. Pese a la orden de reanudación de la marcha que recibió el AVE de Renfe, la velocidad de avance nunca debió rebasar los 40 kilómetros por hora, lo que en el argot ferroviario se conoce como marcha a la vista.

En descarga de cualquier dificultad que pudiera haber tenido la unidad de Iryo para proseguir su viaje hacia Sevilla, Puente afirmó que el tren que tenía detrás nunca debía haber sido liberado hasta que el primero hubiera recuperado la marcha.

World.title: Cómo un buen café puede cambiar un negocio hostelero
World.content:
Entre el café de batalla y la fiebre por su refinación, cada vez más hosteleros abandonan los automatismos a la hora de preparar esta bebida para formarse en su preparación. Un ejemplo es la cafetería Formentor, en Madrid. Tras 70 años en activo, ha transformado su servicio con la ayuda de un experto cafetero

¿Por dónde empieza un buen café? ¿Por los ingredientes, por la forma de prepararlo, por la exigencia del cliente? “El primer paso es convencer a los hosteleros de que cambien su forma de prepararlo”, responde Raúl Villanueva, barista y formador de la marca Café Saula. Él, con dos décadas de experiencia en el sector hostelero, reconoce que deshacerse de las manías y automatismos puede ser complicado. Villanueva forma parte del equipo de seis formadores de Saula, la marca premium de café de Grupo Pascual, que recorren distintos locales del país para enseñar a los hosteleros a servir una bebida equilibrada, rica y estable; para que todas las tazas de café que sirvan tengan la misma calidad. “La resistencia al cambio impide sacar el máximo provecho del producto”, reflexiona. “La idea es culturizar a nuestros alumnos para que entiendan el café y sepan tratarlo mejor. Esto beneficia a todos: a nosotros como marca, a ellos como negocio y a su cliente final”, sostiene.

La cultura del café ha crecido, insiste el experto. Percibe que los consumidores también se preocupan más por lo que consumen. Han pasado a interesarse por el origen, la calidad y la elaboración. A este fenómeno lo impulsa, además, el factor económico. “La diferencia de precios entre un café de alta calidad y otro normalito es ridícula”, añade el barista.

Raúl Villanueva, barista y formador de la marca Café Saula. Cedida por Saula

Villanueva atribuye el cambio de paradigma a la profesionalización del sector y a la labor pedagógica de tostadores, baristas y marcas. Después de cuatro años trabajando para Saula, aún encuentra nudos en los negocios. Cada vez son menos, pero todavía hay algunas personas que ven el café como un producto secundario, tienen poco interés por aprender nuevas técnicas y “no cuidan la receta”. Ni siquiera la prueban. “Preparar un café es un cocinar”, insiste. “Cualquier cambio en molienda, dosis, temperatura, agua o tiempo altera el resultado final”. Por eso, en sus cursos aborda desde la materia prima hasta el funcionamiento de la maquinaria o la texturización de leche.

Los cinco errores cafeteros más comunes del hostelero Según Raúl Villanueva, barista y formador de la marca 'premium' Café Saula Utilizar café viejo Los granos molidos pierden aroma, cuerpo y sabor a medida que se oxidan. Un mal control del 'stock' puede mermar la calidad.

Priorizar la rapidez sobre la calidad La premura puede llevar a desatender la atención a los detalles que marcan la diferencia.

No cuidar correctamente la máquina La acumulación de restos de café y suciedad afecta a la presión y la temperatura de extracción, esenciales para el buen sabor.

No considerarlo una receta (y no probarlo) Muchos hosteleros controlan cocina, vino o cerveza, pero olvidan beber el café que venden. Es un error pensar que basta con pulsar un botón; la preparación depende de múltiples variables.

No formar al equipo Si cada empleado elabora el café de una manera distinta, repercute en la experiencia del cliente. Se vuelve inconsistente.

La calidad acaba por imponerse

La pastelería Formentor abrió sus puertas en Madrid hace 70 años, cuando un matrimonio que regentaba en Mallorca un local llamado el Forn de Santa Eulàlia decidió traer a la capital española el sabor de las ensaimadas. Eran los abuelos de Ane Forteza (San Sebastián, 31 años), que hoy, como tercera generación, está al frente del negocio. “Algunos clientes que nos visitaban junto a sus abuelos llegan ahora acompañados de sus nietos”, se enorgullece.

Tienen dos locales, uno en Chamberí y otro acristalado en el barrio de Salamanca, desde donde Forteza recuerda que cambiar su marca de café fue una difícil decisión. “Muchos nos decían que venían porque les gustaba el sabor”, admite. La mayoría de habituales lo desayunan acompañado de una ensaimada ―las lisas, sin relleno, se hornean continuamente en el local―. A pesar de todo, el pasado julio decidieron dar el paso. “Fue una evolución natural. Somos una empresa que intenta dar productos de la mejor calidad y pensamos que el café tenía que ser acorde”.

De entre todas las marcas, se quedaron con Saula por la formación presencial, el seguimiento constante, la facilidad a la hora de pedir el café (junto a su pedido de leche Pascual), la sustitución de la maquinaria y el esmero en los detalles. La respuesta de los consumidores, al final, ha sido mayoritariamente positiva: “Algunos notaron que era un café más suave y menos tostado”. Tampoco les preocupa los que aún no se adaptan: “Es una cuestión de hábito, la calidad acaba por imponerse”.

Ane Forteza representa la tercera generación al frente de la Pastelería Formentor, fundada por sus abuelos en Madrid. INMA FLORES

Al otro lado de la barra, Andrés Vidarte (Tesalia, Colombia, 30 años) se encarga de servir los cafés con una sonrisa extensa ante unos clientes exigentes que ya le conocen y saludan. Él, que cumple con precisión lo aprendido en las formaciones de Saula, reconoce que algunas pautas le sorprendieron, como la colocación de las tazas (boca arriba, para que se caliente la base y no el borde, donde se apoyan los labios), la cantidad de agua que había que utilizar o la importancia de una limpieza minuciosa y frecuente. “Aprendimos que cualquier resto puede influir en el sabor del café”, señala. El barista, que nació en una zona cafetera de Colombia, dice que la aportación de Saula le ayudó a ser más consciente de todo el ritual de preparación: “Ahora prestamos más atención a aspectos que antes pasaban desapercibidos”, admite.

Los cuatro pasos para servir un buen café Por Andrés Vidarte, barista de la cafetería Formentor (Madrid) 1 Limpiar bien la maquinaria entre servicio; sobre todo, el portafiltros. Además, realizar purgas diarias y lavados profundos periódicos.

2 Controlar la receta con la ayuda de dos máquinas. La primera tiene programada la dosis exacta de café y la segunda, el tiempo de extracción (que suele ser de unos 25 segundos) y la cantidad de bebida que debe salir.

3 Comprobar la temperatura y la presión. La cafetera debe alcanzar y mantener una temperatura estable, que marque aproximadamente 116 ºC, para que se extraigan los aromas y sabores.

4 Finalmente, trabajar la leche (si la lleva), calentar media jarra e introducir la lanza de vapor solo parcialmente para texturizarla (transformarla en una crema suave). Después, girar levemente la taza para una integración proporcionada. FOTOGRAFÍA: Inma Flores

Tueste lento y conservación en lata

Desde sus inicios a finales de los 50 en Cataluña, la filosofía de Saula se basaba en la obsesión por mantener la calidad del producto y del proceso. Lo define Javier Peña, director general de Café del Grupo Pascual, quien precisa que entonces la mayor parte del mercado estaba orientada hacia cafés más amargos y con mayor cuerpo, elaborados principalmente con variedades robustas. “El fundador de esta marca, Lluís Saula, detectó una oportunidad para ofrecer un café de mayor calidad: el café arábica, que es más aromático, complejo y delicado”, añade.

Para alcanzarlo, elaboran una selección muy rigurosa desde el origen, la altura de cultivo, el tamaño o el procesamiento. Peña compara el café con una cereza: “Una vez recolectado, es necesario separar correctamente la pulpa exterior para evitar que la fermentación no controlada afecte al grano”. Su tueste es lento y controlado y permite desarrollar notas achocolatadas y especiadas. La conservación se realiza en lata, con una maduración de tres o cuatro semanas antes de salir al mercado. “Los envases incorporan válvulas unidireccionales que permiten la salida de los gases sin que entre oxígeno, para evitar la oxidación”, expone.

Pascual adquirió hace un par de años Café Saula porque “estaban en sintonía”; ambas se esmeran en un cuidado “extremo”, define Peña. El propósito era expandir este café; a comienzos de 2026 llegó a Madrid y desde este verano a Galicia, Asturias y Cantabria. Peña explica que el crecimiento de esta área dentro de Pascual ha sido significativo en los últimos años: “El objetivo era alcanzar 100 millones de euros en café en 2027, pero podría lograrse antes. En unos siete años se ha duplicado el valor del negocio del café dentro del grupo”. En la actualidad, esta vertical supera los 300 empleados, de los cuales 80 están dentro de Saula.

Javier Peña, director general de Café del Grupo Pascual. Cedida por Saula

Quieren desplegarse, pero con conciencia; sin perder sus estándares de calidad. “Solo trabajamos con establecimientos que se comprometan a tratar bien el producto”, apunta Peña, y pone el ejemplo de Formentor: “Cuando entras, ya se percibe. El olor a pastelería y a un buen café te enganchan”. Por ello, Saula cuida permanentemente de que los empleados estén actualizados en conocimientos, gracias a Raúl Villanueva y otros seis preparadores.

Estos expertos encuentran indicadores inmediatos para saber si el café es de calidad. Por ejemplo, Villanueva lo hace a través de tres sentidos. Por la vista, al observar el color de la crema, la cantidad, la uniformidad: “Las figuras en la leche no garantizan que el café sea bueno, pero sí refuerzan la experiencia”, incide. Por el olfato, ya que el aroma puede revelar los defectos: “Si hay un exceso de extracción, se perciben notas quemadas. O, al contrario, si ha sido insuficiente, falta aroma”, continúa. Por último, el más evidente: el sabor y su regusto: “Un buen café debe tener equilibrio, dulzor, aroma, acidez y cuerpo”, resume.

World.title: Tras las huellas de Miguel Hernández, con el Guadalquivir y el Segura como compañeros de viaje
World.content:
La casa museo de Miguel Hernández en Orihuela, donde vivió con su familia entre 1914 y 1934.

Ruta por las dos patrias del poeta, Alicante y Jaén, por el 116º aniversario de su nacimiento

Este viernes 30 de octubre se cumplen 116 años del nacimiento de Miguel Hernández, un poeta universal al que dejaron morir en la cárcel de Alicante al acabar la Guerra Civil cuando apenas tenía 31 años. La obra hernandiana tiene dos referentes geográficos: su cuna e infancia oriolanas y alicantinas, de un lado, y, de otro, la provincia de Jaén, adonde llegó destinado como comisario de Cultura para dirigir el periódico Altavoz del Frente Sur. De allí era su esposa, Josefina Manresa, y aquí fue nombrado en 2024 Hijo Adoptivo de la provincia a título póstumo.

Estas dos patrias del poeta son el argumento de una ruta turística que tiene a los ríos Guadalquivir y Segura como compañeros de viaje. El Guadalquivir por nacer en el municipio de Quesada, donde se encuentra el Museo Miguel Hernández-Josefina Manresa, y el Segura por ser el río que, desde su nacimiento en Pontones, en la jiennense sierra de Segura, mejor vertebra a los dos territorios hernandianos por excelencia.

Más información De Sitges a Montserrat: cuatro escapadas en los alrededores de Barcelona

La Senda del Poeta, o camino hernandiano, es una ruta que conecta los lugares que marcaron la vida y la obra de Miguel Hernández (1910-1942), un itinerario que arranca en Jaén, donde se encuentra actualmente el legado que conservó su mujer, y que sigue el curso del río Segura hasta llegar a su desembocadura, en Guardamar del Segura (Alicante). A través del sendero GR-125 el itinerario atraviesa varios pueblos levantinos por donde transcurrió la infancia y también los últimos años de vida de Miguel Hernández.

Iniciamos el viaje en Jaén, donde la Diputación adquirió en 2012 el legado personal del poeta, que está compuesto por 5.819 registros bibliográficos y 26.684 imágenes, entre los que se encuentran documentos personales, manuscritos y correspondencia, borradores de sus obras; recortes de prensa, libros, grabaciones sonoras; dibujos, grabados y carteles; y objetos representativos como su máquina de escribir, la maleta o la lechera en la que le pasaba a su esposa Josefina cartas y poemas desde la cárcel. Este legado está repartido entre el Instituto de Estudios Giennenses y el Museo Miguel Hernández-Josefina Manresa de Quesada.

El Instituto de Estudios Giennenses (IEG) es una de las tres patas de un triángulo monumental que forman el Antiguo Hospital de San Juan de Dios (donde se encuentra su sede), los Baños Árabes del Palacio de Villardompardo y la iglesia de Santa Catalina Mártir, junto al antiguo convento de Santo Domingo.

Santo Domingo es el resultado de un proceso constructivo prolongado entre finales del siglo XV y el último tercio del siglo XVI. Sobre algunos de los palacios islámicos previos se comenzó a levantar una iglesia tardogótica de la que aún perviven elementos como la capilla mayor y algunas bóvedas. Entre 1575 y 1582 continuaron las obras del templo y se siguió un nuevo proyecto manierista, configurando la nave, el coro y la portada actual.

Claustro del monasterio de Santo Domingo, en Jaén. diego grandi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La conexión del poeta alicantino con Jaén se inició cuando fue destinado como comisario de Cultura para dirigir el periódico Altavoz del Frente Sur. Coincidiendo con el 84º aniversario de su muerte, la ciudad de Jaén estrenó una ruta literaria que recorre los lugares de su estancia en tierras jiennenses, desde la plaza de los Naranjos, bautizada también como plaza de Miguel Hernández, y que continúa por el refugio antiaéreo de la plaza de Santiago, donde se rememora el bombardeo de Jaén del 1 de abril de 1937 que se saldó con 159 muertos y decenas de heridos. Cuando el bombardeo de Jaén, Miguel Hernández se encontraba fuera cubriendo la batalla de Peñarroya o en la defensa de Medellín, pero Josefina Manresa sí que fue testigo directo.

El otro pilar clave fue su esposa, que era natural de Quesada, localidad que es la cuna del río Guadalquivir y donde desde el año 2015 hay un museo en memoria de los dos. Tras convertirse en la viuda de un poeta maldito, Josefina guardó celosamente los escritos de Miguel, como centinela de su memoria, para que nadie pudiera arrebatarle ese tesoro; documentos de su marido que durante años mantuvo escondidos en costales de los que se utilizaban para llenar el trigo. En el museo quesadeño, que comparte instalaciones con el dedicado al pintor Rafael Zabaleta, se hace un recorrido por la obra y la vida del poeta y su esposa, una historia de amor llena de pasiones y emociones. Como esta carta en la que ella relata sus primeros encuentros: “Me estuvo pretendiendo desde el año 1933 hasta el 27 de septiembre del 34. Pasaba varias veces por la puerta del taller de la calle Mayor, en Orihuela, donde yo trabajaba de modista. Miraba hacia dentro del taller y me di cuenta que me miraba a mí”.

Su estancia en Jaén fue la que inspiró otro de sus poemas más célebres, Aceituneros, que pone letra al himno de la provincia. La coral Encina Hermosa, de Castillo de Locubín, lo ha versionado ahora en clave feminista:

Andaluzas de Jaén

aceituneras comprometidas

decidme en el alma: ¿quién

recogió las olivas?

No las recogió la nada,

ni el dinero, ni el señor

sino la mujer arrastrada,

el cariño y el tesón

Conectada a la luna

y a la rociá de la mañana

las tres dieron la vida

a ese olivo y a sus ramas

Levántate aceitunera de plata

decimos al pie del viento

la aceitunera alzó su mano

poderosa de miramiento

Andaluzas de Jaén

aceituneras comprometidas

decidme en el alma: ¿quién

amamantó los olivos?

Nuestra sangre, nuestro cuerpo

no sólo la del hombre

que se llevó el mérito

de nuestro sufrimiento

Andaluzas, levantémonos

reclamemos nuestro lugar

La fachada de la fundación Miguel Hernández, en Orihuela, donde nació el poeta. mauritius images/ Alamy / CORDON PRESS

Siguiendo la Senda del Poeta

Ya en la provincia de Alicante, y con el río Segura como compañero de viaje, nos adentramos en la llamada Senda del Poeta creada por varias instituciones levantinas en homenaje al escritor, natural de Orihuela. Este itinerario, que puede realizarse en cualquier época del año, se efectúa a pie durante tres días desde la Casa Museo de Miguel Hernández en Orihuela hasta su tumba en el cementerio de Alicante.

Esta ruta, que atraviesa el sendero de gran recorrido GR-125, está dividida en tres etapas. Arranca en Orihuela, ciudad donde nació Miguel Hernández el 30 de octubre de 1910. Orihuela marcó su infancia y juventud de forma decisiva, ya que aquí fue donde inició sus estudios escolares en el colegio Santo Domingo, ayudó a su padre en los trabajos de pastoreo, participó en las reuniones literarias de la tahona de los hermanos Fenoll, publicó sus primeros poemas y conoció a Josefina Manresa. A continuación, se pasa por Redován, donde nació su progenitor, por Callosa del Segura, se llega a Cox, donde Hernández y Manresa vivieron varios años; por Elche, donde murieron su mujer e hijo, y concluye en Alicante.

La primera etapa transcurre también por Granja de Rocamora y finaliza en Albatera, en cuyo término se encontraba el campo de concentración donde perecieron muchos compañeros de Hernández tras la Guerra Civil. Todo ello por caminos con numerosos huertos de naranjos y limoneros que ofrecen al caminante el penetrante olor del azahar, característico de la primavera en la vega baja del río Segura.

La segunda etapa del sendero, entre caminos donde predominan las palmeras, transcurre entre Albatera y Elche, adonde se trasladó Josefina Manresa con su hijo Manuel Miguel tras la muerte del poeta. En el Archivo Municipal de Elche se encuentran depositados un buen número de manuscritos del poeta y aquí también se encuentra la Universidad pública Miguel Hernández que, en 1998, nombró al poeta Doctor Honoris Causa a título póstumo.

El palmeral de la ciudad de Elche, una de las paradas siguiendo las huellas de Miguel Hernández. José Antonio Aldeguer ( GETTY IMAGES )

Finalmente, la tercera y última etapa discurre entre Elche y Alicante, en cuya cárcel falleció el 28 de marzo de 1942. Aquí redactó sus últimos poemas de Cancionero y romancero de ausencias, y en las dependencias de la enfermería carcelaria contrajo matrimonio canónico con Josefina Manresa días antes de morir.

En el cementerio de Alicante, entre campos de almendros, reposan los restos del poeta en una tumba en donde también se encuentran enterrados su mujer y su hijo.

World.content:

There are fears that a “Gen Z” protest, inspired by the ongoing unrest that has swept through France and other countries, could hit the Netherlands over the weekend.

A report in AD found that groups on Telegram, Snapchat and other social media platforms are preparing to riot in cities including The Hague, Maastricht and Eindhoven.

While no applications for protest permits have been submitted, police have said they generally monitor online forums for signs of trouble but would not comment on this matter specifically.

The messages, which include calls to loot shopping centres, were enough to prompt school heads to issue warnings to parents in Maastricht. Limburg police backed the warnings, according to local broadcaster L1 News.

Shopkeepers in The Hague have also started boarding up their windows as a precaution, as some messaging groups are calling for gatherings on the Malieveld and attacks on commercial centres nearby, according to Omroep West.

The protests in France, which have spread to Italy and Spain began over education and living standards among young people. Many of the demonstrations quickly descended into serious rioting, often with heavy police response.

There are similar concerns in Germany, where youth groups are preparing to protest over similar issues on Halloween.

World.title: “No movement” in cabinet talks amid left-right stalemate
World.content:
The cabinet’s attempt to win over left- and right-wing opposition parties in its ongoing tax plan talks failed again on Friday.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and other senior ministers met opposition leaders a day after three right-wing parties, the far-right JA21, orthodox Protestant SGP and farmer-citizen movement BBB, banded together to push their demands as a single bloc. The demands range from harsher asylum measures and changes to abortion rules to scrapping a tax rise to pay for defence.

The move was the latest attempt by the opposition to force the cabinet to pick a side. Opposition parties have said for weeks that the cabinet will never get a broad agreement, because the two sides of the aisle have incompatible demands.

The offer presented on Friday covered how to pay for changes to box 3, the tax on savings and investments, without raising taxes on wealth, sources told the Telegraaf.

The cabinet would use money left over from a fund to refund people who were overtaxed under box 3 in past years, and cut taxes for business owners who pay themselves profits from their own companies. It would also keep a tax deduction for healthcare costs that was due to be scrapped in 2028.

Regardless of the offer, the stalemate appears to continue. Centre-left PRO leader Jesse Klaver said he saw “no movement at all” on his party’s demand for higher taxes on the wealthy and lower taxes on workers.

JA21 leader Joost Eerdmans called it “a tough, complicated conversation”, but said the new right-wing alliance remained intact.

The coalition of D66, VVD and CDA does not have a majority, so it needs support from opposition parties to get its tax plan through parliament.

World.title: Government seeks to ban smoking where children congregate
World.content:
The Dutch cabinet wants to prohibit smoking at locations dominated by children, including petting zoos and after-school and other managed playgrounds.

Sources told broadcaster NOS the proposed ban will be discussed at Friday’s Council of Ministers.

While most such places are already smoke-free, the government wants to ensure that the remaining few ban smoking. The House of Representatives also supports the ban and wanted to extend it to other kid-friendly locations like zoos and amusement parks.

That may come in the future, along with bans at unattended playgrounds and outdoor swimming pools, but for now, the government will focus on managed playgrounds and day care centres where there is wide support for the plan.

The ban is part of the government’s efforts to have a smoke-free generation by 2040. Measures already in place include a display ban, unattractive packaging and fewer locations to purchase cigarettes.

World.title: Herman Brood painting added to national art collection
World.content:
A painting by rock legend and artist Herman Brood has been added to the National Collection, placing Brood in the company of Dutch icons such as Rembrandt, Ferdinand Bol, Piet Mondriaan and Karel Appel.

“We believe that Herman Brood should be given more prestige as an icon of the twentieth century as an artist,” said the cultural heritage anency (RCE).

The untitled acrylic work, made with an ever-present injection syringe and paint rollers, features two men with a pistol. It has been hanging on the wall of the tax office in The Hague but was moved earlier this week to the RCE’s depot in Amersfoort, where it’s been given the name “rock-‘n-roll on canvas”.

The inclusion of the work in the 120,000-strong national collection is official recognition that Brood has contributed substantially to Dutch culture and history. The work will be preserved permenantly and can be lent to museums.

“Junkie who painted”

Rob Dupré, a friend of “The Never Be Clever” and “Saturday Night” singer who died in 2001, told broadcaster NOS that Brood would rise from the dead if he heard the news.

“In life, he was seen as a rock ‘n’ roll singer who worked as an artist. Others called him a junkie who painted. As if everyone could do what he did. This news is like winning gold at the Olympics,” said Dupré, who works to detect counterfeits attributed to the artist.

It’s thought the painting ended up in the tax office to pay off a debt. “He didn’t do receipts and that kind of civil matter,” Dupré said. “He painted five paintings and then spent them on alcohol, drugs and women. He wasn’t really businesslike.”

As to the painting now part of the Rijks collection, Dupré says: “Have you ever had an envelope from the Tax and Customs Administration?… He deliberately painted those two people’s sweaters in exactly the same colour.”

As for the gun? “Everyone would want to have that in their hand when you get a tax assessment, right?” Dupré told AD.

Great honour

“He would have thought this was a great honour,” Brood’s wife Xandra Brood told the AD, adding that she had to point out colours to him because the artist was colour-blind. “He worked very fast and made several paintings one after the other.”

She hopes the painting will eventually hang on the walls of Amsterdam’s Stedelijk Museum, his greatest wish.

This painting’s estimated value is 13,000 to 15,000 euros, but Dupré says that’s maybe gone up 50% since the painting became part of the national collection Thursday.

That inclusion, says Dupré, is official recognition of the artist’s craftsmanship. “He was much more than a side-working rock star. And that is now being recognised.”

World.title: French customs seize thousands of THC sweets bound for NL
World.content:
French customs officers have intercepted 3,560 packs of cannabis-laced sweets that were being shipped from the US to the Netherlands, the European anti-fraud office OLAF said on Thursday.

The sweets contained THC, the main psychoactive substance in cannabis. Of the packs, 3,213 copied the look of a “very well-known European gummy brand”, using altered lettering to resemble its name. OLAF did not name the brand. All the packs have been destroyed.

OLAF did not say who the sweets were meant to be delivered to in the Netherlands.

In a statement, the agency said the familiar packaging gives the false impression of an ordinary, safe product, but that a single product could contain a high amount of THC, and children could be at risk.

Cannabis sweets have caused several scares in the Netherlands. This summer, Utrecht police warned parents after two children became ill from sweets found in a school playground, broadcaster NOS reported.

World.title: Seven Rotterdam police officers to face trial over arrest death
World.content:
Seven police officers will go on trial in January next year over the death of a 32-year-old man who was held in a “prone position” on the ground for a long time after being tasered during an arrest in Rotterdam in 2023, the public prosecution department (OM) said on Thursday.

Two officers chased the man on June 9 that year, first in a police van and then on foot, after reports that he had crashed his bicycle into a car and then cycled on.

When he ignored their instructions, one officer used a taser, but it did not incapacitate him or stop him from further resisting. More officers arrived and several of them pinned him down. Soon after he became unwell and was given CPR but died in hospital.

In February 2024 the OM said it would prosecute eight officers after an investigation by the Rijksrecherche, which investigates the police. A pathologist concluded the man’s death could have been caused by the way he was restrained.

The officers are accused of breaching the rules on the use of force with fatal consequences, which has been a criminal offence in its own right since July 2022.

The OM said on Thursday it had dropped a case against an eighth officer, as he was still in training and was following instructions.

The case will be heard on January 19 and from February 15 to 18 by the Blauwe Kamer, a special court in Utrecht that handles cases against police officers. The court will rule on all seven cases at the same time.

In September another Rotterdam man, Alfredo Goeloe (51), died during an arrest after collapsing while officers held him on the ground. That incident led to protests in the city. The Rijksrecherche is investigating his death as well.

World.title: You can pry Halloween from my cold, witchy fingers
World.content:
You can pry the pumpkins from the cold, dead hands of our regular columnist Molly Quell, who is going to celebrate Halloween despite some Dutch naysayers.

I am throwing a Halloween party. I like Halloween. It has cooler vibes than other second tier holidays (Valentine’s Day, Easter) and less stress than the major ones (Christmas, and for Americans/Canadians, Thanksgiving.)

I have gotten some pushback, however, from some of the Dutchies in my life, who are balking at the “Americanisation” of it all.

“What about Sint Maarten?” a Dutch friend asked me, half joking. The traditional Dutch holiday is celebrated on November 11, named after a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity. Children carry paper lanterns and go house to house, singing, in exchange for sweets.

“You are welcome to celebrate it,” I said. “I don’t.”

“I don’t celebrate Halloween,” she retorted.

“I’ll put you down as a ‘no’ then,” I said.

If my friend does celebrate Sint Maarten, she’s in the minority even in the Netherlands. By some estimates, only 30% of kids are out slinging their lanterns (or in some places, hollowed out turnips) for sweet rewards.

In Utrecht the holiday is celebrated widely, as Sint Maarten is the city’s patron saint. Further afield, however, there’s barely a single flame out on a chilly November evening.

Halloween, on the other hand, is everywhere. Hema has pumpkin candles and Takkie in a witch’s hat. There’s trick-or-treating for kids in community centres, spooky canal tours in Amsterdam, horror movies at every Pathé across the country.

That’s significantly better than a hollowed out turnip.

I admit, the broader point my friend was making is correct. American culture is becoming increasingly dominant and, as many become disillusioned with the United States under the current administration, there will be more and more backlash to things seen as symbols of the country.

There are a lot of American things the Netherlands shouldn’t import. I am on record saying we should ban American influencers from moving here. I am also opposed to importing prudish attitudes towards sex.

Takkie in his little witch’s hat is adorable and I am choosing to defend his (and my) right to celebrate Halloween.

I’ve always been a little surprised that Dutch people don’t embrace Halloween more. They love to dress up in absurd costumes for every other holiday. Have you seen Brabant during Carnival?

Plus, there aren’t really any holidays in autumn. In fact, earlier this year I argued that rather than making Liberation Day (May) a public holiday, as prime minister Rob Jetten suggested, we do Prinsjesdag (September) instead.

Half the country shuts down anyway for the annual announcement of the budget (in 2026, this was even more true, as the train lines were sabotaged) and there’s even a bit of a costume element with the hats.

We need something to celebrate in the fall to take our minds off the impending darkness of winter and Halloween is already right there. It already has built-in rituals, themed food (I will die on this hill defending candy corn) and no obligation to spend time with family.

While the pumpkin spice lattes and the knife-wielding maniacs on film may be an American export, Halloween doesn’t originate in the United States. Historians think it started as a Celtic pagan festival and was taken across the pond by Irish and Scottish immigrants.

And what is a bigger rebuff to the current American administration than celebrating immigration?

Afterwards, the president announced that he would hold a series of meetings with political leaders on Saturday afternoon to discuss the crisis. However, it remains unclear to what extent the government, which is in conflict with the opposition-aligned Nawrocki and is backing the judges seeking to control the court, will engage in that process. Meanwhile, the court itself remains surrounded by riot police and anti-government protesters. On Friday, Nawrocki had been flying to Senegal for a state visit when the crisis at the court broke out. He ordered his plane to turn around in midair and return to Warsaw. At around 1 a.m. on Saturday morning, Maciej Berek, a close associate of Prime Minister Donald Tusk who was recently chosen as a new TK judge, shared videos showing Nawrocki entering the TK building amid a confrontation at its doors. The president was heard asking judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, who is leading the attempt to take control of the court, to move out of his way and could be seen pushing his way past her. Afterwards, presidential aide Marcin Przydacz claimed that Korwin-Piotrowska and another judge, Krystian Markiewicz, had “breached the inviolability of the head of state”. Berek denied this and said that it was the president who “barged into judge Korwin-Piotrowska with great force”. Subsequently, a further film showed Nawrocki, after he had entered the building, in a verbal confrontation with Korwin-Piotrowska and others, in which he can be heard telling them, “you are not Constitutional Tribunal judges”. ⚠️Mamy kolejne nagranie z TK. It also regards the court’s chief justice, Bogdan Świeczkowski, as illegitimate. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. World.title: Chaos at Poland’s constitutional court as government-backed judges seek to oust chief justice
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) was plunged into chaos on Friday evening as one group of judges, backed by the government, moved to take control of the court from its chief justice, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition and President Karol Nawrocki. One of the government-backed judges said that she had suspended the chief justice, Bogdan Święczkowski, from his duties. Police have surrounded the court and were seen preventing Święczkowski from entering the grounds after his supporters had cut through the fence with a power tool. Święczkowski and the opposition claim that an illegal “coup d’état” is underway. Nawrocki, who had been flying to Senegal for a state visit, ordered his plane to turn around and return to Warsaw. Przecież to bezprawie! pic.twitter.com/XbIXigwIi3 — Jan Molski 🇵🇱 (@JanMolski) October 30, 2026 The dramatic events follow a years-long crisis surrounding the TK. Since the current government – a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk – came to power in 2023, it has refused to recognise the court’s legitimacy. That is because three of its judges were unlawfully appointed under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was widely seen to have brought the court under political control. As a result, Tusk’s government has ignored the TK’s rulings and, until this year, refused to even nominate new judges to fill vacancies that arose on the court’s 15-person bench. ‘ That changed in March, when the ruling coalition began filling the backlog of empty seats. So far this year, parliament has chosen eight new judges, meaning that its nominees in theory now have a majority on the court. However, under Polish law, although new TK judges are chosen by parliament, they must swear an oath “before the president”. Nawrocki, who is aligned with PiS, has refused to swear in five of those eight new judges, citing concerns over how they were chosen or their qualifications. Those five judges arranged their own swearing-in ceremonies in parliament and submitted their oaths to the president’s office. However, Święczkowski, who before being appointed as a TK judge had served in the former PiS government, refused to accept those five judges on the court. In doing so, he ignored an order by the European Court of Human Rights that the judges be allowed to take up their positions. Święczkowski argued that the ECHR had no authority to issue such a ruling. The standoff between the government and president over Poland’s constitutional court deepened today, as Maciej Berek, whom the prime minister recently described as his “right-hand man”, took his oath as a new judge without the presence of the president https://t.co/MrExiJRsEN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 14, 2026 Rumours have long swirled that the government would introduce those judges onto the court by force. PiS supporters have been camped outside the TK grounds for weeks with the aim of preventing that from happening. On Friday evening, large numbers of riot police were deployed around the TK. On the court’s website, a brief statement appeared, saying that a “break in the activities” of Święczkowski and his deputy chief justice, Bartłomiej Sochański, had been ordered. The statement did not say who had ordered that break, but it cited article 130 of the law on common courts, under which the president of a court or the justice minister can order an immediate break in a judge’s official duties if they are caught in the act of committing an offence. However, Marcin Matczak, a prominent scholar of constitutional law who was also a critic of PiS’s judicial reforms, wrote on social media, that, while the justice minister exercises oversight over common courts, he cannot do so over the TK. “I consider Bogdan Święczkowski to be the worst person to serve as the president of the TK,” wrote Matczak. “I never thought I’d end up defending him, but this legal basis [for suspending Święczkowski] is nonexistent for a million reasons.” Ze szczątkowych informacji, na jakiej podstawie zawieszono B. She justified her action by accusing Święczkowski of blocking judges from taking up their positions and of overseeing irregularities in the assignment of judges to cases, reports Polskie Radio. SOP is subordinate to the interior minister. She said they had entered the grounds of the court through a gate that leads from the prime minister’s chancellery, rather than the main entrance from the street where protesters are gathered. Korwin-Piotrowska also confirmed to TVP that she was one of seven judges who were inside the TK on Friday evening. Rzeczniczka Trybunału Konstytucyjnego Weronika Ścibor komentuje sytuację w TK. Według jej relacji siedem osób wybranych na sędziów weszło do budynku w asyście funkcjonariuszy SOP, natomiast wiceprezes Bartłomiej Sochański nie został wpuszczony na teren Trybunału. pic.twitter.com/VwxU4UrYuz — OficjalneZero (@OficjalneZero) October 30, 2026 The developments at the court prompted outrage from the opposition. PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński declared outside the court that “as of today, Poland has become a police state, and from there it’s a straight path to authoritarianism, and then to totalitarianism”. Kaczyński called on Nawrocki to return to Poland from his state visit to Senegal and defend the court. The president himself quickly confirmed that he had done so, with flight trackers showing his plane turning around in midair and heading back to Poland. Meanwhile, Zbigniew Kapiński, the chief justice of the Supreme Court – a separate entity from the Constitutional Tribunal – told Kanał Zero that he was “appalled” by what was happening, which was “undoubtedly a coup d’état”. Our most tracked flight right now: A Polish government aircraft en route to Senegal is now returning to Warsaw. https://t.co/YdLhQmV8pl pic.twitter.com/Dz9KPgI3eI — Flightradar24 (@flightradar24) October 30, 2026 Tusk, however, issued a statement on social media defending what was taking place at the TK. “Restoring the rule of law is our duty,” he wrote. “After years of PiS-led lawlessness, this is a difficult process, sometimes painful, and it requires decisive action. There is no other way.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland approves first fast-track renewable energy zones
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has introduced its first fast-track zones for renewable energy projects as the coal-dependent country seeks to speed up its transition to cleaner sources of electricity. The regional assembly in Wielkopolska province, western Poland, this week approved plans covering 105.4 hectares across four municipalities, where investors will be able to develop solar farms under simplified planning and environmental procedures. The environment ministry estimates that the changes, introduced under an EU directive, could reduce project preparation times from three to four years down to just one or two years. Pierwsze #OPRO już są! Sejmik województwa wielkopolskiego przyjął dziś pierwsze w Polsce plany OPRO. Obejmą one ok. 105,4 ha w gminach Lwówek, Rawicz, Słupca i Złotów.🔆 ❓Czym jest OPRO? ✅To Obszary Przyspieszonego Rozwoju #OZE, czyli tereny, na których – już podczas ich… — Marek Pogorzelski (@rzeczni_MKiS) October 26, 2026 Under the scheme, planning and much of the environmental assessment will be completed before investors apply for permits, allowing projects to move forward more quickly. Environmental authorities will also have a maximum of 45 days to review projects with a capacity of at least 150 kW. Industry representatives told energy Świat OZE, a renewable energy news service, that obtaining an environmental decision can currently take up to 150 days. The newly designated areas, known as Accelerated Renewable Energy Development Zones (OPRO), will be located in the municipalities of Złotów, Lwówek, Rawicz and Słupca. Together, they have an estimated technical potential of 66-80 megawatts of solar capacity, depending on the arrangement of the panels. Maria Niewitała-Rej, a climate and energy policy analyst at the Reform Institute, a Warsaw-based think tank, told the Dziennik Gazeta Prawna newspaper that while “the scale of the Wielkopolska plan is modest, the adoption of the first resolutions is a step in the right direction”. The creation of accelerated renewable energy development zones stems from the EU’s revised Renewable Energy Directive (RED III), which requires member states to designate areas where renewable energy projects can be developed more quickly. Under the directive, permitting procedures in these zones should take no longer than 12 months for onshore projects and 24 months for offshore projects. EU rules required the first zones to be designated by 21 February 2026, making Poland’s adoption several months late. Polish state mining firm JSW, which is the EU's largest producer of coking coal and one of Poland's biggest employers, has announced that it will cut over 4,000 jobs, 21% of its workforce, by the end of this year as it seeks to stem large financial losses https://t.co/EWP3rAVMaH — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 2, 2026 Poland has long had one of Europe’s most polluting energy sectors. The country still produces around half of its electricity from coal, by far the higher proportion in the EU. However, the share of renewables has grown significantly in recent years. It nearly doubled from 14.7% of the energy mix in 2021 to 29.4% in 2025. Onshore wind was the largest contributor last year, accounting for 14.2%, followed by solar at 12.1% and biomass at 1.8%. Poland’s national energy and climate plan, approved in June, envisages coal accounting for just 0-5% of the energy mix by 2040. Around 15-16% will come from nuclear, 7-8% from gas, with most of the rest from renewables: onshore wind (22-27%), offshore wind (18-21%) and solar (14-18%). Poland’s first offshore wind farm has begun to deliver electricity, with Prime Minister @donaldtusk celebrating the development as a "key element of our energy security and sovereignty". The government wants 20% of power to come from offshore wind by 2040 https://t.co/EodvInFmrn — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 10, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish Left seeks to end state funding of clergy’s social contributions as government reform stalls
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Left, a junior partner in Poland’s ruling coalition, has proposed a bill to abolish the Church Fund, which provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy. It says it is frustrated by delays in fulfilling a pledge made by most parties in the wide ruling coalition to reform the fund. However, another coalition partner, the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL), says that it will oppose the bill, calling instead for a system allowing taxpayers to allocate part of their taxes to religious institutions of their choice. Senior church figures also say they have not been consulted. 📣 Lewica składa ustawę likwidującą Fundusz Kościelny. Czas na realizację umowy koalicyjnej w zakresie świeckiego państwa‼️ Co zakłada nasz projekt? ⬇️ ✅ Składki na duchownych przestają być w 80 procentach finansowane z budżetu państwa jak dotychczas. 50% składek pokrywać… pic.twitter.com/syqUMdCugr — Lewica (@__Lewica) October 29, 2026 The Church Fund, originally established in 1950 to compensate religious communities for property seized by the communist authorities, provides state subsidies for the health insurance contributions of clergy, for religious organisations’ charitable activities, and for the renovation of religious buildings. It now supports all legally recognised religious denominations in Poland, including those that did not lose property at the time. Last year, the state spent 275.7 million zloty on the Church Fund. This year it has budgeted 272.6 million zloty. Most of this money is then used to cover 80% of clergy members’ social security contributions. Under the bill proposed by The Left, churches would pay half of the contributions, with clergy covering the other half. For regular workers, such contributions are funded jointly by employees and their employers, Anna Maria Żukowska, the head of The Left’s parliamentary caucus, pointed out, as quoted by the Polish Press Agency (PAP). “We are introducing the same arrangement for priests and members of the clergy.” At least 17.5bn zloty in state funds went to religious bodies from 2021-23, with over 95% going to Catholic organisations, the state auditor has found. In response, the speaker of parliament has proposed measures to reduce and better oversee such spending https://t.co/IN3dpY4La2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 16, 2025 An exception is made in the bill for members of enclosed religious orders and missionaries, who would have their contributions paid in full by their churches. The cost of maintaining historic churches would be covered by the National Fund for the Protection of Monuments, Żukowska explained. Włodzimierz Czarzasty, who is the leader of The Left as well as the speaker of the Sejm, the more powerful chamber in the Polish parliament, said the party did not oppose religion but wanted clergy to be treated equally under the law. “I would like to remind my coalition partners: our coalition agreement includes a commitment to work toward establishing the principles of a secular state in Poland,” he said, speaking alongside Żukowska. “Our patience is running out”. Ahead of the 2023 election, both the centrist Civic Coalition (KO) led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and The Left pledged to abolish the Church Fund, while the centre-right Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) proposed replacing state funding with voluntary taxpayer contributions. PSL had no equivalent formal party-wide pledge. In 2024, after the coalition came to power, Tusk announced plans to reform the fund and appointed a government working group led by the PSL leader and deputy prime minister, Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz. The group’s work has since stalled. Kosiniak-Kamysz yesterday dismissed The Left’s proposal, saying it has “not the slightest chance of support in parliament”. His party, the second largest in the coalition with 32 of 239 MPs, sees the existing fund as an inexpensive form of compensation and will oppose abolishing it, he vowed. Instead, taxpayers should be able to allocate part of their taxes to a religious institution of their choice, a system used in several European countries, to “let the Polish people themselves decide whether or not they want to contribute,” he said, quoted by broadcaster Polsat News. Interior minister Marcin Kierwiński, a member of Tusk’s Civic Coalition (KO), said that he supported reform, but criticised The Left for submitting the bill without consulting its coalition partners. A long-term decline in trust in the Catholic church in Poland has accelerated over the last year, with only 35% of Poles now saying they trust the church. Meanwhile, the armed forces now enjoy record-high trust of 94% https://t.co/ErCBE4HwWR — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 17, 2025 Religious communities also criticised the proposal for not having been discussed with them in advance. In a press statement sent to PAP, the Polish Episcopal Conference (KEP), the main organ of the Catholic church in Poland, said any solution should comply with the country’s agreement with the Vatican, as well as the constitutional principle that relations between the state and religious communities be regulated by mutual agreement. Bishop Jerzy Samiec, head of the Evangelical-Augsburg Church in Poland, the country’s biggest Protestant body, pointed to the significant costs churches face in maintaining their properties, including care homes and other facilities. The Catholic Church, Poland’s dominant religious institution, has seen a long-term decline in public trust, with only 35% of Poles saying they trusted it in 2025. That has coincided with a series of crises in recent years, in particular over revelations of child sexual abuse by members of the clergy and negligence in dealing with them by the church hierarchy. A variety of surveys, including from the church itself, show that religious attendance and identification have been declining in Poland in recent years. A growing number of Poles are turning away from the Catholic church, but not from religious belief itself. This creates challenges for the church, but also for Polish identity, which has historically been linked to Catholicism, writes Katarzyna Skiba https://t.co/udWGzd0X7F — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 18, 2023 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Polish opposition leader sparks controversy with speech on potential EU exit talks
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Jarosław Kaczyński, the leader of Poland’s largest opposition party, has sparked controversy by appearing to suggest that Poland and some other allied European Union member states could launch the process of leaving the EU if they fail in efforts to reform it. His remarks were condemned by Prime Minister Donald Tusk and other figures from the pro-EU ruling coalition, who have long accused Kaczyński and his national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party of seeking “Polexit” from the EU. However, Kaczyński responded by accusing Tusk of misrepresenting his words, insisting that he wants Poland to reform the EU rather than leave it. Kaczyński pomylił Krynicę z Kremlem. pic.twitter.com/tX0G04krze — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) October 29, 2026 The comments in question came in an hour-long speech by Kaczyński at the Krynica Forum, an annual conference bringing together leaders from politics, business and civil society, which he used to outline his vision for sweeping reforms of the EU. Repeating his longstanding criticism of Brussels, Kaczyński warned that there had been a “consistent drive to transform the EU into a centralised state” with too much power over national governments. He also called the European Parliament in its current form a “parody”. But soon, said Kaczyński, “a window of opportunity” for reform may appear because “completely different governments could emerge” in Poland, France and Spain, all of which will hold elections within the year. PiS has previously enjoyed close relations with Marine Le Pen’s far-right National Rally (RN) party in France and the nationalist Vox party of Santiago Abascal in Spain. The EU is preparing a "German plan" that would "annihilate the Polish state", said Kaczyński as Poland marks Independence Day. He warned that the incoming opposition government will "strive to implement this plan" and called on Poles to "fight" against it https://t.co/QDbxmiaazJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 11, 2023 Kaczyński suggested that Poland, if led by PiS, could work with other like-minded EU governments to push for reform of the bloc by influencing public opinion, identifying breaches of EU treaties, creating a blocking minority in the European Council, and trying to change the EU’s treaties. However, the PiS leader then warned that, “if [those] approaches fail to yield results, the states that want change could conclude a new treaty with the elements we are seeking, but with a delayed entry into force”. Kaczyński then noted that the EU treaties “include provisions specifying the terms under which a state may withdraw from the EU. This all begins with negotiations. And simply begin these negotiations”. “It is a tough approach, a risky one, but the situation is so dire that it is worth employing such a method if all others fail to yield results,” he added. The remarks immediately prompted condemnation from figures in Tusk’s ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right. They accused Kaczyński of effectively calling for Polexit – something they have long claimed he wants, even though PiS has not explicitly called for it before. “Jarosław Kaczyński has just announced that Poland should begin negotiations on the terms of its withdrawal from the EU,” wrote Tusk himself on X. “This is, among other things, what the current struggle in Poland is about – a tough struggle. I do not intend to lose it.” “So they do want Polexit after all,” wrote foreign minister Radosław Sikorski. “Customs borders with Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Lithuania…An end to subsidies for farmers and investments…And they swore on their lives that they’d never do that.” In a video published later on Thursday, Tusk declared that next year’s parliamentary elections would help decide “whether Poland remains in the European Union or leaves it”. Jarosław Kaczyński ogłosił właśnie, że Polska powinna zacząć rokowania o warunkach wyjścia z Unii Europejskiej. O taką między innymi stawkę toczy się dziś w Polsce walka. Twarda walka. Nie zamierzam jej przegrać, nawet jeśli nie wszyscy zagrają ze mną. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 29, 2026 Kaczyński responded by saying that “Tusk is lying as usual”. He emphasised that he believes “the EU is needed but it requires thorough reform” so that it “benefits not the elites, but ordinary citizens”. PiS deputy leader Przemysław Czarnek said on Thursday that his party was “considering all scenarios, including the possibility that the EU will kill itself”. However, he added that the priority remained reforming the bloc and “PiS has no plans to leave the EU”, reports the Polish Press Agency (PAP). When PiS was in power from 2015 to 2023, it regularly clashed with Brussels over a variety of issues, including judicial reform, trade, climate policy, and migration. Since Tusk, a former president of the European Council, took power in 2023, his government has greatly improved relations with Brussels. Tusk jak zwykle kłamie. Najwyraźniej wychodzi z założenia, że dzień bez kłamstwa jest dniem straconym… Unia Europejska jest potrzebna, ale wymaga gruntownej reformy. Kryzys i zapaść w jej obecnym kształcie to efekt rządów Merkel i jednego z jej pomocników, Tuska. Nie ma co się… — Jarosław Kaczyński (@OficjalnyJK) October 29, 2026 Poland has been the largest net recipient of EU funding since joining the bloc in 2004. A study published earlier this year found that the country’s economy is 42% larger than it would have been had Poland not been part of the EU. Opinion polls consistently show a large majority of Poles in favour of remaining part of the EU. However, recent years have seen an uptick in support for Polexit, as well as for anti-EU far-right parties. PiS has increasingly found itself competing against such parties for votes. Regular polling by state research agency CBOS shows that, while opposition to EU membership fell to a record low of 5% in 2022, it has subsequently risen, standing at 14% in the most recent survey. World.title: Polish bishop convicted for failing to promptly report child sex abuse allegations
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. In the first ruling of its kind in Poland, a Catholic bishop has been found guilty of failing to promptly inform the law enforcement authorities about allegations of child sex abuse committed by priests under his authority. Andrzej Jeż, the bishop of Tarnów, was handed a non-custodial sentence that will require him to donate 25% of his earnings for two years to a charity that supports victims of child sexual abuse. However, the verdict can still be appealed, and the diocese of Tarnów has already announced that it “disagrees with the court’s ruling” and that an appeal will be filed. Pierwszy taki wyrok w Polsce. Biskup skazany za zwlekanie z powiadomieniem prokuratury o pedofilach w sutannach Ordynariusz tarnowski bp Andrzej Jeż jest pierwszym biskupem oskarżonym o zbyt późne powiadomienie prokuratury o pedofilii w Kościele. I pierwszym, który który został… — Bartosz T. Wieliński 🇵🇱🇪🇺🇺🇦🇬🇱 (@Bart_Wielinski) October 29, 2026 The case relates to alleged abuse by two priests who worked under Jeż’s authority. They can be identified only as Stanisław P. and Tomasz K. under Polish privacy law. In 2022, prosecutors discontinued an investigation into allegations against Stanisław P. because the statute of limitations had expired, despite concluding that he had harmed at least 95 children and committed “sexual acts” against 77 of them over several decades in parishes in Poland and Ukraine. In 2023, prosecutors decided to charge Tomasz K., who allegedly sexually abused children as early as 2018. However, they have been unable to formally present the charges to him because of his poor health, news website OKO.press reported earlier this year. Though Jeż was not accused of complicity in the alleged abuse itself, he was charged under a 2017 law making it a criminal offence not to “immediately notify the authorities” of “credible information” about sexual abuse of minors. The offence is punishable by up to three years in prison. Investigators say that, although an internal church probe into Stanisław P. was initiated in the 2000s and a decision to remove him from the clergy was made in 2013, Jeż only notified the prosecutor’s office in 2020. In the case of Tomasz K., the bishop notified prosecutors only in 2021. In court, prosecutor Marcin Stępień said that Jeż’s failure to report the abuse promptly had allowed the statute of limitations to expire in the case of some of Stanisław P.’s victims. Stępień also noted that the bishop had only come forward with the information when media coverage brought the allegations against Stanisław P. to light, reports broadcaster TVN. A church commission set up to investigate child sex abuse in a Catholic diocese in Poland has identified at least 50 victims and 29 abusers. It also found that bishops repeatedly failed to take action when credible reports of abuse were submitted to them https://t.co/MRNl5vWp4E — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 13, 2026 Prosecutors sought a 10-month prison sentence, suspended for three years, and a fine of 20,000 zloty (€4,550). Jeż, however, denied the allegations against him and sought an acquittal. He argued that he had reported the alleged abuse to the authorities as soon as there was credible information. On Thursday, the court found the bishop guilty, giving him a sentence known as “restriction of liberty” (ograniczenie wolnośći), under which a convict is not imprisoned but required to do some kind of social good. In Jeż’s case, the court ordered that 25% of his salary for two years be donated to the Empowering Children Foundation (Dajemy Dzieciom Siłę), which supports victims of child abuse. He was additionally ordered to pay 20,000 zloty to the Fund for Assistance to Victims and Post-Penitentiary Assistance. In a statement after the verdict was issued, the diocese of Tarnów said that it “disagreed with the court’s ruling” and that, after a written justification from the court was reviewed, “an appeal will be filed”. The Catholic church in Poland has in recent years been hit by a series of revelations regarding historical abuse of minors by members of the clergy and allegations that bishops covered cases up. The Vatican has taken action against a number of Polish bishops over the issue. Most recently, in 2024, the Vatican announced the resignation of the bishop of Łowicz, Andrzej Dziuba, due to his “negligence in handling cases of sexual abuse against minors”. In February, a commission created by the diocese of Sosnowiec following a series of scandals announced that it had identified at least 50 children who were harmed and 29 people suspected of abusing minors, most of them members of the clergy. World.title: Turkish engineer creates live 3D pixel map of adopted hometown Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Turkish software engineer has, with the help of AI and vast quantities of Polish public data, created a precise digital replica of Warsaw, the city where he lives. The map, which can be explored for free online, features almost 200,000 buildings, moving trams that match their real-life schedules, changing light and weather conditions, and over 45,000 accurately placed streetlamps that turn on at night. It is even possible to fly a virtual plane through the city. The person behind the project, Bedirhan Yildirim, was inspired by recent efforts to produce similar maps of New York and London. While he initially considered producing one of Istanbul, his hometown, he decided instead to pick the city he lives in, Warsaw. “It is smaller, mostly flat, and I walk its streets every day,” he explained of his choice. Yildirim then used AI coding agents to create the map through a process of trial and error, constantly tweaking and improving the model. The initial version took only two days to produce and was launched on 22 October, but it has been regularly improved since then based on feedback from users. The work was made possible by what Yildirim says is the “incredible amount of data” Poland’s national mapping office, GUGiK, provides for free, including 3D building models, terrain scans, and even details of almost 2 million trees. Further information, including on parks, streetlamps, and traffic lights, was taken from OpenStreetMap, a freely licensed database. Meanwhile, timetables from Warsaw’s public transport authority, ZTM, and Poland’s national rail operator, PKP, allowed the map to feature accurately timed trams and trains. Current weather conditions are input from Open-Meteo, an open-source meteorological service. But users can also choose to manually adjust the time of day or year, with light and weather changing accordingly. An observation deck at the top of the EU's tallest building, Varso Tower in Warsaw, has opened to the public. Located 230m up on the tower's 53rd floor, the attraction offers a 360° panorama of Poland's capital.https://t.co/VeEapOmh4s — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 9, 2025 The result is an incredible level of explorable detail, from major landmarks, such as the communist-era Palace of Culture and Science and Varso Tower, the EU’s tallest building, down to the seating steps and bars along the Vistula River boulevards. The map also features graveyards reflecting Warsaw and Poland’s diverse past, including Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Jewish and Tatar Muslim graves. Around 1 November, when Poles visit cemeteries around All Saints’ Day, candles glow around the graves. A final touch Yildirim has added is a flight simulator, allowing users to travel over the city – and complete missions – in a Cessna aeroplane, an air ambulance, a flying car, or even a UFO that takes off from the Copernicus Science Centre and travels to the National Stadium. I turned Warsaw into a flight sim 🛩️ Take off from Chopin, fly through the ring over the Palace of Culture, then land a UFO inside Stadion Narodowy as the roof opens 🛸 Desktop only for now. Can you land it? 👇 pic.twitter.com/DT2fdk1Vem — Bedirhan (@bedcodes) October 27, 2026 Speaking to Notes from Poland, Yildirim says that he moved to Poland in 2022 to pursue a job in IT before starting his own business. Initially living in Kraków, the country’s second-largest city, he then moved to Warsaw in 2025. Asked what his own personal favourite places in the city are, Yildirim points to Warsaw’s parks, such as Skaryszewski, Pole Mokotowskie and Łazienki. His favourite neighbourhood is Saska Kępa on the right bank of the Vistula. The software engineer adds that his project is an example of how AI can be an “amazing tool to do 90% of the job very quickly”. The remaining 10% of human input “is what keeps it from being ‘AI slop'”. Yildirim says that, without the use of AI, the map of Warsaw he created would have needed an entire team to build over a period of months. World.title: Poland detains Ukrainian accused of arson attack in Romania on behalf of Russia
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland has detained a Ukrainian citizen who is wanted by Romania on suspicion of involvement in an arson attack on a defence company carried out on behalf of Russia. On Tuesday, the Polish police’s Central Investigation Bureau (CBŚP) announced that anti-terrorism officers had detained the man, who can be named only as Artem S. under Polish privacy law, in Warsaw under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Romania. In the early hours of 14 September, a fire broke out in the city of Brașov, Romania, in the immediate vicinity of premises belonging to Carfil, a manufacturer of military equipment. Carfil is a subsidiary of ROMARM, a state-owned defence company. On Monday this week, the Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) said it had determined that the fire had been deliberately caused by a “sabotage network coordinated from Russia”. It added that “several citizens of former Soviet states who reside in the EU” had been involved in the arson attack. The SRI also revealed that the group’s activities were not limited to Romania. “Its coordinators in Russia had assigned it a wide range of targets across the region, including state-owned and private arms manufacturing facilities, as well as sites of military and industrial interest.” In a separate statement, Romania’s Directorate for Investigating Organised Crime and Terrorism (DIICOT) confirmed that the suspects were a Ukrainian, who was at large in Poland, and two Belarusians, who had already been detained in Germany, where they “had been preparing to commit similar acts”. Polish broadcaster RMF reports, based on sources, that Artem S.’s role in the Brașov attack was to identify a target and to arrange payment for those involved. A Polish court will now decide whether the 25-year-old should be extradited to Romania. Poland itself has been a primary target for Russia’s campaign of sabotage and other so-called “hybrid actions” in Europe. Many of those detained and convicted have been Ukrainian and Belarusians, though some Polish citizens have also been implicated. Poland is the "primary focus" of Russia's sabotage campaign in Europe, finds a new report by the International Centre for Counter-Terrorism. Among 151 incidents identified since 2022, 31 of them took place in Poland – more than in any other country https://t.co/QXfSI00FD6 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 3, 2026 In some cases, such operatives are amateurs – so-called “disposable agents” – recruited, coordinated and paid through messaging service Telegram. Some have also been pre-existing criminal groups hired by Russia to carry out such tasks. In August, a drone production plant belonging to private Polish arms company WB Electronics was targeted in an arson attack that Poland has blamed on Russia. The following month, a ground station in Poland used by Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite internet company, was likewise hit by an arson attack that Poland blamed on Russia. Two Turkish men were later detained in Germany on suspicion of carrying out the attack.
